passages.title: AI agents and MCP
passages.text: Connect AI agents to Fabrica property data and documentation through hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.

passages.title: AI agents and MCP
passages.text:
The Fabrica MCP server gives AI agents read-only access to the data behind the Fabrica protocol: tokenized properties, the lending market, account portfolios, protocol-wide statistics, parcel geometry, and map images. It implements the Model Context Protocol (https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP), the open standard that assistants and agent frameworks such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor use to call external tools, so any MCP client that supports remote servers can connect to it.

It serves two audiences: people who use an AI assistant and want it to answer questions about Fabrica properties from live data, and developers building agents that reason over tokenized real property.

Everything the server exposes is public data already available through the Fabrica GraphQL API. No API key, account, or wallet is required, and the server never asks for one.

passages.title: AI agents and MCP
passages.text:
| Network | URL | Data |
|---|---|---|
| Ethereum mainnet | `https://mcp.fabrica.land/mcp` | Real US parcels. Responses carry a legal notice. |
| Sepolia testnet | `https://mcp-testnet.fabrica.land/mcp` | Test properties only. |

The network is fixed per URL: an agent connected to the testnet server cannot reach mainnet data, and vice versa. Add both as separate servers if you want to try things on testnet before mainnet.

The hosted server is stateless. Each request is served by a fresh server instance with no session, the transport is Streamable HTTP with JSON responses, and only `POST` is accepted (a `GET` returns 405, and a request body over 1 MB is refused with 413). Browser-based clients can call it directly, since responses carry permissive CORS headers. The hosted endpoints are deployed from the `main` branch of the public repository, so they track its current tool set, and both serve the property card described below.

passages.title: AI agents and MCP
AI agents and MCP
passages.text:
The server also runs locally over stdio from a clone of the repository. It is not published to npm, so install from source (Node 20 or later):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fabrica-land/fabrica-mcp.git
cd fabrica-mcp
npm install
npm run build
```

Then point your client at the built entry point. With Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add fabrica -- node /absolute/path/to/fabrica-mcp/dist/index.js
```

With Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`), here selecting Sepolia:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fabrica": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/fabrica-mcp/dist/index.js"],
      "env": { "FABRICA_NETWORK": "sepolia" }
    }
  }
}
```

A local server connects to Ethereum mainnet unless told otherwise. All environment variables are optional:

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `FABRICA_NETWORK` | `ethereum` | `ethereum` or `sepolia` |
| `FABRICA_API_URL` | `https://api.fabrica.land/graphql` | Fabrica GraphQL API the tools read from |
| `FABRICA_METASTREET_SUBGRAPH_URL` | selected per network | Subgraph the server reads lending-pool statistics from |
| `FABRICA_MEDIA_URL` | `https://media.fabrica.land` | Media service that renders the map images |
| `FABRICA_MCP_APPS` | `enabled` on Sepolia, `disabled` on mainnet | `enabled` or `disabled`: whether `get_land_property` also serves the property card |

passages.title: AI agents and MCP
passages.sectionTitle: What the Server Can and Cannot Do
passages.text: Every tool is read-only, and says so in the standard MCP way: each tool is registered with a human-readable `title` and with annotations `readOnlyHint: true`, `destructiveHint: false`, and `idempotentHint: true`, so a client that gates state-changing tools behind confirmation can treat every Fabrica tool as a plain read. The server queries the public Fabrica GraphQL API (plus a lending-pool subgraph for pool statistics and the Fabrica media service for map images) and returns formatted results. It holds no keys, signs nothing, and cannot transfer a token, list a property, place a bid, or open or repay a loan. An agent that wants to act on what it learns has to do so through the application (https://fabrica.land) or directly against the smart contracts with the user's own account.

passages.title: AI agents and MCP
passages.sectionTitle: What the Server Can and Cannot Do
passages.text: **Mainnet legal notice.** On the mainnet endpoint, the server's instructions carry a legal notice written as a statement of facts rather than as directions to the agent. It states that Fabrica properties are real parcels of land in the United States, each held in a trust whose beneficial interest is represented by an ERC-1155 token, and that acquiring, transferring, listing, or borrowing against a token has real-world legal and financial consequences: owning a token means owning the beneficial interest in the trust that holds the property, with the trustee designated by the token holder and by default the holder; owners can carry obligations tied to the land, such as property taxes, maintenance, and environmental liability; transfers and sales are legally binding and can trigger tax events such as capital gains or transfer taxes; the operating agreement (the trust instrument) attached to each token sets out the owner's rights and obligations, and its URL is included in property details; and the data is informational, not financial or legal advice. Property search, property detail, and protocol statistics responses on mainnet also carry a one-sentence version of the notice. The testnet server states instead that its properties are test tokens with no real-world legal or financial effect.

passages.title: AI agents and MCP
passages.sectionTitle: What the Server Can and Cannot Do
passages.text:
**Default filters.** Property searches and protocol statistics exclude burned tokens, premints (properties still being added), and tokens below a minimum numeric encoding of Property checks, together with a small set of known spam entries. The default minimum is 72,032, the same threshold the Fabrica marketplace applies to its public listings; the API pairs any minimum with a verified-deed requirement, so the default leaves out every property the marketplace would not sell, including any whose recovery status is not Normal. The `minScore` input of `search_land` (the minimum numeric encoding) overrides the default. A search with `ownedBy` and no `minScore` lists every property in that account, as the owner's own holdings appear in the application, and `get_land_portfolio` applies no minimum.

**Errors.** Tools return an `error` field with a plain-language message instead of raising, and a result that carries one is flagged with the MCP `isError` marker so clients can tell failure from data. A property that does not exist is reported as such; a failure of the underlying API is reported as an API error carrying the API's own message, so an agent can tell the two apart. A request to the underlying API that does not answer within 20 seconds is reported as an error that suggests retrying, and a map image larger than 5 MB is refused with a request for smaller dimensions. The county outline in `get_land_boundary` is an extra layer: if it cannot be fetched, the parcel geometry is still returned and the failure is listed under `warnings`.

passages.title: AI agents and MCP
passages.text:
Eleven tools, all read-only. Inputs marked with an asterisk are required; every other input is optional. Property tools accept either a `tokenId` or the property `slug` from its Fabrica URL (for example `us/nevada/elko-county/elko/apn-063025003`).

| Tool | Inputs | Returns |

|---|---|---|

| `search_land` | `region` (US state code), `minAcres`, `maxAcres`, `minScore`, `hasListings`, `hasLoans`, `ownedBy` (account address), `limit` (default 20, max 100), `offset` | Matching properties with location, acreage, the numeric encoding of Property checks, estimated value, listing price, loan flag, owner, and property link, plus the total match count for paging (an offset past the end says so rather than reporting no matches) |

| `get_land_property` | `tokenId` or `slug` | Full detail: location, legal description and trust name, operating agreement URL, Property checks (how many pass, with each check's result and the numeric encoding), valuation with per-source pricing, ownership and holders, active loans and DeFi lending pool capacity, active listings and bids (in US dollars when the API prices them so, otherwise in the order's own currency), the owner's description and photos (up to eight, with resized thumbnails) and parcel map image links in both themes, recent activity, whether the property is still a premint, and warnings for recovery, default, or liquidation status. Boundary geometry comes from `get_land_boundary` |

passages.title: AI agents and MCP
passages.text:
| `get_land_boundary` | `tokenId` or `slug`, `includeCountyBounds` (default true) | GeoJSON FeatureCollection with the parcel boundary (or a point when no boundary exists) and the county outline |

| `get_land_map_image` | `tokenId` or `slug`, `theme` (`dark` by default, or `light`), `width`, `height` (100 to 1280 pixels, default 640) | Inline static map image of the parcel boundary, or a pin when no boundary exists |

| `explain_property_checks` | `tokenId` or `score` | Explains Property checks: a digit-by-digit breakdown of the numeric encoding's five groups against the 75,342 maximum, with the individual check results when a token is given. The result states that the encoding is positional, not a percentage or a grade, and no percentage is reported |

| `get_fabrica_lending_market` | `status` (`active`, `repaid`, `liquidated`, `all`), `borrower`, `lender`, `since` (ISO date), `limit` (default 20, max 100) | Market summary (loans by status, loan volume per currency, average APR of active loans), DeFi lending pool statistics (value locked, in use, available, utilization, loan counts), matching loans with their terms and venue, and the ten most recent loan events |

| `estimate_land_borrowing` | `tokenId` or `slug` | DeFi lending pool availability for the property (the advertised maximum principal in whole USDC, rounded down, subject to available pool liquidity, and the available durations) and any active loan on it. The amount is an estimate; the amount and rate are set by a live quote when borrowing |

passages.title: AI agents and MCP
passages.text:
| `get_land_portfolio` | `address`* | Properties held, lending positions as borrower and as lender, credit history, marketplace activity, and total portfolio value for an account, scoped to the server's network and token contract. The outstanding-loans total is null when a loan has no dollar price |

| `get_land_portfolio_map_image` | `address`*, `theme`, `width`, `height` | Inline static map with every property held by the account plotted as points |

| `get_land_activity` | `tokenId`, `slug`, or `address`; `type` (for example `loan`, `transfer`, `sale`, `mint`); `limit` | Event timeline for a property or an account: mints, transfers, sales, loans started, repaid, or liquidated, and configuration changes |

| `get_fabrica_stats` | none | Protocol-wide figures: token count and estimated value, states represented, loan counts and loan volume per currency, lending-pool statistics, active listings, and the token contract address (on mainnet, the retired peer-to-peer lending contracts are listed separately as historical) |

passages.title: AI agents and MCP
passages.text: Monetary values are formatted in US dollars where the source provides a dollar figure. Activity amounts are derived from the event's own currency amount and decimals: stablecoin amounts read as dollars and other currencies in their own unit (for example WETH), and the API's dollar figure is used only as a fallback. Loan principals are stated in the loan's own currency, and loan volumes are totaled per currency rather than summed across currencies or presented as dollars. Each loan and lending event names its venue: pool loans read "Pool-based lending", and loans made through the former peer-to-peer integration are labeled as retired. Borrow quotes list only the DeFi lending pool, since that integration has shut down (see Peer-to-Peer Lending). Loan counts are reported by status; the server does not publish an aggregate repayment rate. This table is derived from the server source and checked against the hosted endpoints; the `tools/list` response of the deployment you are connected to is authoritative.

passages.title: AI agents and MCP
passages.text:
In clients that support MCP Apps (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps), such as Claude on the web and in the desktop app, `get_land_property` renders a property card inline in the conversation instead of a block of JSON. The card shows:

- a gallery with the parcel map first, followed by the owner's photos when the property has any
- the property name, location, and acreage
- how many Property checks pass (for example "16 of 18 pass", as on fabrica.land), estimated value, listing price, and borrowing capacity
- **Buy** (when the property is listed and its token has been issued), **Make an offer**, **Contact owner**, and **View on Fabrica** buttons

Every button opens the property's page on Fabrica, where the user completes the action and signs with their own account. The server never prepares or submits a transaction, so the card changes how the data is shown, not what the server can do. Clients without MCP Apps support receive the same data as JSON.

The card is served as an MCP resource at `ui://fabrica/property-card`, and the `get_land_property` tool points to it through its metadata; a client that supports MCP Apps picks it up automatically. It renders in the client's sandbox and loads images only from Fabrica's IPFS gateway, the Fabrica media service, and the map-tile provider behind it. Both hosted endpoints serve the card. A local server serves it by default on Sepolia and not on mainnet; set `FABRICA_MCP_APPS=enabled` to turn it on there, or `disabled` to turn it off.

passages.title: AI agents and MCP
passages.text: The server is developed in the public repository github.com/fabrica-land/fabrica-mcp (https://github.com/fabrica-land/fabrica-mcp) under the MIT license. The repository also holds a checked-in snapshot of the GraphQL schema that every query is validated against, so an upstream API change surfaces as a reviewable diff rather than a runtime failure.

passages.title: AI agents and MCP
passages.text: `https://docs.fabrica.land/mcp` gives agents this documentation and the API reference. Add it the same way when an agent needs to answer questions about the protocol, the trust, or the API.

passages.text:
- `fabrica.land/llms.txt` (https://fabrica.land/llms.txt): a summary of Fabrica written for language models, served as `text/markdown`, listing the hosted MCP servers, the GraphQL endpoint, the token contract and the documentation. Every page of fabrica.land points to it with `Link: </llms.txt>; rel="describedby"` and `rel="llms-txt"` headers, and a request for the homepage with `Accept: text/markdown` returns it in place of the HTML (other pages are not served as markdown)
- GraphQL API at `https://api.fabrica.land/graphql`: public, no API key, introspection enabled

passages.title: Protocol Overview
passages.text:
Fabrica is designed as an open, non-custodial protocol.

Fabrica is built on the principle that property ownership should be as direct and self-sovereign as holding any other digital asset. The protocol creates a binding connection between onchain tokens and real-world property rights, with no intermediary standing between the token holder and their property. The connection is legal, not nominal: transferring the token to a new owner is intended to operate as a conveyance of the underlying property. First American has underwritten title insurance on a property that went through the Fabrica trust, validating the chain of title the structure produces (see Title insurance after tokenization (https://blog.fabrica.land/title-insurance-after-tokenization)). California State Board of Equalization Tax Counsel stated in a written informational analysis (2022) that "a transfer of the digital Token is, in substance, a transfer of the underlying real property itself."

Fabrica is a full system, not a single smart contract. The legal trust, the regulatory licenses, the validation and Property checks services, the lending and oracle integrations, the valuation pipeline, and the county recording infrastructure compose into one protocol that has operated in production through the full property lifecycle, including loans originated, repaid, and defaulted through to recovery.

passages.title: Protocol Overview
passages.text: The protocol is asset-class-agnostic. The trust, token, and validation model apply to any deeded real property; nothing in the architecture is land-specific. Land is the current focus because it is the most underserved and least encumbered real property. Land is the last major asset class not yet onchain. Treasuries are tokenized. Gold is tokenized. Land is next.

passages.title: Protocol Overview
passages.text:
The Fabrica Trust is designed with no corporate intermediary:

* **No Company in the Trust**: Fabrica as a company has no role in the trust structure. The trust exists solely between the property, the trustee (often the owner themselves), and the token holder.
* **Direct Control**: The token holder controls the property directly. There is no intermediary to go through and no permission to ask: not Fabrica's, not anyone's. Your rights come from the trust agreement, not from us, so they hold even if Fabrica disappeared.
* **No Custodianship**: Fabrica never holds or controls your property token. Property tokens are always in the owner's account.

passages.title: Protocol Overview
passages.text:
Anyone can interact with the protocol without requiring approval:

* **Open Smart Contracts**: The token contracts implement standard interfaces (ERC-1155, ERC-7496, ERC-7572) and can be accessed by any compatible application.
* **Permissionless Transfers**: Property tokens can be transferred, sold, or used as collateral without requiring Fabrica's involvement.
* **Open Source Legal Instruments**: The trust agreement is open source under CC0-1.0, available for anyone to review, use, or adapt.

passages.title: Protocol Overview
passages.text:
The protocol is designed to function independently of Fabrica's existence:

* **Walk-Away Test**: Every token holder can control and operate their property through their token, regardless of whether Fabrica continues to exist as a company.
* **Direct Contract Interaction**: Users can interact directly with the smart contracts via Etherscan or any Web3 interface.
* **Emergency Redemption**: Token holders can burn their tokens and work with any lawyer to transfer title out of the trust, no Fabrica involvement required.
* **Token Recovery**: Even if wallet access is lost, the trust agreement provides a self-service recovery path that works through the county recording system, no blockchain access needed.
* **Decentralized Storage**: Property data is stored on IPFS, not on Fabrica servers.

***

passages.title: Protocol Overview
passages.text:
| Pillar                     | Description                               | Learn More                           |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| **Blockchain Layer**       | ERC-1155 smart contracts and IPFS storage | Property Token   |
| **Validation Services**    | Title verification and Property checks    | Validators         |
| **Ecosystem Integrations** | DeFi lending and marketplaces             | Integrations     |
| **Legal Foundation**       | Trust structures and operating agreements | Legal Wrappers |

***

passages.title: Protocol Overview
passages.text:
**For Property Owners:**
* You have complete control over your property at all times
* No one can prevent you from transferring, selling, or using your property as collateral
* Your ownership is secured by cryptographic keys, not by trusting a company
* Even if Fabrica ceased operations, your property rights remain intact and enforceable

**For Developers and Operators:**
* Build on standard, open interfaces without requiring Fabrica's permission
* Access property data from decentralized infrastructure
* Integrate with any ERC-1155 compatible protocol or marketplace
* Transfer property as a token transfer, in place of the per-transaction title work, escrow, recording, and settlement float of a traditional closing; the cost is similar whether one property or many are moved
* Draw loans against held property programmatically through the lending integration, priced off the public valuation feed, without a separate origination process per asset

**For the Ecosystem:**
* A true public good infrastructure for onchain real estate
* No single point of failure or central authority
* Composable with existing DeFi and NFT infrastructure
* Land as collateral across DeFi, the missing RWA primitive

***

passages.title: Protocol Overview
passages.text:
The protocol implements widely-adopted standards for maximum compatibility:

| Standard | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| **ERC-1155** | Multi-token standard for property tokens |
| **ERC-7496** | Dynamic traits for onchain metadata |
| **ERC-7572** | Contract-level metadata |
| **IPFS** | Decentralized storage for property data |

passages.title: Build on Fabrica
passages.text: Build applications, marketplaces, and lending venues on Fabrica's permissionless property-token, trust, and price-oracle primitives.

passages.title: Build on Fabrica
passages.text: Fabrica is an open protocol for representing real estate onchain. The property tokens, the public legal trust, and the signed price oracle are standard, permissionless primitives: anyone can build applications, marketplaces, or lending venues on them without Fabrica's involvement.

passages.title: Build on Fabrica
passages.text:
The Fabrica token contracts are open source and available for review:

- **Repository**: github.com/fabrica-land/fabrica-v3-contracts (https://github.com/fabrica-land/fabrica-v3-contracts)
- **Standards**: ERC-1155, ERC-7496 (Dynamic Traits), ERC-7572 (Contract Metadata)
- **License**: MIT (LICENSE (https://github.com/fabrica-land/fabrica-v3-contracts/blob/main/LICENSE))

passages.title: Build on Fabrica
passages.text:
The Fabrica Trust operating agreement is fully open source under CC0-1.0 (public domain):

- **Repository**: github.com/fabrica-land/fabrica-connectors (https://github.com/fabrica-land/fabrica-connectors)
- **Contents**: Legal templates, operating agreements, trust documentation
- **Usage**: Free to use, modify, and redistribute without attribution

The trust has evolved through multiple versions, with the current production agreement at v4.4. Changes are documented in the repository's changelog. Key improvements have included:

- Self-custody model refinements
- UCC Article 12 alignment (controllable electronic record framework), replacing an earlier UCC Article 8 opt-in
- Cross-chain and layer-2 support abstractions
- Clarified custody vs. beneficial ownership language
- Token recovery mechanism for lost wallet access (no Fabrica involvement, no court process)
- Lender protections under functional-contract custody
- Estate succession path for deceased token holders
- Involuntary loss of title: automatic dissolution when record title leaves the trust by external operation of law (tax sale, foreclosure, eminent domain, etc.), with bearer-token wind-up authority and judicial reinstatement on operative-instrument reversal
- Beneficial interest declared personal property in the land-trust tradition, with a full UCC Article 9/12 build-out, financed-purchase designations, succession following lawful wallet control, and an unsolicited-transfer disclaimer (v4.4)

passages.title: Build on Fabrica
passages.text:
The Fabrica MCP server gives AI agents read-only access to property, lending, portfolio, and protocol data over the Model Context Protocol. It is hosted at `https://mcp.fabrica.land/mcp` (Ethereum mainnet) and `https://mcp-testnet.fabrica.land/mcp` (Sepolia), with no API key required, and also runs locally from a clone:

- **Repository**: github.com/fabrica-land/fabrica-mcp (https://github.com/fabrica-land/fabrica-mcp)
- **License**: MIT (LICENSE (https://github.com/fabrica-land/fabrica-mcp/blob/main/LICENSE))
- **Guide**: AI agents and MCP, with connection instructions and the tool reference

passages.title: Build on Fabrica
passages.text:
Fabrica tokens are standard ERC-1155 tokens compatible with any NFT marketplace. However, traditional marketplaces weren't designed for real estate operations. There's an opportunity to build specialized marketplaces that:

- Understand property token structure and metadata
- Integrate validation and Property checks
- Support real estate-specific workflows
- Implement appropriate compliance checks

passages.title: Build on Fabrica
passages.text:
Third parties can build validators to serve specific:

- Geographic regions
- Property types (residential, commercial, agricultural)
- Compliance frameworks
- Market segments

See our Build Your Own Validator documentation for requirements.

passages.title: Build on Fabrica
passages.text:
Fabrica is built to be composable with DeFi. The combination of standard ERC-1155 property tokens, a public legal trust, and a public signed price oracle provides the primitives that DeFi protocols need to build against tokenized real estate.

**Public price oracle.** The Fabrica Price Oracle publishes EIP-712 signed price quotes for every Fabrica property token via a public HTTP endpoint. The endpoint returns a valuation panel: one entry per configured valuation source for the token, each carrying its own signed quote, with failures isolated per entry, so a source that cannot produce a quote returns a null entry with a reason rather than breaking the panel. Any pool, vault, or contract that implements the standard `IPriceOracle` interface can consume the quotes to value Fabrica-tokenized collateral. The oracle is free to consumers; it is intended to be funded on the property side by a planned yearly fee to token holders, which is not charged today. Anyone can also publish a competing oracle that signs comparable quotes for the same tokens; pool deployers choose which oracle to trust.

**Permissionless lending pools.** The canonical Fabrica-deployed lending pool is a renounced fork of the original, audited MetaStreet v2 contracts. The contracts are open source (MIT-licensed), with no admin keys, no upgrade path, and no governance lever, so no one (including Fabrica) can alter the pool's terms or seize deposits. Pool deployment is permissionless: anyone can deploy a pool that references the public oracle, without Fabrica's involvement.

**Things you can build:**

passages.title: Build on Fabrica
passages.text:
- **Lending protocols and vaults.** Use the Fabrica oracle to value collateral, the standard token interface to take custody, and the trust agreement to handle default liquidation through onchain token transfer.
- **Aggregators and rate optimizers.** Route capital across multiple Fabrica pools (or other RWA protocols that consume the same oracle) to find the best available rate.
- **Curated vaults.** Deploy Morpho-style curated vaults that allocate capital across Fabrica pools and other strategies. The Fabrica oracle is one of the price feeds the curator can wire in.
- **Stablecoin and synthetic collateral.** Use baskets of Fabrica tokens as backing for stablecoins or synthetic assets, with the public oracle providing transparent onchain valuation.
- **Insurance products.** Underwrite property-specific risks (title, flood, vacancy) using the onchain provenance signals and public valuation feed.
- **Fractional ownership platforms.** Issue derivative tokens that represent shares of pools or baskets of Fabrica tokens.
- **Indices and portfolios.** Build geographic, property-type, or risk-stratified indices that reference live oracle data.

passages.title: Build on Fabrica
passages.text:
Beyond individual owners and DeFi builders, the protocol can serve businesses that buy, hold, finance, or sell real property in volume.

In the traditional system, each transfer carries a largely fixed cost, title work, escrow, recording, closing, and days or weeks of settlement float, regardless of how many properties are moved. On Fabrica, a transfer is a token transfer: settled in seconds, with beneficial ownership following the token. The recorded title stays in the trust's name, so no new deed is recorded at the county for each transfer; the recording step happens once when the property is added and once when it is removed, not on every trade. This changes the cost structure of property operations:

passages.title: Build on Fabrica
passages.text:
- **Per-transaction cost.** The title work, escrow, recording, and settlement float of a closing are replaced by an onchain transfer. The cost is similar whether one property or many are moved.
- **Liquidity on held inventory.** Property held free and clear can be borrowed against programmatically through the lending integration, priced off the public valuation feed, without a separate origination or refinancing cycle per asset.
- **Programmable workflows.** Acquisition, financing, hedging, and disposition are onchain operations that can be automated and composed. A resale or a hedge is another token transfer rather than a second closing through escrow.
- **Any property type.** The trust, licenses, and validation are asset-class-agnostic. The same rails apply to any deeded real property, with land as the current focus.
- **Build on top, or operate on the rails.** The protocol is open and permissionless: a business can integrate Fabrica into existing systems and transact directly with the contracts without Fabrica's involvement. Operating a validator whose Property checks are recognized by the ecosystem currently requires registration and certification through Fabrica (see Build Your Own Validator).

passages.title: Build on Fabrica
passages.text: The Fabrica MCP server already lets an AI agent search properties, read a property's legal description and Property checks, inspect the lending market, and analyze any account's portfolio, all read-only and without credentials. Agent builders can compose those tools with the public GraphQL API, the signed price oracle, and the standard token interface to build due-diligence assistants, portfolio monitors, lending analytics, and research tools over tokenized real property.

passages.title: Build on Fabrica
passages.text:
Opportunities exist for:

- Property data aggregation
- Valuation services
- Title search integration
- Geographic information systems

passages.title: Contract Metadata (ERC-7572)
passages.text: The ERC-7572 collection-level contract metadata Fabrica exposes to marketplaces.

passages.title: Contract Metadata (ERC-7572)
passages.text: Fabrica token contracts implement the ERC-7572 (https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7572) standard for contract-level metadata, providing enhanced discoverability and interoperability for property tokens.

passages.title: Contract Metadata (ERC-7572)
passages.text:
Unlike token-specific metadata (which describes individual properties), contract-level metadata provides information about the token contract itself, including:

* Contract name and description
* External links (documentation, website)
* Supported interfaces
* Issuer information
* Legal framework references

passages.title: Contract Metadata (ERC-7572)
passages.text:
The Fabrica token contract implements the ERC-7572 interface:

```solidity
function contractURI() external view returns (string memory);
```

This function returns a URI pointing to a JSON metadata file that follows the ERC-7572 metadata schema:

```json
{
    "name": "Fabrica Land",
    "symbol": "Fabrica",
    "description": "Own real land, onchain. Fabrica turns real estate into non-custodial, permissionless digital assets you can buy, sell, or borrow against in seconds. Each NFT represents true legal ownership of real property, held directly in your wallet.",
    "image": "https://ipfs.fabrica.land/ipfs/QmNeEqLTrKTru1qFUEDiE1Zkb2qdCEvzfqmFbbVXUggF5D",
    "banner_image": "https://ipfs.fabrica.land/ipfs/Qmb7CimDCxPkp8eMnJMD2nhYmEZPgB45x6kTt5eKBq9pJ8",
    "featured_image": "https://ipfs.fabrica.land/ipfs/QmaGGi6EWCUJkQkvfkskBQWAsR5A1AQ74CaE5cdidW7psR",
    "external_link": "https://fabrica.land",
    "collaborators": [
        "0x1908d26657e238a9f464a98b1f017F4cbd2066c7"
    ]
}
```

passages.title: Contract Metadata (ERC-7572)
passages.text:
Contract-level metadata provides several advantages:

1. **Marketplace Integration**: Enables marketplaces to display collection information
2. **Verification**: Helps users verify the authenticity of Fabrica token contracts
3. **Discoverability**: Improves contract discoverability through metadata indexing
4. **Legal Framework**: Links to the legal framework governing the token contract

passages.title: Contract Metadata (ERC-7572)
passages.text:
Contract metadata can be accessed by:

1. Calling the `contractURI()` function directly on the token contract
2. Using blockchain explorers that support ERC-7572

This implementation enhances the overall ecosystem by providing standardized contract-level information that complements the token-specific metadata for individual properties.

passages.title: DeFi & Integrations
passages.text: >- Fabrica property tokens are standard ERC-1155 tokens, compatible with a wide range of DeFi protocols and NFT infrastructure. This page provides an overview of key integrations and how they enable new use cases for property owners.

passages.title: DeFi & Integrations
passages.text:
Property tokens can be used as collateral to access liquidity without selling the underlying property. This is particularly valuable for owners of unimproved land, a multi-trillion dollar U.S. market traditionally underserved by banks, but because the collateral and valuation feed are standardized, the same mechanism extends to any deeded real property held as a token.

Lending on Fabrica is pool-based and near-instant through the primary live integration, subject to available pool liquidity; the standard token also supports direct peer-to-peer lending where an active venue exists:

| Protocol | Model | Description |
|----------|-------|-------------|
| **Pool-Based Lending** | Pool-based | Loans from an automated pool with dynamic pricing, priced off a public signed valuation feed. The primary live integration. |
| **Peer-to-peer** | Direct | Lenders and borrowers agree on custom terms directly, on any NFT-supporting protocol (Gondi (https://gondi.xyz) is a good option today). NFTfi was the former direct integration and has shut down. |

See Lending for complete documentation on borrowing and lending against property tokens, including lender protections under UCC Article 9 and Article 12.

passages.title: DeFi & Integrations
passages.text:
As standard ERC-1155 tokens, Fabrica properties can be listed on any compatible NFT marketplace, including OpenSea and others. However, traditional NFT marketplaces were not designed for real estate operations.

Fabrica's custom marketplace at fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land) offers:

* A better understanding of property token structure.
* Integration with validation and Property checks.
* Real estate-specific features and workflows.

passages.title: DeFi & Integrations
passages.text: The Fabrica MCP server exposes property, lending, portfolio, and protocol data to AI agents over the Model Context Protocol. It is hosted per network at `https://mcp.fabrica.land/mcp` (Ethereum mainnet) and `https://mcp-testnet.fabrica.land/mcp` (Sepolia), needs no API key, and is read-only: it cannot move tokens or funds. On mainnet its instructions carry a legal notice stating that the properties are real US land held in trust and that acquiring, transferring, listing, or borrowing against a token has legal, tax, and liability consequences set out in the trust instrument attached to it. In clients that support MCP Apps, a property lookup renders as a card whose buttons open the property on Fabrica to buy, make an offer, or contact the owner.

passages.title: DeFi & Integrations
passages.text:
Developers can build on top of the Fabrica protocol to create new applications and services. The smart contracts implement standard interfaces (ERC-1155, ERC-7496, ERC-7572) for maximum compatibility.

We encourage developers interested in building alternative marketplace clients or new applications for the Fabrica protocol to [contact us](mailto:info@fabrica.land).

See our Build on Fabrica documentation for more information on integrating with the protocol.

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text: >- A public, signed AVM price feed for tokenized real property. Free for any consumer to read; subsidized by the property side.

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
The Fabrica Price Oracle publishes EIP-712 signed price quotes for individual Fabrica property tokens (ERC-1155 NFTs that legally represent real property held in the Fabrica trust). The public API returns a valuation panel: one entry per configured valuation source for the token, with each signed quote bound to a specific token contract, token ID, currency token, and source-specific EIP-712 domain.

The oracle is built to be consumed by:

- the DeFi lending pool contracts (and any contract conforming to the `IPriceOracle` interface) to determine collateral value when originating loans against Fabrica tokens
- Other DeFi lending protocols that want a verifiable reference value for loans against tokenized real property
- Aggregators, vault curators, and analytics tools that need a verifiable onchain or offchain reference price for tokenized parcels
- Third-party valuation services that want to compare or benchmark against the Fabrica AVM

The oracle is free to consumers. It is intended to be funded by token holders through a planned yearly fee on the property side, which is not charged today. It follows the same posture as a published Zestimate-style reference value, not investment advice. The architecture is intentionally non-exclusive: any party can run a competing oracle that signs quotes for the same tokens, and any pool deployer can wire any oracle they want into their pool's `oracleContext`.

passages.title: Price Oracle
Price Oracle
passages.text:
| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `networkName` | `enum` | One of `ethereum`, `sepolia` |
| `contractAddress` | `address` | Fabrica ERC-1155 token contract address |
| `tokenId` | `uint256` | Fabrica token ID to value |

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text: The canonical `valuation/v1` endpoint does not accept query parameters. It returns the unconditional Fabrica valuation panel for the token, independent of the caller or borrower.

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text: The endpoint is **public and unauthenticated**. There is no API key requirement. Reasonable rate limiting is applied at the edge; high-volume integrators (block explorers, vaults, mirrored oracles) should reach out to Fabrica for an integration partnership.

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
```bash
curl 'https://api.fabrica.land/valuation/v1/sepolia/0xb52ED2Dc8EBD49877De57De3f454Fd71b75bc1fD/12345678'
```

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
The previous pool-specific route remains available as a deprecated compatibility alias:

```
GET https://api.fabrica.land/pool-lending/{networkName}/{poolAddress}/{contractAddress}/{tokenId}/signed-valuation
```

Use this alias only for integrations that still need the old single `{ quote, signature }` response shape. New integrations should use `/valuation/v1/...`; the matching panel entry contains the same quote and signature consumed by the old route. The alias takes no `borrower` parameter: the signed quote does not bind a borrower, so the same token yields the same quote regardless of who fetches it.

| Deprecated parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `poolAddress` | `address` | Address of the lending pool whose EIP-712 domain should be used. Pool must be registered in Fabrica's oracle map. |

***

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
The response is a JSON object with a `networkName`, an `asOf` timestamp, and a `valuations` array. Each valuation entry identifies its `source`, schema `version`, oracle `signer`, optional signed `quote`, and optional `signature`.

```json
{
  "networkName": "sepolia",
  "asOf": "2026-06-11T20:15:30.000Z",
  "valuations": [
    {
      "source": "Fabrica v3 Property Prices",
      "version": "1.0",
      "signer": "0x8a4f...2c91",
      "signature": "0x1c2b...90ab",
      "quote": {
        "token": "0xb52ED2Dc8EBD49877De57De3f454Fd71b75bc1fD",
        "tokenId": "12345678",
        "currency": "0x1c7D4B196Cb0C7B01d743Fbc6116a902379C7238",
        "price": "75000000000",
        "timestamp": 1781208330,
        "duration": 1200
      }
    },
    {
      "source": "0x62c2940Cc4aB105cfdA49Bdabc3b7A9741Ba9c9e",
      "version": "1.0",
      "signer": "0x8a4f...2c91",
      "signature": null,
      "quote": null,
      "reason": "valuation_unavailable"
    },
    {
      "source": "Fabrica Lending Pool",
      "version": "1.0",
      "signer": "0x8a4f...2c91",
      "signature": "0x3d4e...12fa",
      "quote": {
        "token": "0xb52ED2Dc8EBD49877De57De3f454Fd71b75bc1fD",
        "tokenId": "12345678",
        "currency": "0x1c7D4B196Cb0C7B01d743Fbc6116a902379C7238",

```

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `networkName` | `enum` | Network used to resolve the token and valuation sources |
| `asOf` | `string` | ISO-8601 timestamp when the panel was produced |
| `valuations` | `array` | One entry per configured valuation source for the network |

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | `string` | Valuation source label. For pool-backed entries this is the EIP-712 domain name, falling back to the pool address when the domain is empty. |
| `version` | `string` | Entry schema version. Current value: `1.0` |
| `signer` | `address` (string) | Oracle signer address that produced `signature` for this entry's quote |
| `signature` | `bytes` (hex string) or `null` | 65-byte ECDSA signature over the EIP-712 hash of `quote`. `null` when the token is not yet minted or the source cannot produce a signed valuation. |
| `quote` | `object` or `null` | Signed price quote. `null` when the source cannot publish a valuation for this request. |
| `reason` | `string`, optional | Machine-readable failure reason, present when `quote` and `signature` are `null` because the source failed. Current failure reason: `valuation_unavailable`. |

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `token` | `address` (string) | Fabrica ERC-1155 token contract address |
| `tokenId` | `uint256` (string) | Fabrica token ID |
| `currency` | `address` (string) | Currency the price is denominated in (USDC for the canonical Fabrica oracle: `0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48` on mainnet) |
| `price` | `uint256` (string) | Price **per unit of the token's total supply**, scaled to USDC's 6 decimals. See "Price scaling" below. |
| `timestamp` | `uint64` (number) | Unix timestamp (seconds) at which the quote starts being valid. The publisher backs this off by 10 minutes from real wall-clock time to absorb chain-time skew on consumers. |
| `duration` | `uint64` (number) | Validity window in seconds. The quote is valid from `timestamp` to `timestamp + duration`. After expiry, onchain verification reverts with `InvalidTimestamp`. |

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
The `price` field is the **unit price per token share**, not the price of the whole property. Fabrica tokens are ERC-1155 with arbitrary `totalSupply`; the property's full appraised value is divided by `totalSupply` to produce a unit price, then scaled to the currency's decimals (6 for USDC). Consumers that want the property-level value should multiply `price` by the token's `totalSupply()`.

This matches the `SimpleSignedPriceOracle.price()` semantics: the onchain function aggregates quotes across multiple `tokenIds` and returns an average per-unit price, weighted by `tokenIdQuantities`.

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text: If the oracle's eligibility rule fails (proof of title invalid, fees not in good standing, token not validated by Fabrica, etc.) the returned `price` is `"0"`. A zero price is still a valid signed quote; onchain verification rejects it with `InvalidQuote` because the contract requires `quote.price != 0`. A zero quote in the response is an honest signal that Fabrica is not currently publishing a price for the token; integrators should surface this as "not currently priced" rather than as an error.

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
If the token has been configured but not yet minted, the panel entry returns the `quote` with `signature: null`. These quotes cannot be used onchain and exist only as a forecast for UI surfaces.

***

passages.title: Price Oracle
Price Oracle
passages.text:
The EIP-712 domain is configured per pool and pinned to the onchain `SimpleSignedPriceOracle` contract that the consuming pool uses:

| Domain field | Source |
|---|---|
| `name` | `oracle.domain` from Fabrica's per-pool config |
| `version` | `oracle.verifyingContractVersion` (must match the onchain `DOMAIN_VERSION()` (currently `1.2`) returned by the deployed `SimpleSignedPriceOracle`) |
| `chainId` | The chain ID of the network in the request path |
| `verifyingContract` | The deployed `SimpleSignedPriceOracle` contract address for that pool |

passages.text:
| Network | Pool address | `SimpleSignedPriceOracle` (verifyingContract) | Domain `name` | `version` | TTL (seconds) |

| Sepolia (default pool) | `0x00E5cb8833fdaCFc6a97faA0B54384adE19bE61A` | `0x2E5113D939ff6c2F5a3FEe3AB961e112AB6B9B37` | `Fabrica v3 Property Prices` | `1.2` | 600 |

Multiple pools per network are supported. Each pool can pin its own `SimpleSignedPriceOracle` contract and its own eligibility rule (the Sepolia CA-only pool, for example, additionally restricts to California-state tokens). The valuation panel includes one entry per configured oracle, and each entry is signed with the domain values for that entry's source pool.

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text: To recover the signer or verify a quote offchain, integrators must use the same domain values that the consuming pool's oracle uses. These are addressable onchain via the oracle contract's `eip712Domain()` method (OpenZeppelin's standard EIP-5267 accessor). Read it once and cache it rather than hardcoding from this table, since deployments can be updated.

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
The Fabrica oracle signs with a key whose public address is registered in the consuming `SimpleSignedPriceOracle` for that collateral token. Query the active signer via `priceOracleSigner(collateralToken)` on the oracle contract. Do not hardcode the signer address from documentation, as keys can be rotated by the oracle's owner.

***

passages.title: Price Oracle
Price Oracle
Price Oracle
Price Oracle
Price Oracle
Price Oracle
passages.text:
`SimpleSignedPriceOracle.price(...)` aggregates across multiple `tokenIds`:

```
totalOraclePrice = sum_i (signedQuotes[i].quote.price * collateralTokenQuantities[i])
count = sum_i (collateralTokenQuantities[i])
return totalOraclePrice / count
```

This is the **average per-unit price across all collateral pieces**, weighted by quantity. For a single ERC-1155 with `quantity = 1` it is just the per-unit price from the quote.

***

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.sectionTitle: How the oracle prices a token (architecture)
passages.text: The price returned by the Fabrica AVM is computed from a stack of independent inputs and safety filters before signing. Integrators do not need to understand the internals to consume the oracle; the architecture is summarized here so consumers can reason about failure modes.

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
| Input | Source | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Algorithmic land valuation | Third-party AVM signal | Primary market-value estimate for raw land |
| Confidence level of the algorithmic estimate | Third-party AVM signal | Multiplier in `[0, 1]` applied to the estimate |
| Fabrica AVM estimated value | Fabrica's in-house automated valuation model | Independent valuation signal for cross-validation, trained on closed deed transactions with geospatial enrichment (slope, flood zones, road access, zoning, comparable sales) |
| Fabrica AVM confidence level | Fabrica's in-house model | Multiplier in `[0, 1]` applied to the Fabrica AVM estimate |
| County assessor parcel value | Public county tax assessor records | Conservative fallback (used at 30% of the assessed value) when no algorithmic valuation is available |
| Token validation status | Fabrica validator contract | Token must be validated by a Fabrica validator |
| Property checks results | Fabrica scoring service | Proof of title, fees in good standing, and other token-status signals |

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text: A per-pool rule evaluated server-side determines whether a token is currently eligible to receive a non-zero signed price. The default Fabrica rule requires that the token be validated by a Fabrica validator and (for non-premint tokens) that proof-of-title checks pass. Once the planned yearly oracle fee is charged, the default rule is also intended to require that the property be in good standing on it; no such fee is charged today. If the rule evaluates falsy, the signed price is `0`. The rule is configurable per pool, so pool deployers can tighten or loosen the gate without changing the oracle code.

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
The oracle takes the **minimum** across independent AVM signals (each weighted by its confidence) before signing. Consumers see only the resulting MIN value, signed once. Independent AVMs that converge are more trustworthy; large divergence is a signal of data quality issues, and the conservative side protects pool depositors from oracle drift. Significant divergence is logged for audit.

This MIN-of-N safety logic is the architecturally preferred mode. The roadmap extends it from server-side aggregation across two sources to onchain aggregation across N independent publishers; see "Roadmap" below.

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
The signed price reflects several conservative haircuts applied in this order:

1. **Confidence-weighted estimate** per source: `estimate * confidence`
2. **MIN across AVM sources** (when both signals are available)
3. **Per-unit normalization**: divide by `totalSupply` so the quote is a unit price
4. **Low-value adjustment**: properties below $25,000 receive an additional quadratic discount; high-value properties pass through unchanged. This is a heuristic for the historically lower liquidity of low-value parcels.
5. **Liquidation discount**: properties with at least one prior onchain liquidation receive a 0.25× multiplier (75% haircut) to reflect realized auction outcomes.

These adjustments are part of the published oracle's safety design. The signed price is borrower-independent: the same token yields the same quote regardless of who requests it.

***

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
| Dimension | Current |
|---|---|
| Supported chains | Ethereum mainnet, Sepolia |
| Token contracts | The Fabrica ERC-1155 token deployed on each network (mainnet: `0x5cbeb7a0df7ed85d82a472fd56d81ed550f3ea95`) |
| Token universe | All Fabrica-validated tokens with at least minted supply or valid premint configuration |
| Property types | Currently raw land. Tokens with detected residential structures are flagged but not excluded by the default rule. |
| Jurisdictions | All 50 US states. International parcels are out of scope. |
| Currency | USDC only |

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
The publisher generates a fresh signed quote on every API call. Underlying valuation inputs refresh on independent cadences (third-party AVM signals refresh on a nightly schedule; Fabrica's in-house AVM recomputes on token mint, on validation events, and on a periodic batch schedule; county assessor data refreshes on token mint and on parcel-data refresh events).

The signed quote's `duration` field defines the onchain validity window. The default is set per pool (typically a few minutes to an hour) plus 10 minutes of slack. Integrators should fetch a fresh quote immediately before any onchain action that consumes it.

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
The oracle's price is derived from a mix of public and licensed third-party data sources. Consumers receive only the derived signed price; redistribution of underlying raw inputs is not granted by consuming this endpoint. Fabrica's own AVM glue code is targeted for open-source release, allowing third parties to build a comparable model from open inputs.

Fabrica makes no warranty of accuracy on derived values. The oracle is a published reference price, not investment advice, not a binding appraisal, not a fairness opinion.

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
- **Stale quotes**: a quote outside its validity window will revert onchain (`InvalidTimestamp`). Refetch.
- **Wrong domain**: if the consuming pool's oracle uses a different EIP-712 domain than the publisher signed against, signature recovery returns the wrong address and onchain verification reverts (`InvalidSigner`). Make sure your pool's `priceOracle` registration matches the network's canonical Fabrica oracle deployment.
- **Zero price**: rule-failure tokens return a signed `price = 0` quote. Onchain consumers reject with `InvalidQuote`. Offchain consumers should treat zero as "not currently priced."
- **Unminted tokens**: the panel entry returns `signature: null`. The quote is a forecast and cannot be used onchain.

***

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text: The Fabrica AVM oracle is intended to be paid for on the property side, not the consumer side. The planned model is a yearly fee charged to the token holder via Fabrica's existing property-side billing rail. No such fee is charged today.

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.sectionTitle: Illustrative pre-launch pricing (not currently billed; subject to change)
passages.text:
The plan below is illustrative only. No oracle fee is charged today.

| Plan | Pricing | What it includes |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | A planned yearly fee paid in stablecoin; pricing to be announced before launch | Continuous AVM publication, signed quote endpoint, Property checks endpoint, metadata refresh on demand |

This mirrors the economic model of property tax assessors, title insurance, and Zillow-for-agents: the asset side pays for the data service, and consumers (lenders, buyers, analytics tools, pool deployers) consume it free of charge. Once the fee is charged, the oracle is intended to publish for a token only while its yearly fee is current, and otherwise return a signed price of zero. Until then, this check does not apply.

Final pricing and billing UX are subject to change before formal launch.

***

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
Alongside the price, the oracle relies on Property checks: the tests a validator runs on each token, its owners and the property, each with its own data source. Property checks are a separate signal from the price: a token can carry a high estimated value and still fail checks, or the reverse.

Property checks are currently embedded in the price oracle's eligibility rule. A standalone Property checks endpoint with its own EIP-712 signed payload is on the roadmap; this section will be updated when it ships.

Until then, integrators that need more than binary eligibility can read the per-check booleans via the Fabrica scoring API.

***

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
The current oracle is a single-publisher single-signer architecture. The strategic goal is progressive decentralization of this surface:

1. **Server-side MIN across two AVM signals (live)**: The publisher's safe-appraisal logic takes the minimum across two independent AVM signals (each weighted by confidence) before signing. The signed quote already reflects two-source agreement.
2. **Multi-publisher quote aggregation (planned)**: The onchain `SimpleSignedPriceOracle` already supports rotating the signer per collateral token via `setSigner(...)`. The architectural goal is a variant oracle contract that requires N signatures from N independent publishers and takes MIN (or median, configurable) onchain. Any pool deployer can then consume any combination of publishers without trusting a single party.
3. **Open-source AVM recipe (planned)**: The Fabrica AVM glue code is targeted for open-source release. Once published, any party can stand up a competing oracle that signs comparable prices for the same tokens, and pool deployers can wire whichever oracle they prefer.
4. **Property checks as a standalone oracle (planned)**: Lift the per-check results into a separately signed payload with its own endpoint and EIP-712 typehash, so consumers can read price and Property checks independently.

These are forward-looking commitments. Timelines depend on the broader product roadmap and are not contractual.

***

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:
The published oracle data is provided under the following terms:

- **No warranty.** The oracle's price is a derived estimate from third-party data sources. Fabrica makes no representation as to accuracy, completeness, or fitness for any particular purpose.
- **Not financial advice, not an appraisal.** Consumers must conduct their own due diligence. The oracle is a reference price, not a binding valuation, not a fairness opinion, not regulatory or legal advice.
- **Underlying data is a mix of public and licensed third-party sources.** Consumers may use the signed price quote in their own protocols and applications. Redistribution of underlying raw inputs is not granted by consuming this endpoint.
- **No guarantee of continuous availability.** Fabrica intends to operate this oracle as durable public infrastructure but reserves the right to rotate signers, deprecate endpoints with reasonable notice, or pause publication for specific tokens (e.g., on revocation of validation status).
- **Sanctions screening.** The oracle endpoint applies sanctions screening at the request layer where required by applicable law. Quotes are not signed for tokens or borrower addresses on sanctions lists.

For commercial integration partnerships, custom pricing, or higher rate limits, contact `info@fabrica.land`.

***

passages.title: Price Oracle
passages.text:

passages.title: Property Token
passages.text:
>- Complete reference for Fabrica Property Tokens, including structure, ownership, and governance.

Each property is represented as a standard ERC1155 (https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1155) token.

passages.title: Property Token
passages.text:
```
id : uint256
supply : uint256
operatingAgreement : string
definition : string
configuration : string
validator : address
```

passages.title: Property Token
passages.sectionTitle: Key Defining Elements Stored on IPFS
passages.text:
1. Definition Object: Describes what the token immutably represents.
2. Configuration Object: Provides additional information about the property and title documents.
3. Operating Agreement: Acts as the legal "firmware" of the property.

passages.title: Property Token
passages.text:
A property, defined by an `id`, can have a `supply` of one or multiple tokens, which are fungible among themselves:

* A `supply` of one means there can only be one owner for that property.
* A `supply` of more than one means the property is owned proportionally to token allocation (e.g., owning 57 of 100 tokens means 57% ownership).

> Fractional ownership (supply > 1) is currently experimental. It is designed for small groups such as friends or family members co-owning a property, not for passive investors or securities-like arrangements.

passages.title: Property Token
passages.text:
Beneficial ownership is determined by how the token is held, as described in detail in the Operating Agreement:

| Custody Type            | Description                         | Beneficial Owner                    |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| **EOA (Wallet)**        | Direct wallet holding               | The wallet controller               |
| **Holding Contract**    | Multi-sig, DAO treasury, or similar | The controlling entity/group        |
| **Functional Contract** | Escrow, lending collateral, bridge  | Unchanged until token transfers out |

**Examples:**

* Token in MetaMask wallet → Wallet owner is the beneficial owner.
* Token in multi-sig → The group controlling the multi-sig.
* Token locked as collateral in a lending protocol → Original owner remains the beneficial owner while under loan.

passages.title: Property Token
passages.text:
For properties with multiple token holders, the smart contract enforces these thresholds:

| Action                     | Required Ownership |
| -------------------------- | ------------------ |
| Update configuration       | at least 50% of supply |
| Update operating agreement | at least 70% of supply |
| Change validator           | at least 70% of supply |

passages.title: Property Token
passages.text:
The `validator` property references the entity responsible for verifying property claims and maintaining the NFT's good standing. Property owners elect a validator (identified by a smart contract address) to handle:

* Title verification against public records.
* Property checks, the validation checks run on each token.
* Media and metadata generation for marketplaces.
* Ongoing compliance monitoring.

See Validators for detailed information about the validation process and Property checks.

passages.title: Property Token
passages.text:
Fabrica tokens implement ERC-7496 (https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7496) for crucial token traits, providing standardized onchain access to metadata. This allows applications to query the validator and operating agreement directly from the smart contract, enhancing interoperability with platforms like OpenSea.

**Dynamic Traits** (stored onchain via ERC-7496) are reserved for data needed for secure onchain operations. This is distinct from the Configuration Object, which contains broader property metadata stored on IPFS.

passages.title: Smartcontracts
passages.text: Fabrica's onchain contracts: addresses, upgradeability, and deterministic token IDs.

passages.title: Smartcontracts
passages.text: Fabrica's property NFTs are implemented as smart contracts on multiple blockchain networks. Below are the current and historical contract addresses. Always verify contract addresses before transacting.

passages.title: Smartcontracts
passages.text:
Fabrica smart contracts use the UUPS (Universal Upgradeable Proxy Standard) pattern, allowing the protocol to:

- Deploy bug fixes and security patches
- Add new features and improvements
- Maintain compatibility with existing tokens

The token contract's upgrade capability is currently controlled by Fabrica (decentralized upgrade governance is planned but not yet implemented). This does not compromise the walk-away test: a property's ownership rests on the trust agreement, the data pinned to IPFS, and the offchain county recovery path, all of which continue to function even if the contract were frozen or Fabrica disappeared. By contrast, the Fabrica-deployed lending pool is a renounced, MIT-licensed fork with no admin keys, no upgrade path, and no governance lever.

All contract upgrades are announced through official channels and can be verified onchain.

passages.title: Smartcontracts
passages.text:
Token IDs are generated deterministically from a hash of:

- Chain ID
- Contract address
- Operator address
- Session ID
- Operating agreement URI

This approach prevents frontrunning attacks and ensures unique, predictable token identifiers across the protocol.
