For live lending statistics, see our Dune dashboard (https://dune.com/fabrica/dashboard).

passages.title: Lending
passages.text:
When you take a loan against your property token:

1. **Collateralization**: Your property token is locked in a lending protocol's smart contract
2. **Funds Received**: You receive loan funds (typically in stablecoins)
3. **Ownership Retained**: You remain the beneficial owner of the property during the loan
4. **Repayment**: Upon repayment, your token is returned
5. **Default**: If you fail to repay, the lender can claim the property token

While your token is held as collateral, you retain full rights to use and access the property. The lending protocol holds the token as security, but you remain the owner in every practical sense.

***

passages.title: Lending
passages.text:
The live, integrated lending path on Fabrica is pool-based and near-instant.

| Protocol | Model | Status |
|----------|-------|--------|
| **Pool-Based Lending** | Pool-based | The primary live integration: liquidity for borrowers, passive diversified exposure for lenders. |
| **Peer-to-peer** | Direct | Use any NFT-supporting lending protocol (Gondi (https://gondi.xyz) is a good option today). NFTfi was the former in-app integration and has shut down. |

Because property tokens are a standard, the protocol is not tied to any single lending venue: it works with any NFT peer-to-peer lending protocol (such as Gondi (https://gondi.xyz)), runs on a pool-based path in-app, and can support new venues as they emerge, with no change to the token. Its first peer-to-peer integration, NFTfi, has since shut down.

***

passages.title: Lending
passages.text:
Loans are made by third-party lending protocols and pool participants, not by Fabrica. Fabrica builds the collateral rails and surfaces the offer; it is not the lender, broker, or guarantor of any loan.

**Benefits:**
* Access capital without selling your property
* Lenders price off the property and its valuation rather than your personal credit, so there is no personal credit check or bank approval
* Funds available promptly rather than in weeks
* Retain property rights during the loan

**Considerations:**
* Interest rates vary by protocol and property value
* Failure to repay results in loss of the property token (see Loan Defaults & Liquidation)
* Property taxes and obligations remain your responsibility during the loan

***

passages.title: Lending
passages.text:
If you provide capital, see For Capital Providers for how to lend through a pool or build your own underwriting, and Lender Protections for the UCC Article 9 and Article 12 framework.

***

passages.title: Lending
passages.text:
The Fabrica Trust structure provides lenders with strong security:

* **UCC Compliance**: The trust agreement includes provisions under UCC Article 9 and Article 12, allowing lenders to perfect their security interest by control, without additional filing
* **Reliable Collateral**: Upon default, the property token transfers to the lender or is auctioned to repay the loan
* **Transparent Ownership**: Ownership is verifiable both onchain and at the county recorder

See Lender Protections for details on the legal framework protecting lenders.

passages.title: Lender Protections
passages.text:
Legal framework protecting lenders who finance Fabrica properties.

The Fabrica Trust structure includes legal mechanisms for lenders financing property tokens. These protections are designed to help lenders perfect their security interest and pursue recovery of collateral in the event of default; recovery outcomes are not guaranteed.

passages.title: Lender Protections
passages.text: The Fabrica Trust is designed so that lenders are protected at every stage of a loan, from origination through repayment or default.

passages.title: Lender Protections
passages.text:
When a property token is deposited into a lending protocol's smart contract, the smart contract holds the token as collateral. Under the trust agreement, this is classified as a **functional contract** (Section 7.3(b)): the protocol has custody of the token, but the borrower retains beneficial ownership of the property until the loan resolves.

This distinction is critical: it means the lender holds real collateral (the token, which controls the trust, which holds the property), while the borrower continues to use the property and bear its obligations during the loan.

passages.title: Lender Protections
passages.text:
The trust's token recovery mechanism (Section 10.2) includes a built-in protection for lenders: the self-service recovery process can only be initiated when the token is in a personal wallet (EOA or Smart Wallet). A borrower cannot use the recovery process to reclaim a token that is held in a lending contract.

This means a borrower cannot circumvent a loan by claiming they lost their keys. The token must be returned to the borrower (through repayment) before any recovery process can begin.

passages.title: Lender Protections
passages.text:
If a token is stolen before or during a loan, the trust agreement distinguishes between the original owner's rights and a good-faith lender's rights:

* An unauthorized transfer does not transfer beneficial ownership (Section 7.5)
* However, a lender who obtained control of the token for value, in good faith, and without notice of the theft can qualify as a **qualifying purchaser** under UCC Article 12 and take free of adverse claims (a fact-dependent statutory defense, not yet tested in court for tokenized real property)
* In that case the original owner's remedy is against the thief, not against the good-faith lender

***

passages.title: Lender Protections
passages.text: The trust agreement incorporates two UCC frameworks that provide lenders with well-established legal protections for secured transactions. See UCC Article 12 for a detailed explanation of how these provisions work.

passages.title: Lender Protections
passages.text:
The property token is treated as a **controllable electronic record** (CER) under UCC Article 12. This means:

* **Control-based perfection**: Once a borrower grants a security interest, the lender perfects it by control (the token sitting in the lending smart contract) with no UCC financing statement or county lien filing required
* **Qualifying purchaser protection**: Lenders who obtain control for value, in good faith, and without notice of competing claims take free of adverse claims
* **Smart contract compatibility**: Depositing a token into a lending smart contract is designed to constitute "control" under UCC § 12-105

passages.title: Lender Protections
passages.text:
The beneficial interest in the trust is personal property and a "general intangible" under UCC § 9-102(a)(42), of which the token is the authoritative record. A security interest in the token or the beneficial interest attaches under UCC § 9-203 to the extent the borrower expressly grants it in an authenticated security agreement, and is perfected, prioritized, and enforced under Article 9 as personal-property collateral. The collateral is always the token and, where expressly granted, the beneficial interest; no mortgage or lien on the land itself is created, so enforcement never requires a real-property foreclosure.

On default, the enforcement process follows UCC Article 9 (Secured Transactions). The trust agreement specifies that the standards and procedures encoded in lending smart contracts are "agreed standards" for purposes of UCC 9-603, intended to satisfy the secured party's enforcement duties, and the borrower's redemption right under UCC 9-623 is preserved. The UCC's baseline commercial-reasonableness requirement still applies and cannot be waived.

See Loan Defaults & Liquidation for the complete default and enforcement process.

passages.title: Lender Protections
passages.text: Custody is handled by a technology-neutral rule (trust agreement Section 11.3): a custodian holding the token for a lender or borrower, directly or through sub-custodians, acquires no beneficial interest by reason of that holding, and the token's controllable-electronic-record status is unaffected by any custody arrangement. Custodial holding is available for institutional arrangements but never required.

passages.title: Lender Protections
passages.text:
The trust agreement includes an important boundary: UCC "control" determines rights in the token as a controllable electronic record, but does not by itself transfer, encumber, or create any interest in the recorded title to the property. Transfer of recorded title still requires a deed satisfying applicable real property law.

This means the UCC collateral framework and the real property framework operate in parallel without conflicting.

***

passages.title: Lender Protections
passages.text:
| Stage | Protection |
|-------|------------|
| **Loan initiation** | Token transfers to lending protocol's smart contract, establishing control, which perfects the lender's security interest |
| **During loan** | Borrower cannot use token recovery to circumvent the loan; lender's interest is perfected through control |
| **On repayment** | Token returns to borrower; lender's interest is released |
| **On default** | Formal UCC notice sent to borrower; objection window protects borrower rights; lender claims token or receives auction proceeds |

***

passages.title: Lender Protections
passages.text:
While the token serves as collateral, the borrower retains:

* **Beneficial ownership**: The borrower remains the owner of the property
* **Right to use**: Full access to and use of the property
* **Property rights**: All rights under the Fabrica Trust; the token itself is held as collateral and cannot be freely transferred while the loan is active. Owners can still list the property for sale, with the loan settled from the proceeds at closing.
* **Right to redeem**: The borrower can repay the loan at any time to reclaim the token

The lending protocol holds the token as security, but the borrower is the owner in every practical sense until default and liquidation occur.

***

passages.title: Lender Protections
passages.text:
Validators monitor property status and run Property checks on each token. Checks that are relevant to lending decisions include:

* **Tax status**: Whether property taxes are current
* **Lien status**: Whether lien data shows a voluntary lien, such as a mortgage, with an open balance
* **Owner checks**: Whether current owners have identity-verification records, and whether their addresses appear on the flagged-address list Fabrica uses
* **Recovery status**: Whether a validator has set the token's status to stolen, distressed (at risk of involuntary loss of title) or void (dissociated from the property)

Lenders can use Property checks as part of their own due diligence when evaluating specific properties for peer-to-peer loans. They are a starting point for your own research, not a title search or title insurance.

***

passages.title: Lender Protections
passages.text:
Beyond the UCC and trust provisions, lenders benefit from:

* **Onchain transparency**: Ownership, loan status, and property history are verifiable on the blockchain
* **County records**: The underlying property ownership is recorded at the county level, providing a public record
* **20+ regulatory licenses**: Fabrica is licensed for title, escrow, and related services in 20+ states. Tokenization and transfer are available in all 50 states
* **Open source trust**: The trust agreement is publicly available (https://github.com/fabrica-land/fabrica-connectors) for legal review

> While Fabrica has designed robust protections, the trust model has never been tested in court. Lenders should conduct appropriate due diligence and consider consulting legal counsel for significant lending activities.

passages.title: Pool-Based Lending
passages.text:
Get near-instant loans against your property from an automated lending pool.

The DeFi lending pool (formerly called the Fabrica lending pool) enables near-instant, pool-based lending against property tokens, subject to available pool liquidity. It is the primary live lending integration: property owners can access capital through automated loans, while capital providers earn interest through diversified exposure to real estate collateral, at variable rates that are not guaranteed, with deposited capital at risk.

The pool is a renounced fork of audited, open-source lending-pool contracts (see Build on Fabrica): open source (MIT-licensed), with no admin keys, no upgrade path, and no governance lever, so no one (including Fabrica) can alter its terms or seize deposits. Pool deployment is permissionless, and anyone can deploy a pool that references the public oracle. See Build on Fabrica for the trustless-pool design.

Pricing is driven by a public, signed valuation feed (see Price Oracle), so a quote is available for any eligible token at any time without waiting for a counterparty. This is what makes the path instant and programmatic. Funding itself depends on available pool liquidity.

passages.title: Pool-Based Lending
passages.text:
1. **Request a Loan**: Select your property and request a loan on Fabrica
2. **Automatic Valuation**: The pool uses automated valuation to determine loan terms
3. **Funding**: Accept the terms and receive funds promptly
4. **Repay Anytime**: Pay back principal plus interest to reclaim your token

No waiting for lender offers, the pool provides liquidity based on your property's estimated value.

passages.title: Pool-Based Lending
passages.text:
1. **Deposit Capital**: Add funds to the DeFi lending pool
2. **Select Risk Profile**: Choose a tranche that matches your risk appetite
3. **Earn Automatically**: Your capital is deployed to loans as borrowers request them
4. **Withdraw**: Remove your capital when you choose (subject to liquidity)

Capital providers earn interest without needing to evaluate individual properties or manage loan terms. Returns are variable and not guaranteed, and deposited capital is at risk.

***

passages.title: Pool-Based Lending
passages.text:
The pool aggregates capital from multiple providers into a shared pool. Each loan draws from this pool, combining capital from different providers at their specified terms.

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **Automated Valuation** | Property values are estimated using third-party data and algorithms |
| **Dynamic Terms** | Rates and LTV ratios adjust based on pool utilization and risk parameters |
| **Tranche Selection** | Capital providers choose their risk/return profile |
| **Settlement** | Borrowers receive funds promptly upon acceptance |

Because each loan aggregates capital from multiple providers with different terms, the final rate and conditions are dynamic, determined by the pool's composition at the time of the loan.

passages.title: Pool-Based Lending
passages.text:
The pool uses estimated property values as a starting point, but doesn't rely on raw estimates alone. Additional risk factors are applied to protect capital providers:

* **Liquidity Assessment**: Properties in less liquid markets may receive lower loan amounts
* **Property Tax Status**: Borrowing requires the property's taxes to be verified as current. A property whose tax status is unverified or past due is not eligible for a new loan until that is resolved
* **Fraud Prevention**: High-risk or unusual properties are filtered
* **Default History**: Properties that have defaulted previously may be restricted
* **Borrower Track Record**: Borrowers with poor repayment history may receive reduced terms

This multi-factor approach helps ensure the pool extends credit responsibly while still providing fast liquidity to qualified borrowers. If a property is not currently eligible, the property page tells the owner that borrowing is unavailable and, where possible, why (for example, property taxes that have not been verified as current); a borrower with an active loan sees the same reason when new lending against the property is paused. Other visitors see no borrowing details either way. See Property Valuation for more about how property values are estimated.

***

passages.title: Pool-Based Lending
passages.text:
**Advantages:**
* **Speed**: Get funds promptly, without a closing or approval cycle
* **No Negotiation**: Accept or decline the offered terms, no back-and-forth
* **Predictable Process**: Automated valuation means consistent, transparent pricing

**Loan Terms:**
* Loan amounts based on property valuation and loan-to-value (LTV) limits
* Interest rates determined by pool dynamics
* Flexible repayment: you can pay off at any time. Prorated loans charge interest only for the time elapsed; fixed-term loans owe the full repayment amount regardless of early payoff. The exact payoff amount is always shown before you confirm.
* Pay off from account funds, or by card on pools that can accept a repayment made on the borrower's behalf: the card charge covers only the shortfall, lands in your account first, and you then confirm the payoff. Card payments are processed by Coinflow, Fabrica's payment provider, and are offered where Fabrica has turned the card option on for the network.

During the loan, your property token is held in the lending pool's smart contract. You retain beneficial ownership and can use the property normally.

***

passages.title: Pool-Based Lending
passages.text:
**Advantages:**
* **Automatic Deployment**: Capital is automatically deployed to loans
* **Diversification**: Exposure spread across multiple properties
* **Risk Selection**: Choose tranches that match your risk tolerance

**Tranches:**

Capital providers select a tranche based on their preferred loan-to-value (LTV) ratio:

* **Lower LTV Tranches**: Lower risk, lower returns. Your capital backs the safest portion of loans.
* **Higher LTV Tranches**: Higher risk, higher returns. Your capital covers riskier portions but earns more.

Capital providers can get started by reaching out at [hello@fabrica.land](mailto:hello@fabrica.land). See For Capital Providers for background on how the pool works.

***

passages.title: Pool-Based Lending
passages.text:
If a borrower fails to repay:

1. **Default notice**: The borrower receives a formal UCC notice (Notice of Disposition) informing them the collateral will be sold
2. **Auction**: After the notice period, the property token is auctioned to repay the pool
3. **Lender recovery**: Auction proceeds repay capital providers based on tranche seniority
4. **Surplus returns**: Any proceeds above the loan amount return to the original borrower

Unlike peer-to-peer lending, capital providers don't receive the property token directly. Instead, the auction mechanism handles liquidation and distributes proceeds.

Borrowers who default on pool loans receive a reduced credit multiplier, which limits future borrowing capacity from the pool. See Loan Defaults & Liquidation for the complete default process and credit impact details.

***

passages.title: Pool-Based Lending
passages.text:
**Borrowers**: Visit fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land) and open your property. The Instant Liquidity card on the property page shows the amount available to you, the available durations, the interest and the repayment date before you confirm. Other visitors see only that the property has liquidity ready, not the owner's figures; a signed-out owner is asked to log in to see what they can borrow.

**Capital Providers**: Deposit at fabrica.land/pools (https://fabrica.land/pools), or reach out at [hello@fabrica.land](mailto:hello@fabrica.land); see For Capital Providers for background. A deposit can be funded from account funds or, where the pool accepts bank deposits and Fabrica has turned the option on for the network, by bank transfer or wire on the same payment screens used for purchases, with the fee and the date the deposit reaches the pool shown before you confirm; a deposit in transit is listed until it arrives.

Step-by-step help: How do I take a loan? (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/11149960-how-do-i-take-a-loan)

passages.title: Loan Defaults & Liquidation
passages.text:
>- What happens when a loan is not repaid, and how the default process protects both borrowers and lenders.

When a borrower fails to repay a loan by the maturity date, the loan enters default. Fabrica has built a structured default process that follows established commercial law (UCC Article 9) to protect both borrowers and lenders.

This page explains what happens at each stage, what rights each party has, and how the process differs between lending protocols.

***

passages.title: Loan Defaults & Liquidation
passages.text:
Borrowers receive reminder emails 14 days, 5 days, and 1 day before maturity (in the property's local timezone), and reminders may include a refinance or extension offer when available. There is no grace period at maturity.

***

passages.title: Loan Defaults & Liquidation
passages.text:
A loan defaults when it reaches its maturity date without full repayment. There is no automatic grace period beyond the contractual deadline.

| Stage | What Happens |
|-------|-------------|
| **Maturity reached** | Loan expires without repayment; default is detected automatically |
| **Default notice** | Borrower receives notification of the default |
| **UCC notice** | Borrower receives a formal notice under the Uniform Commercial Code |
| **Objection window** | Borrower has a defined period to object, redeem, or request an accounting |
| **Liquidation** | If the borrower does not act, the lender claims the token or an auction occurs |

The exact timeline depends on the lending protocol:

| Protocol | UCC Notice Type | Objection Window |
|----------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Pool-based** | Notice of Disposition (sale of collateral) | 10 days |
| **NFTfi** | Notice of Default (proposal to accept collateral) | 20 days |

The NFTfi figures describe the historical NFTfi integration. Other peer-to-peer venues set their own notice types and objection windows.

***

passages.title: Loan Defaults & Liquidation
passages.text:
A defaulted loan does not immediately transfer ownership. The borrower retains rights during the objection window:

**Right to redeem.** The borrower can repay the full loan amount (principal plus accrued interest) at any time before liquidation completes. Repayment returns the property token to the borrower and cancels the default.

**Right to object.** The borrower can formally object to the lender's proposed disposition of the collateral within the objection window.

**Right to an accounting.** The borrower can request a statement of the total amount owed, including principal and interest.

**Continued beneficial ownership.** Until liquidation is finalized, the borrower remains the beneficial owner of the property under the Fabrica Trust.

***

passages.title: Loan Defaults & Liquidation
passages.text: The default process follows **UCC Article 9** (Secured Transactions), which governs what happens when a borrower defaults on a secured loan.

passages.title: Loan Defaults & Liquidation
passages.text:
The UCC provides a well-established legal framework that courts, attorneys, and financial institutions understand. Fabrica's default process follows the same UCC Article 9 framework that governs traditional secured-loan defaults.

The Fabrica Trust agreement specifies that the standards and procedures encoded in the lending smart contracts are "agreed standards" for purposes of UCC 9-603. The UCC's baseline commercial-reasonableness duty still applies and cannot be waived; in a contested disposition a court has the final say.

passages.title: Loan Defaults & Liquidation
passages.text:
Each UCC notice includes:

* The borrower's identity
* The trust name and property description (legal description, county, and token identifier)
* The debt amount owed
* The type of disposition proposed (strict foreclosure or sale)
* The borrower's rights during the objection window

***

passages.title: Loan Defaults & Liquidation
passages.text:
The former NFTfi integration used a **strict foreclosure** model under UCC 9-620/9-621:

1. Borrower receives a Notice of Default proposing that the lender accept the collateral in full satisfaction of the debt
2. Borrower has **20 days** to object, redeem (repay), or request an accounting
3. If no objection is raised and no repayment is made, the lender claims the property token
4. The lender becomes the new beneficial owner of the trust and the property

After claiming the token, the lender can:
* Hold the property as an investment
* Sell it on the Fabrica marketplace or any NFT marketplace
* Remove the property, converting to traditional title ownership (see Remove a Property)

The specifics above (notice type, 20-day window, strict foreclosure) applied to NFTfi. Another peer-to-peer venue would follow its own contract's notice and liquidation terms, which the trust treats as the agreed standards for that loan (see UCC Article 12).

passages.title: Loan Defaults & Liquidation
passages.text:
The lending pool uses a **public auction** model under UCC 9-610:

1. Borrower receives a Notice of Disposition informing them the collateral will be sold
2. The property token is auctioned after the notice period
3. Auction proceeds are distributed to capital providers by tranche seniority
4. Any surplus above the total debt returns to the original borrower

Capital providers do not receive the property token directly. The auction mechanism handles liquidation and distributes proceeds automatically.

***

passages.title: Loan Defaults & Liquidation
passages.text:
Defaults affect a borrower's ability to access future loans:

| Defaults | Credit Multiplier |
|----------|------------------------------|
| 0 | 1.0x (full borrowing capacity) |
| 1 | 0.5x (50% of normal capacity) |
| 2+ | 0.05x (effectively restricted) |

This multiplier is applied to the property valuation when calculating the maximum loan amount a borrower can receive from the lending pool. Peer-to-peer lenders set their own terms and may independently consider a borrower's history.

***

passages.title: Loan Defaults & Liquidation
passages.text:
It is important to understand the boundaries of the default process:

* **Default does not automatically transfer ownership.** The borrower remains the beneficial owner until liquidation completes.
* **Default does not affect other properties.** Each loan is secured by a specific property token. Default on one loan does not encumber other properties.
* **Default does not bypass the trust.** The lender who acquires a token through liquidation becomes a beneficiary under the same Fabrica Trust agreement, with the same rights and obligations as any property owner.
* **Default does not require Fabrica's involvement.** The smart contract enforces the loan terms. Fabrica sends notices as a service, but the onchain mechanics operate independently.

***

passages.title: Loan Defaults & Liquidation
passages.text:
Once liquidation completes:

1. The property token transfers to the new owner (lender or auction winner)
2. The new holder becomes the beneficial owner under the trust
3. All property obligations (taxes, maintenance, compliance) transfer to the new owner
4. The loan is marked as liquidated and closed

The new owner has the same rights as any Fabrica property owner, including the ability to borrow against the property, sell it, or remove it back to traditional ownership.

passages.title: Peer-to-Peer Lending
passages.text:
>- Borrow against your property or lend to property owners through peer-to-peer loans.

In peer-to-peer lending, a lender and borrower agree directly on loan terms, rather than drawing from a pool. Because Fabrica property tokens are standard ERC-1155 NFTs, they can be used as collateral in **any peer-to-peer lending protocol that supports NFTs**, with no Fabrica-specific integration required. A token holder simply takes a loan on whichever venue is active and competitive.

Fabrica's first peer-to-peer integration was a direct, in-app one with NFTfi, where the earliest loans against property tokens were originated and ran their full course onchain (repaid, or liquidated on default). That direct integration has since been removed and NFTfi has shut down, but the point it proved still holds: the tokens are standard collateral that outlives any single venue. A good peer-to-peer venue to use today is Gondi (https://gondi.xyz). For in-app borrowing, Fabrica also offers a pool-based path.

> The sections below describe how the former NFTfi integration worked, retained as a worked example of the peer-to-peer model. NFTfi has shut down and there are no outstanding NFTfi loans against Fabrica properties; another peer-to-peer venue (such as Gondi) would differ in its specifics.

passages.title: Peer-to-Peer Lending
passages.text:
1. **List Your Property**: A Fabrica property token was automatically available as collateral on NFTfi
2. **Receive Offers**: Lenders reviewed the property and submitted loan offers with their terms
3. **Accept an Offer**: The borrower chose the offer that best fit their needs
4. **Receive Funds**: Loan funds (typically stablecoins) were transferred to the borrower's account
5. **Repay**: The borrower paid back principal plus interest by the due date to reclaim the token

During the loan, the property token was held in NFTfi's smart contract. The borrower retained beneficial ownership and full rights to use the property.

passages.title: Peer-to-Peer Lending
passages.text:
1. **Browse Properties**: Lenders reviewed Fabrica properties on fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land)
2. **Conduct Due Diligence**: They evaluated the property using metadata, Property checks, and third-party valuations
3. **Make an Offer**: They specified their terms, loan amount, interest rate, and duration
4. **Await Acceptance**: The property owner reviewed and accepted the offer
5. **Earn Interest**: They received repayment with interest, or claimed the property token on default

***

passages.title: Peer-to-Peer Lending
passages.text:
NFTfi loans were fully customizable. Lenders specified:

| Term | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Principal** | The loan amount offered |
| **Interest Rate** | Annual percentage rate (APR) |
| **Duration** | Loan period (typically 7-90 days) |
| **Currency** | Usually USDC or ETH |

Borrowers could receive multiple offers and choose the one that best suited their needs.

***

passages.title: Peer-to-Peer Lending
passages.text:
Lenders could target their offers to specific borrowers:

* **Current Owner Only**: Offer available only to the current property owner
* **Any Owner**: Offer transfers with the property if sold during the offer period
* **Specific Future Owner**: Offer reserved for a known buyer (useful for financing purchases)

***

passages.title: Peer-to-Peer Lending
passages.text:
NFTfi enabled property purchases with built-in financing:

1. A lender created an offer for a property listed for sale
2. A buyer could use that offer to finance their purchase
3. The buyer paid only the down payment at purchase
4. The loan initiated automatically with the sale

This streamlined property acquisition for buyers who wanted to preserve capital.

***

passages.title: Peer-to-Peer Lending
passages.text:
If a borrower failed to repay by the loan end date:

1. **Default notice**: The borrower received a formal UCC notice (Notice of Default) proposing that the lender accept the collateral
2. **20-day objection window**: The borrower could repay, object, or request an accounting
3. **Lender claims token**: If no action was taken, the lender claimed the property token through NFTfi
4. **Ownership transfers**: The lender became the new beneficial owner of the property

The lender then has full ownership rights and can:
* Sell the property on Fabrica or other marketplaces
* Hold the property as an investment
* Develop or utilize the land
* Remove the property, converting to traditional title ownership

See Loan Defaults & Liquidation for the complete default process, borrower rights, and UCC compliance details.

***

passages.title: Peer-to-Peer Lending
passages.text:
For borrowing inside the Fabrica app, use the pool-based path: browse your properties on fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land), select a property, and click "Get Instant Loan" to see available terms (see Pool-Based Lending).

For a peer-to-peer loan, use any lending protocol that accepts ERC-1155 NFT collateral and follow that venue's process to make or accept an offer against your property token. Gondi (https://gondi.xyz) is a good option today (the former NFTfi integration, whose mechanics are described above, has shut down). Because property tokens are standard ERC-1155 tokens, they remain usable as collateral wherever such lending is offered.

passages.title: Mail Forwarding
passages.text:
Receive scanned property correspondence directly to your email.

When a property is added, the trust is assigned a physical mailbox. Counties and other parties send official correspondence to this address, and Fabrica forwards it to you electronically.

passages.title: Mail Forwarding
passages.text:
1. **Mailbox Assignment**: Each trust receives a dedicated physical mailing address
2. **Mail Collection**: Official correspondence arrives at this address
3. **Scanning**: Fabrica scans all received mail for the property
4. **Email Delivery**: Scanned documents are forwarded to the current token holder's email

passages.title: Mail Forwarding
passages.text:
Common correspondence forwarded to property owners includes:

| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Tax Bills** | Property tax statements and payment notices |
| **Assessment Notices** | Changes to assessed property value |
| **County Communications** | Official notices from the local jurisdiction |
| **Legal Documents** | Any legal correspondence addressed to the trust |

passages.title: Mail Forwarding
passages.text:
To receive forwarded mail:

* **Register an Account**: Create an account on fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land)
* **Provide Email**: Ensure your email address is up to date
* **Connect Your Wallet**: Link the wallet holding your property token to your account

When a property transfers to a new owner, mail forwarding automatically routes to the new token holder (if they have a registered account).

***

passages.title: Mail Forwarding
passages.text:
> Mail forwarding is a convenience service, not a guarantee of receiving all property-related communications.

**Counties may not send notices reliably:**
* Some jurisdictions don't mail tax bills consistently
* Address changes may not be processed promptly
* Notices can be delayed or lost in transit

**Your responsibility:**
* Proactively track tax due dates for your property
* Verify payment status directly with the county
* Don't rely solely on receiving a mailed notice before paying

Property tax information is also included in your token's metadata and monitored by validators as part of Property checks. However, the ultimate responsibility for timely tax payment rests with the property owner.

***

passages.title: Mail Forwarding
passages.text:
Mail forwarding is provided as part of the Fabrica validator's services in the United States. Other validators operating in different jurisdictions may offer similar or alternative notification services.

See Validators for more information about validation services.

Step-by-step help: What happens to mail sent to my property or trust? (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/16280934-what-happens-to-mail-sent-to-my-property-or-trust)

passages.title: Death & Estate Planning
passages.text:
How tokenized property passes to heirs and legal successors.

When a property owner dies, their tokenized property needs to transfer to their heirs or estate. The Fabrica Trust addresses this directly, providing clear paths whether or not the heirs have access to the deceased owner's wallet.

***

passages.title: Death & Estate Planning
passages.text:
The trust agreement (Section 7.6) provides that succession follows lawful control. The person who lawfully succeeds to control of the wallet, called the **Key Successor**, can keep operating immediately, without a court order as a condition of continuity. Lawful succession can come through a will, a trust, intestacy, a survivorship or community-property rule, or the wallet's own recovery or succession arrangement. A Key Successor can:

* **Exercise owner rights directly**, including using, transferring, or selling the property
* **Dissolve the trust** by removing the property (burn the token, receive a deed)
* **Continue holding** the property as a tokenized asset

Lawfulness is what matters: merely finding someone's keys does not make access lawful, and a person who obtains access by theft is not a Key Successor.

Because the property's recorded title is held by the Fabrica Trust (not by the deceased individual), the owner's death does not itself require the land to be conveyed by a new deed; the trust continues to hold title. The beneficial interest, which is personal property under the trust agreement, passes under the estate law of the owner's domicile, and it may still be subject to estate administration, creditor claims, and estate tax depending on the jurisdiction. The agreement makes no claim of automatic probate avoidance. Property owners should consult an estate planning attorney for guidance specific to their situation.

passages.title: Death & Estate Planning
passages.text:
This path requires no court order as a condition of continuing to operate the property, and no Fabrica involvement. Deeding the property out of the trust to a successor does require recorded proof of succession at that step.

***

passages.title: Death & Estate Planning
passages.sectionTitle: If Heirs Do Not Have Wallet Access
passages.text:
If the heirs cannot access the wallet, the trust agreement provides a modified version of the Token Recovery process (Section 10.3 of the trust agreement). The process follows the same self-service recovery path with these modifications:

**1. Claimant identity**

The claimant is the deceased owner's legal successor: an executor, administrator, or heir as determined by applicable law.

**2. Proof of legal succession**

The Notice of Lost Token Control must be accompanied by proof of legal succession that is valid under the laws of the jurisdiction where the property is located. Acceptable documents include:

* Letters testamentary
* Letters of administration
* Small estate affidavit
* Any equivalent instrument recognized by local probate or succession laws

This proof is recorded together with or as an exhibit to the Notice.

**3. Completion**

After the 90-day Quiet Period expires without contest or wallet activity, the legal successor steps into the position of the beneficiary. They can then direct the trustee to execute a Deed of Distribution, transferring the property out of the trust.

If the legal successor cannot obtain proof of succession that satisfies the requirements of the jurisdiction where the property is located, the dissolution proceeds through the court order path.

***

passages.title: Death & Estate Planning
passages.text: Property owners can simplify the inheritance process by taking a few steps during their lifetime:

passages.title: Death & Estate Planning
passages.text:
* **Document wallet recovery information** (seed phrases, hardware wallet locations) in a secure location accessible to your estate
* **Include digital asset instructions** in your estate plan or will
* **Consider a multi-sig wallet** where a trusted family member or attorney holds one of the required keys

passages.title: Death & Estate Planning
passages.text:
* **Name a trustee** other than yourself, so the trust has continuity if you are incapacitated
* **Inform your estate attorney** that you hold tokenized real estate and provide them with a copy of the Fabrica Trust agreement
* **Include the property token** in your asset inventory for estate planning purposes

passages.title: Death & Estate Planning
passages.text:
For tax purposes, the beneficiary of the Fabrica Trust is treated as the property owner. Estate tax treatment of tokenized property follows the same rules as traditional real property. Property owners should consult with a tax advisor for guidance specific to their situation.

***

passages.title: Death & Estate Planning
passages.text:
The trust agreement does not currently include specific provisions for incapacity (where the owner is alive but unable to manage their affairs). However:

* If the owner has granted a **power of attorney** that covers digital assets, the agent may be able to act on their behalf
* If the owner is under a **court-appointed conservatorship or guardianship**, the conservator or guardian may petition the court to manage or dissolve the trust under the court order path
* If the owner has set up a **multi-sig wallet**, other signers may be able to act

> Estate planning for digital assets is an evolving area of law. Property owners should consult with an attorney who is familiar with both real estate and digital asset law to ensure their estate plan adequately covers tokenized property.

passages.title: Property Lifecycle
passages.text:
Explore the stages from tokenization to redemption in real estate.

Tokenizing your land is what unlocks the rest: once a property is a token you can sell it in minutes or borrow against it, with adding a property taking about 10 minutes of your time. Any real estate property can be added to Fabrica (aka tokenized), fully used onchain, and, if necessary, removed back to the legacy system.

---

passages.title: Property Lifecycle
passages.text:
| Stage                        | Description                                              |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Add a Property** | Upgrade a property onchain here: https://fabrica.land/go |
| **Onchain**   | Transfer, trade, or use the token as collateral          |
| **Remove a Property** | Redeem the token back to traditional ownership           |

---

passages.title: Property Lifecycle
passages.text:
Adding a property converts traditional ownership into an onchain NFT through title review, legal wrapper creation, and token issuance.

**Key steps:** Property submission → Title review → Identity verification → Legal wrapper creation → Document signing → Recording → Token issuance

Learn more about adding a property →

---

passages.title: Property Lifecycle
passages.text:
Once issued, the property NFT can be transferred, used as collateral, held, or utilized within other onchain applications and protocols. Ownership transfers occur entirely onchain without traditional deed recordings.

**Transfer types:** Direct wallet transfers, marketplace sales, DeFi collateralization

Learn more about Onchain Transfers →

---

passages.title: Property Lifecycle
passages.text:
Removing a property converts onchain ownership back to traditional real estate ownership by burning the token and transferring the title.

**Key steps:** Initiation → Document preparation → Token burn → Title transfer → Entity dissolution

Learn more about removing a property →

---

passages.title: Property Lifecycle
passages.text: Throughout all stages, validators continuously verify property claims, update Property checks, and maintain metadata.

passages.title: Remove a Property
passages.text:
Redeeming tokens back to traditional ownership

Removing a property (aka redeeming the token) converts onchain ownership back to traditional real estate ownership. The property owner redeems their token in exchange for full traditional title.

passages.title: Remove a Property
passages.text:
1. **Initiation**: The token holder initiates redemption through the Fabrica platform.
2. **Document Preparation**: Legal documents are prepared to transfer the title out of the holding entity.
3. **Token Redemption**: The NFT is redeemed via the smart contract `burn()` function.
4. **Title Transfer**: The deed is recorded, transferring the title from the holding entity to the owner.
5. **Entity Dissolution**: The holding entity is dissolved.

***

passages.title: Remove a Property
passages.text:
When a token is redeemed (burned):

| Action                 | Result                                                                 |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Supply Reduction**   | The total supply of the token is permanently reduced/burned.          |
| **Ownership Transfer** | Legal ownership transfers from the holding entity to the last beneficial owner. |
| **Record Updates**     | County records are updated to reflect the change.                       |
| **Trust Dissolution**  | If a holding entity was used, it is dissolved.                          |

***

passages.title: Remove a Property
passages.text:
Redemption is implemented through:

```solidity
function burn(
    address from,
    uint256 id,
    uint256 amount
) public whenNotPaused returns (bool success)

function burnBatch(
    address from,
    uint256[] memory ids,
    uint256[] memory amounts
) public whenNotPaused returns (bool success)
```

***

passages.title: Remove a Property
passages.text:
Property owners always have multiple paths to redeem, even if the Fabrica platform is offline:

**Direct Smart Contract Interaction**
Users can invoke the `burn()` function directly on the Fabrica smart contract via Etherscan; the trustee's recorded deed out of the trust then completes the redemption (any lawyer can assist, see Legal Assistance below).

**Legal Assistance**
A lawyer can assist in drafting a deed from the holding entity into the new owner's name. The Fabrica Trust instrument is explicitly designed to facilitate this process independently, supporting continuous accessibility regardless of Fabrica's operational status.

**Lost Key Recovery**
If you have lost access to your wallet and cannot burn the token, the Fabrica Trust provides a separate recovery path that does not require blockchain access. See Token Recovery for the complete process.

***

passages.title: Remove a Property
passages.text:
Removing a property typically takes a few hours or days to complete, depending on the jurisdiction and recording requirements.

Step-by-step help: How do I remove a property from Fabrica? (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/8546018-how-do-i-remove-a-property-from-fabrica)

passages.title: Add a Property
passages.text:
>- Transforming traditional property ownership into digital assets for onchain use.

Adding a property (aka tokenizing it) is what unlocks everything else: once your land is a token, you can sell it in minutes or borrow against it (including land that banks won't lend on), without re-recording a deed for each transaction. Adding a property transforms traditional ownership into a digital asset that can be used onchain.

The entire process requires just 10 minutes online from the property owner. Start here: Add your property (https://fabrica.land/go)

There are three ways in:

passages.title: Add a Property
passages.text:
* **From the homepage map.** Every US parcel lights up on the map at fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land). Click a parcel that is not yet on Fabrica and the map asks whether it is your land; confirm, sign in if needed, and the property is set up and claimed for your account, then its page opens. (A click on a parcel already on Fabrica opens its property page instead.)
* **By search.** fabrica.land/go (https://fabrica.land/go) finds a parcel by address, parcel number, or a point on the map and walks through the same steps one at a time.
* **From the property's own page.** A property that was started without an owner (for example from a mailed QR code, or by a visitor who did not sign in) shows **Claim this property** on its page until someone claims it. Sign in and claim it there; the page reloads in the owner view, with any pending steps. If the record was started under an earlier version of the trust agreement, claiming it opens a fresh record for the same parcel under the current agreement, with a new token id, and the old link follows to it. A property that has already been claimed, or whose token has been issued, never shows the button.

A property page is created the moment the process starts, and the owner can list it for sale right away (see below).

passages.title: Add a Property
passages.text:
1. **Property Submission**: The owner provides property information to Fabrica or another validator, including how title is currently held as the recorded deed states it (for example "an unmarried person" or "a married person, as their sole and separate property"); the deed into the trust names the owner the same way. Some jurisdictions ask further questions that their recording forms need.
2. **Title Review**: The validator verifies ownership, chain of title, and encumbrances.
3. **Identity Verification**: The owner completes KYC/AML verification (see Regulatory Framework).
4. **Legal Wrapper Creation**: A holding entity (typically a Fabrica Trust) is created to hold the title.
5. **Document Signing**: The owner signs deed and trust documents, normally with a remote online notary.
6. **Recording**: The deed is recorded at the local jurisdiction, transferring title to the holding entity. Where the county supports it, recording is electronic.
7. **Token Issuance**: An NFT is issued via the smart contract `mint()` function.

passages.title: Add a Property
passages.sectionTitle: Selling While the Property Is Being Added
passages.text:
The steps above do not have to finish before the property can be put to work. The property page goes live as soon as the process starts, and the owner can list the property for sale right away while title review, document preparation, and the remaining steps continue in the background.

* **Listing is immediate.** Set a price and go live at any point during the process. Buyers can discover the property and make offers while the remaining steps complete.
* **Paperwork can wait for a buyer.** Document signing, recording, and token issuance can complete at closing, after a buyer commits. Signing ahead of time is optional: completing the paperwork early issues the token sooner, which enables instant purchases of a listed property and borrowing against it.
* **Fees stay deferred either way.** The setup fee is authorized up front, which charges nothing, and is collected once, the first time the property is sold, borrowed against, or used in another app; it is waived if the property is removed unused. The fee dialog states the amount, these three outcomes, and what the fee covers before the owner authorizes it. See Fees.

While these background steps run, the property page shows a compact status indicator that tells the owner when a step actually needs their input and marks the steps that can wait until closing. See Selling Your Property for how listing works during this period.

passages.title: Add a Property
passages.text:
When a user initiates tokenization, the validator conducts a comprehensive review that confirms:

| Check                      | Description                                                            |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Present owner identity** | Identifies who is named as grantee on the most recently recorded deed. |
| **Chain of title**         | Confirms deeds record transfers from grantors to grantees in a chain.  |
| **Encumbrances**           | Identifies any liens or encumbrances that may affect the property.     |
| **Legal description**      | Helps ensure a match between prior deeds and the onchain description.      |

passages.title: Add a Property
passages.text:
Properties with existing liens can still be added, but these affect Property checks and may restrict certain features:

| Encumbrance Type            | Impact                                             |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Tax liens or due taxes      | Unpaid property taxes fail a Property check.       |
| Mortgage liens              | Outstanding loans may restrict lending features.   |
| Any other involuntary liens | Outstanding issues may affect the ability to add the property. |

Owners should resolve liens so their Property checks pass and their property token keeps full utility.

passages.title: Add a Property
passages.text:
Users receive a link to meet remotely with an online notary and sign documents. In jurisdictions where online notarization isn't available, remote or in-person notarization can be arranged.

Signed documents are then:

* Electronically submitted to counties via e-recording, or
* Physically mailed to counties lacking digital processes.

passages.title: Add a Property
passages.text:
Some counties do not accept electronic recording from Fabrica. For a property in such a county, Fabrica can switch the process to paper while the documents are under review. On the paper route:

1. The documents are prepared with full notary blocks, including in jurisdictions where Fabrica otherwise uses electronic signatures only.
2. The owner signs them in person before a notary, with no online signing session to complete.
3. The owner records the deed at the county and returns the recorded copy to Fabrica.
4. Fabrica checks the county index, attaches the recorded deed to the property with its instrument number and recording date, and the token is issued.

A paper-route property goes through the same title review, identity verification, and fee approval as any other, and it appears on the marketplace from the moment the process starts, like every property being added.

passages.title: Add a Property
passages.text:
An owner can cancel the process at any point before the token is issued, and Fabrica can reject a document set during review. In either case, starting again on the same parcel opens a fresh process under the current rules, with the owner's questions asked again and the documents generated anew, rather than resuming the old one. A setup fee that was already authorized or paid carries over, so it is never authorized or charged twice.

The final notarized and recorded deed is also attached directly to the Property Token, enabling buyers and lenders to verify the outcome and cross-check with county records.

passages.title: Add a Property
passages.text:
After the property is added:

* The property title is held by the holding entity (e.g., Fabrica Trust).
* The property token represents beneficial ownership of the property.
* The token holder has full property rights as defined in the Operating Agreement.

Step-by-step help: How do I add a new property to Fabrica? (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/8542400-how-do-i-add-a-new-property-to-fabrica)

passages.title: Onchain Operations
passages.text:
Transferring and utilizing property tokens effectively.

Once issued, a property token can be transferred, used as collateral, integrated into compatible applications and protocols, or simply held. Fabrica prioritizes blockchain as the definitive source of truth: ownership transfers occur entirely onchain without traditional deed recordings.

passages.title: Onchain Operations
passages.text:
| Type                  | Description                                                      |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Direct Transfer**   | Simple wallet-to-wallet transfer of ownership.                    |
| **Marketplace Sale**  | Sale via OpenSea, Fabrica marketplace, or other NFT marketplaces. |
| **Collateralization** | Using the NFT as collateral for loans (e.g., the DeFi lending pool).   |

***

passages.title: Onchain Operations
passages.text:
Ownership is legally transferred through onchain token transactions. Token holders have full property rights granted by the property's legal wrapper, as defined in the Operating Agreement. However, the legal wrapper entity remains the recorded owner on county tax rolls.

**Key points:**

* Transfers happen entirely onchain without traditional deed recordings.
* The holding entity remains the recorded owner at the local jurisdiction level.
* Beneficial ownership follows the token as defined in the Operating Agreement.
* Validators continuously monitor and update Property checks.

***

passages.title: Onchain Operations
passages.text:
Some U.S. counties require notification when the ultimate beneficiary changes without a traditionally recorded deed. In such cases, Fabrica or another authorized validator assists users by notifying counties using jurisdiction-specific forms.

County notification procedures vary significantly across states. For detailed requirements, see the validator guide.

***

passages.title: Onchain Operations
passages.text: Beneficial ownership depends on how the token is held. See Custody Types in the Property Token reference for details on wallet, multi-sig, and smart contract custody.

passages.title: Token Recovery
passages.text:
What happens when you lose access to your wallet or private keys.

Losing access to a wallet's private keys is one of the most common concerns in crypto. For most digital assets, lost keys mean lost assets. The Fabrica Trust structure is designed differently: because the property exists in the real world and the trust agreement governs ownership, the protocol includes a legal recovery path that does not depend on blockchain access.

> For a detailed look at how the recovery mechanism was designed, see Lost Keys, No Lost Land (https://blog.fabrica.land/lost-keys-no-lost-land) on the Fabrica blog.

***

passages.title: Token Recovery
passages.text:
The Fabrica Trust provides two paths for recovering property when wallet access is lost:

| Path | When to Use | Timeline |
|------|------------|----------|
| **Self-Service Recovery** | Owner lost their own keys, no competing claims | ~90 days |
| **Court Order** | Theft, disputes, contested ownership | Varies by jurisdiction |

***

passages.title: Token Recovery
passages.text: This is the primary recovery path. It allows a property owner who has lost access to their wallet to recover full ownership of their property without Fabrica's involvement and without going to court.

passages.title: Token Recovery
passages.text:
**1. Record a Notice of Lost Token Control**

The owner executes a sworn affidavit, notarized and in recordable form, declaring that they have lost the ability to redeem the Property Token. The Notice must identify:

* The full legal description of the property (matching the token's legal description) and the assessor parcel number where the county uses one
* The trust name exactly as the property is vested of record, and the recording reference of the deed that conveyed the property into the trust
* The claimant's name and a mailing address for contest notices
* The Token ID and Token Contract address
* The Blockchain Network
* The last known wallet address holding the token
* A description of the circumstances of loss

The Notice also requests indexing against both the trust and the claimant, so it surfaces in a title search. It is recorded with the county recorder where the property is located.

**2. Notify Interested Parties**

Within 10 calendar days of recording, the owner sends a copy of the recorded Notice by certified mail to:

* The property address (as shown in county assessor records) and, if different, the assessee mailing address on the county tax roll; for unimproved land with no situs address, the assessee mailing address alone satisfies this
* Any holders of recorded liens, mortgages, or encumbrances against the property
* Any secured party of record under a UCC financing statement covering the token or the beneficial interest

passages.title: Token Recovery
passages.text:
Within the same 10 days, the claimant also sends an onchain notice: a transaction directed to the wallet holding the token that identifies the recorded Notice, so anyone watching the token's address sees the claim.

**3. Wait Through the Quiet Period**

A **90-day Quiet Period** begins on the date the Notice is recorded. During this period:

* Any interested party can contest the Notice by recording an instrument with the same county recorder (such as a lis pendens or affidavit of adverse claim); a contest is also effective if the recorder refuses a tendered instrument, or if notice of filed legal proceedings is delivered to the trustee and claimant, before the Quiet Period expires
* If the wallet holding the token initiates any blockchain transaction during this period, the process halts automatically (this protects against false claims of lost access)
* If a contest is made through any of these channels, the process halts and the matter moves to the court order path

**4. Deliver a Sworn Certificate**

After the Quiet Period expires without any contest or wallet activity, the owner delivers a sworn certificate to the trustee confirming:

* No blockchain transaction was initiated by the wallet during the Quiet Period
* No contest was recorded or delivered during the Quiet Period, and no instrument inconsistent with the claim appears in the county records (whenever recorded), except as disclosed in the certificate
* The owner remains the rightful beneficiary

**5. Receive a Deed of Distribution**

passages.title: Token Recovery
passages.text:
The trustee executes a Deed of Distribution transferring the property out of the trust into the owner's name. The deed is recorded at the county level, completing the transfer to traditional ownership.

**6. Token Becomes Void**

Upon recording of the Deed of Distribution, the original Property Token becomes a **Void Token**. It confers no ownership rights regardless of who holds it on the blockchain.

***

passages.title: Token Recovery
passages.text:
When the self-service path cannot be used, a court can order dissolution of the trust. This applies to:

* **Stolen tokens**: Where the token was taken through unauthorized access
* **Contested ownership**: Where multiple parties claim beneficial ownership
* **Interrupted quiet period**: Where a blockchain transaction occurs during the Quiet Period and the origin is disputed
* **Any other situation** where the self-service process cannot complete

The court order substitutes for both the token burn requirement and the cryptographic signature requirement. Courts with jurisdiction include California state or federal courts (San Francisco County) or courts where the property is located.

***

passages.title: Token Recovery
passages.text:
A Void Token is a Property Token that has been dissociated from the property and the trust. Key characteristics:

* **No ownership rights**: A Void Token confers no beneficial ownership, no owner rights, and no interest in the property
* **Exists onchain**: The token may continue to exist as a blockchain record, but it represents nothing
* **Not revived by recovery**: A token voided through this recovery process cannot be reconnected to the property. (The one different case is involuntary loss of title under Section 10.5, such as a tax sale or foreclosure: there the Void Token carries wind-up rights to residual proceeds, and the trust is reinstated if a court later sets the external transfer aside)
* **No reliance on control**: Even if someone has "control" of a Void Token under UCC Article 12, they acquire no property rights

The legal validity of the void status is established by the recorded Deed of Distribution, not by any offchain database or platform status.

***

passages.title: Token Recovery
passages.text:
The recovery mechanism works because the Fabrica Trust is designed with two layers of ownership:

1. **Onchain layer**: The token on the blockchain
2. **Offchain layer**: The trust agreement and county records

Under normal operation, these layers are synchronized: the token holder is the beneficial owner. But the trust agreement explicitly provides for situations where the onchain layer becomes inaccessible. The 90-day Quiet Period provides a safeguard against abuse, and the county recording system provides public notice and legal enforceability.

This approach mirrors established legal processes like quiet title actions, which courts and title companies already understand and accept.

***

passages.title: Token Recovery
passages.text:
The recovery mechanism includes multiple protections to prevent misuse:

| Safeguard | How It Works |
|-----------|-------------|
| **Sworn affidavit** | Filing a false affidavit is perjury, a criminal offense |
| **County recording** | Creates public, searchable notice of the claim |
| **Certified mail notice** | Helps ensure lienholders and interested parties are informed |
| **90-day Quiet Period** | Gives any legitimate holder time to respond |
| **Blockchain monitoring** | Any wallet activity during the Quiet Period halts the process |
| **Contestability** | Any party can challenge the claim by recorded instrument, refused tender, or delivered notice of litigation |
| **Court fallback** | Disputes are resolved by courts with jurisdiction |

***

passages.title: Token Recovery
passages.sectionTitle: What To Do If You've Lost Access
passages.text:
1. **Do not panic.** Your property is not lost. The trust agreement provides a clear recovery path.
2. **Try key recovery first.** Check for seed phrase backups, hardware wallet recovery, or wallet provider support.
3. **If keys cannot be recovered**, initiate the self-service process by preparing a Notice of Lost Token Control.
4. **Consider working with a lawyer.** While the process is designed to work without legal counsel, an attorney familiar with real estate law can assist with the notarization, recording, and certified mail steps.
5. **Contact Fabrica support** (optional). Fabrica can help guide you through the process, but your recovery does not depend on Fabrica's involvement.

***

passages.title: Token Recovery
passages.text:
The recovery mechanism is designed to work regardless of whether Fabrica continues to exist:

* The trust agreement is open source and self-contained
* The county recording system is a public institution
* Any notary and any lawyer can assist with the process
* No Fabrica approval, platform access, or involvement is required

This is consistent with Fabrica's walk-away test: every property owner can operate independently of the platform.

Step-by-step help: I lost access to my account. Is my property gone? (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/16280942-i-lost-access-to-my-account-is-my-property-gone)

passages.title: Property Obligations
passages.text: >- Owning a property onchain comes with the same obligations as owning a property traditionally.

passages.title: Property Obligations
passages.text:
Owning a property token means owning the underlying real property, with all the rights and responsibilities that entails. This page outlines the ongoing obligations property owners should be aware of.

> Property obligations vary significantly by jurisdiction. The information below reflects common requirements in the United States, where Fabrica validators provide support. Property owners in other jurisdictions should consult local professionals.

passages.title: Property Obligations
passages.text:
The owner of the Fabrica property token is responsible for paying property taxes. Taxes are assessed by local governments, and failure to pay may result in:

* Liens being placed against the property
* Penalties and interest charges
* Potential foreclosure proceedings

passages.title: Property Obligations
passages.text:
In the United States, the Fabrica validator assists property owners with tax obligations:

* Property tax information is included in token metadata
* Validators monitor tax status as part of ongoing validation
* Tax delinquencies affect the property's Property checks

The holding entity (e.g., Fabrica Trust) remains the recorded owner at the local jurisdiction level, so tax notices are typically sent to the trust.

> While Fabrica forwards mail and monitors tax status, property owners should proactively verify and pay taxes on schedule. Tax notices are not always reliably delivered by counties, so don't rely solely on receiving a notice before paying.

Fabrica provides mail forwarding to help you receive tax bills and other official correspondence electronically.

passages.title: Property Obligations
passages.text:
Property insurance is the owner's responsibility. Considerations include:

* **Liability coverage**: Protection against claims from injuries on the property
* **Property coverage**: Protection against damage or loss
* **Title insurance**: Protection against title defects. A title review is performed when the property is added; title insurance may be available and varies by underwriter and jurisdiction

Insurance requirements may vary based on property type (developed vs. unimproved land) and location.

passages.title: Property Obligations
passages.text:
Property owners remain responsible for:

* Maintaining the property in compliance with local codes
* Addressing any violations or citations
* Managing access and use of the property
* Environmental compliance where applicable

passages.title: Property Obligations
passages.text:
Property obligations that are not met can cause some of your token's Property checks to fail. Issues that may cause a check to fail include:

* Unpaid property taxes
* Some outstanding liens, such as a mortgage with an open balance

The checks do not detect every lien, easement or other claim against the property. Failed Property checks may impact your ability to sell the property or use it as collateral for lending.

passages.title: Property Obligations
passages.text:
Property obligations are highly dependent on where the property is located. In the United States, Fabrica's validator infrastructure helps manage these obligations as part of the protocol's application layer.

For properties in other jurisdictions, local validators would need to implement equivalent support. The Fabrica framework provides a model for how jurisdiction-specific obligations can be integrated with onchain property ownership.

Property owners should always:

* Consult local real estate professionals
* Understand jurisdiction-specific requirements
* Maintain records of compliance

See Regulatory Framework for more information on how Fabrica operates within legal requirements.

Step-by-step help: Who pays property taxes? (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/8809464-who-pays-property-taxes)

passages.title: Buying a Property
passages.text:
Purchase property tokens on Fabrica or other NFT marketplaces.

Buying a property on Fabrica is straightforward. Browse available listings, evaluate properties using the provided data and Property checks, and complete your purchase using your preferred payment method.

passages.title: Buying a Property
passages.text:
Browse properties at fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land). Each listing includes:

* **Property Details**: Location, size, legal description, and parcel information
* **Property checks**: What each check tests and whether it passed, a starting point for your own research, not a title search or title insurance
* **Valuation Data**: Third-party estimates and assessed values
* **Documents**: Recorded deeds and trust documents attached to the token
* **Maps and Media**: Satellite imagery, parcel boundaries, and photos

The homepage is a map of US land with the properties for sale listed beside it: pan or zoom and the list follows the map, filter by state, and sort by price or acreage; on a phone the properties for sale come first. Every state, county and place has its own page (for example `fabrica.land/us/arizona` or `fabrica.land/us/arizona/coconino-county`) that opens the marketplace on that area, and a property's county and state link to those pages. Property cards show how many active offers a property has. On a property page, the map can be expanded and its flyover played or paused.

passages.title: Buying a Property
passages.text:
On a property page, one Marketplace card carries the decision: whether the property is for sale, the asking price, the estimated value with the sources behind it (see Property Valuation), and the Buy now and Send offer actions. When a listed property cannot be bought at the moment, the card says that buying is paused and why (for example, the asking price does not cover the seller's loan payoff), and offers a way to message the owner. When the property backs a loan from the DeFi lending pool, the card says so and that the sale pays the loan off at closing, so the buyer never takes it over. A Records card shows the legal description, the deed into the trust, the trust and its agreement, and the token, and the property's history is told as a short account of what the land has been through on Fabrica: listings, sales, transfers, and each loan from start to finish.

***

passages.title: Buying a Property
passages.text:
Before purchasing, review:

| Factor | What to Check |
|--------|---------------|
| **Property checks** | Which checks passed or failed, and what each one tests |
| **Duplicate Claim** | Watch for a "duplicate claim" warning, which means another token claims the same legal parcel |
| **Encumbrances** | Check for liens, easements, or other claims on the property |
| **Property Taxes** | Review tax status and payment history |
| **Valuation** | Compare asking price to third-party estimates |
| **Documents** | Review the recorded deed and trust agreement |

Property checks give a quick summary, but reviewing the underlying data helps you make an informed decision.

passages.title: Buying a Property
passages.text:
When more than one token references the same county parcel (the same assessor parcel number and holding entity), Fabrica surfaces a **duplicate claim** warning so buyers are not misled. Because a single deed can belong to only one owner, at most one of those tokens represents the real property. The warning appears on the property page, as a ribbon on the property's marketplace card, on the map, and again in the purchase flow. If you see it, confirm the deed and current ownership before buying, since purchasing a duplicate may leave you without the underlying property.

***

passages.title: Buying a Property
passages.text:
Checkout runs on Fabrica's own payment screens. You choose how to pay, and each option shows its processing fee and the date by which the property becomes yours before you choose; totals include processing fees.

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Account funds** | Stablecoins already in your Fabrica account. No processing fee, and the sale settles right away |
| **Bank transfer** | A one-time debit from a bank account you link. The property stays the seller's until the payment clears |
| **Card** | A card payment. The limit per payment includes the fee |
| **Wire** | For larger amounts. You send it from your bank: the app shows the recipient, routing and account details, the reference to include and a send-by date, and emails them to you. A wire sent from an account in another name, or without the reference, is returned |
| **External wallet** | Connect an external wallet and pay with stablecoins |

Bank, card and wire payments are processed by Coinflow, Fabrica's payment provider, which is named on the screen. Fabrica turns each of these options on per network; an option that is switched off or paused is not offered, and the checkout says so (for example, that bank payments are paused and account funds still work). Each option has its own limit, and an option that cannot take the amount says so.

passages.title: Buying a Property
passages.text:
**Identity verification.** Bank transfers and wires always need identity verification, and card payments above a threshold do too; account funds never do. Verification happens once: your name, home address, date of birth and the last four digits of your Social Security number are checked by the payment provider (occasionally with a photo of your ID and a selfie), and Fabrica keeps only whether you are verified. The same verification covers cashing out. Linked banks and cards and your verification status are managed from the Payment methods section of your profile.

All prices are displayed in USD. Payments are processed and settled in stablecoins. Buyers paying directly from their own crypto wallet pay the Ethereum network fee for the purchase transaction; bank and card buyers never touch it.

**While a bank payment clears.** The token stays with the seller until the bank clears the payment: the property page and its cards show "Sale pending" for the whole time, the expected date is shown, and you are emailed when ownership moves. If the property is sold to someone else before your bank payment clears, the app tells you that your payment is being returned to your bank. A card payment completes the purchase shortly after it goes through. A declined or returned payment is explained in plain words with what to do next, and nothing is charged for a declined card.

***

passages.title: Buying a Property
passages.text:
If a property isn't listed for sale, or if you want to negotiate:

1. **Submit an Offer**: Specify your offer amount and expiration
2. **Owner Reviews**: The property owner sees your offer on their dashboard, with the marketplace fee and the amount they would receive (marked as estimates until the fee is final)
3. **Acceptance**: If accepted, the sale completes onchain and the seller's dialog finishes as soon as the sale transaction is mined
4. **Expiration**: Unaccepted offers expire automatically

You can submit offers on any property, whether or not it's actively listed for sale. An owner whose property is still being set up can accept an offer only once setup is complete.

***

passages.title: Buying a Property
passages.text:
Financing a purchase by paying only a down payment, while a loan covers the rest and initiates automatically at the sale, was offered through the former NFTfi integration (now shut down) and depended on lenders having active offers. It is not currently offered in-app; for external venues see Peer-to-Peer Lending.

Today, the supported route is to acquire a property and then borrow against it through the pool-based lending integration (Pool-Based Lending), which provides instant liquidity against the token you hold. See Lending for the current options.

***

passages.title: Buying a Property
passages.text:
When you buy a property:

1. **Transaction Executes**: Payment and token transfer happen atomically onchain (for a bank-funded purchase, once the payment clears)
2. **Token Received**: The property token appears in your Fabrica account
3. **Ownership Transfers**: You become the beneficial owner of the trust and property
4. **County Notification**: Where required by the local jurisdiction, Fabrica assists with notifications

Right after a purchase, listing or removing the property is held for a moment until Fabrica's records show you as the owner. If you own properties through several linked accounts, a property page tells you which of your accounts owns it and offers to switch.

***

passages.title: Buying a Property
passages.text:
As the new owner, you have full property rights:

* **Use the Property**: Access, develop, or enjoy as permitted by local regulations
* **Sell or Transfer**: List for sale or transfer to another account
* **Borrow Against It**: Use as collateral for lending
