* **Remove a Property**: Convert back to traditional title ownership by removing the property

You also inherit property obligations including taxes and compliance. See Property Obligations for details.

***

passages.title: Buying a Property
passages.text:
Properties can also be purchased on OpenSea and other ERC-1155 compatible marketplaces. When buying externally:

* You'll need a compatible wallet with sufficient funds
* Property context and Property checks may not be displayed
* Financing options are not available
* Transaction fees vary by marketplace

The token functions identically regardless of where you purchase it.

Representing a buyer? See For Real Estate Professionals.

Step-by-step help: What's the process for purchasing a property on Fabrica? (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/8542420-what-s-the-process-for-purchasing-a-property-on-fabrica)

passages.title: Trading Properties
passages.text:
Buy land in minutes. Sell in seconds.

Fabrica property tokens can be bought and sold on the Fabrica marketplace or any NFT marketplace that supports ERC-1155 tokens. Onchain settlement means a sale closes in minutes, with no escrow or recording delay. The Fabrica marketplace at fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land) is built specifically for real estate transactions: the homepage is a map of US land with the properties for sale beside it, and every state, county and place has its own marketplace page.

Trading at volume (flippers, land funds, operators) is where the cost structure changes most: per-transaction costs collapse compared with conventional closings, and inventory stays liquid. See Operating property at scale.

passages.title: Trading Properties
passages.text:
| Platform | Best For | Features |
|----------|----------|----------|
| **Fabrica Marketplace** | Real estate buyers and sellers | Full property details, Property checks, lending integration, listing distribution |
| **External Marketplaces** | Broader NFT audience | Standard NFT trading experience |

***

passages.title: Trading Properties
passages.text:
The Fabrica marketplace offers capabilities designed for real estate:

* **Property Context**: Full property details, maps, documents, and legal information
* **Property checks**: The results of each validator check, displayed prominently
* **Flexible Payments**: Pay with account funds (stablecoins), by bank transfer, card or wire, with the fee and expected date shown per option (see Buying)
* **Lending Integration**: Borrow against owned properties through the pool-based lending integration (see Lending)
* **Listing Distribution**: Listings can be federated to MLSs and other platforms
* **Instant Settlement**: Onchain transactions complete immediately

***

passages.title: Trading Properties
passages.text:
Browse available properties, evaluate using Property checks and property data, and purchase using your preferred payment method.

Learn more about Buying →

***

passages.title: Trading Properties
passages.text:
List your property for a fixed price or receive offers from interested buyers. Listings on Fabrica can be distributed to other marketplaces to expand reach.

Learn more about Selling →

passages.title: Selling Your Property
passages.text:
List your property for sale on Fabrica or any NFT marketplace.

Fabrica property tokens can be sold directly on the Fabrica marketplace or on any NFT marketplace that supports ERC-1155 tokens. This flexibility allows property owners to reach both real estate buyers and the broader NFT market.

passages.title: Selling Your Property
passages.text: The Fabrica marketplace at fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land) is designed specifically for property transactions and offers the best experience for buying and selling real estate tokens.

passages.title: Selling Your Property
passages.text:
1. **Sign In**: Log in to your Fabrica account (by email or with a wallet)
2. **Select Your Property**: Navigate to your property and click "List for Sale"
3. **Set Your Price**: Enter your asking price in USD
4. **Sign the Listing**: Approve the listing with your signature
5. **Go Live**: Your property appears in the marketplace for buyers to discover

Your property remains in your account while listed. The listing is a signed order that authorizes the transfer only when a buyer pays your asking price.

**Photos and videos.** Buyers see your media first, so prepare it from the property page before or after listing. You can add images and videos, caption each one, and review the change summary before saving; a file that cannot be accepted (an unsupported format such as SVG, or a file over 100 MB) is named with the reason while the others still go through, and the save reports each step as it completes. You can also drag photos into order and choose the cover buyers see first, both while the property is still being added and after the token is issued. A video plays in the property's media viewer, and a "Show all" control opens the full gallery.

passages.title: Selling Your Property
passages.sectionTitle: Listing While Your Property Is Being Added
passages.text:
You do not need to wait for the add-a-property process to finish before listing. A property that is still being added can be listed for sale as soon as its page is live, and the remaining steps (document signing, recording, token issuance) continue in the background or complete at closing.

Until the paperwork is signed and the token is issued, the listing is visible and buyers can make offers, but it cannot be purchased instantly; a committed sale completes the remaining paperwork at closing. Completing the paperwork ahead of a sale enables instant purchases. Once the token is issued, a listing created earlier can be confirmed with a single signature to make it instantly purchasable.

passages.title: Selling Your Property
passages.text:
When you list a property on Fabrica, your listing can be federated to other marketplaces and MLSs (Multiple Listing Services) to expand its reach. This allows you to expose your property to a larger audience of potential buyers beyond the Fabrica marketplace.

Your contact details stay out of the listing data. Each distributed listing carries a dedicated Fabrica contact address in its contact fields instead of your email address. When a buyer sends an inquiry through an outside site, Fabrica verifies that the message genuinely comes from that listing service and forwards it to the email on your account, with the buyer's own address set as the reply address, so answering an inquiry is as simple as replying to the email. The buyer also receives a reply pointing them to your property page on Fabrica, where they can buy or make an offer directly. One note: the listing description you write is distributed exactly as you wrote it, so avoid putting personal contact details there.

passages.title: Selling Your Property
passages.text:
Buyers can submit bids on your property, even if it's not listed for sale:

* **Review Offers**: See all pending offers on your property dashboard; property cards show how many active offers a property has
* **Evaluate Terms**: Each offer shows the amount and expiration, and accepting one shows the marketplace fee and what you receive (marked as estimates until the fee is final)
* **Accept**: Accept an offer to complete the sale; the dialog finishes as soon as the sale transaction is mined. A property that is still being set up can accept offers once setup is complete
* **Counter or Decline**: Ignore offers that don't meet your expectations

This bid system allows buyers to express interest and negotiate, giving you flexibility to sell at the right price.

passages.title: Selling Your Property
passages.text:
Fabrica uses Seaport (https://github.com/ProjectOpenSea/seaport), the same protocol powering OpenSea, for secure and efficient transactions:

* **Offchain Orderbook**: Listings and offers are stored on Fabrica's servers
* **Onchain Settlement**: The actual transfer executes onchain when a sale completes
* **No Custody**: Your token stays in your account until the moment of sale
* **Atomic Swaps**: Payment and property transfer happen in a single transaction

***

passages.title: Selling Your Property
passages.text:
When your property sells on Fabrica:

* **Stablecoin Settlement**: Crypto-funded sales settle atomically, and proceeds arrive in your account as stablecoins right away
* **Bank-Funded Sales**: Sales paid from a buyer's bank account or card complete when the buyer's payment clears. Until then the token stays yours and the property shows "Sale pending"; current timelines are in the help center under what happens when your property sells (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/8546153-what-happens-when-your-property-sells)
* **Cash Out**: From your profile, choose an amount, a destination (a bank account or debit card in your name) and a speed; each speed shows its fee, the amount you receive and the expected date, and speeds that cannot take the amount are hidden. You approve a one-time permission for the payment provider (Coinflow) to use that amount from your account, and you are emailed when the money arrives. Before a first cash out you verify your identity once (the same verification used for bank payments) and add a payout bank; a newly added destination is confirmed by email and its first cash out runs at standard speed. The smallest cash out is $5. Cash out is turned on per network by Fabrica; current limits are in the help center

***

passages.title: Selling Your Property
passages.text:
As standard ERC-1155 tokens, Fabrica properties can be listed on any compatible NFT marketplace, including:

* **OpenSea**: The largest NFT marketplace with broad buyer reach
* **Other Marketplaces**: Any platform supporting ERC-1155 tokens

passages.title: Selling Your Property
passages.text:
While selling on external marketplaces is fully supported, keep in mind:

| Factor | Fabrica Marketplace | External Marketplaces |
|--------|--------------------|-----------------------|
| **Buyer Audience** | Real estate focused | General NFT collectors |
| **Property Context** | Full property details, maps, documents | Basic NFT metadata |
| **Property checks** | Displayed prominently | May not be visible |
| **Lending Integration** | Borrow against holdings via the lending pool | Standard purchase only |
| **Listing Distribution** | Federated to MLSs and other platforms | Single marketplace only |
| **Support** | Fabrica team assistance | Marketplace support |

External marketplaces work well for reaching a broader audience, but buyers may have less context about the property and the Fabrica system.

***

passages.title: Selling Your Property
passages.text:
When your property sells:

1. **Automatic Transfer**: The property token transfers to the buyer's account
2. **Ownership Update**: The buyer becomes the new beneficial owner of the trust
3. **County Notification**: Where required by the local jurisdiction, Fabrica assists with county notifications
4. **Validation Continues**: The property's Property checks keep running for the new owner

The new owner receives all rights and obligations associated with the property. See Property Obligations for details on what ownership entails.

Working with clients? See For Real Estate Professionals.

Step-by-step help: How do I list a property for sale on Fabrica? (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/8542455-how-do-i-list-a-property-for-sale-on-fabrica)

passages.title: FabricaAVM
passages.text:
>- Fabrica's in-house automated valuation model for raw land: how it works at a high level, the confidence it reports, and its limits.

FabricaAVM is Fabrica's in-house automated valuation model, purpose-built for raw land. General-purpose AVMs are designed for residential property and tend to be unreliable on vacant parcels, so Fabrica maintains its own model focused on the land case. Most platforms that tokenize real-world assets carry no native valuation layer at all; maintaining a land-specific model and publishing it as a signed, onchain price feed is part of what makes Fabrica usable as lending and DeFi infrastructure, not just a registry.

passages.title: FabricaAVM
passages.text:
FabricaAVM produces, for a given parcel, an estimated market value and a confidence level. At a high level it combines three kinds of input:

* **Transaction data** with enough history and breadth to find meaningful comparables, filtered to genuine arms-length sales.
* **Parcel characteristics** such as location, size, shape, access, topography, and zoning.
* **An ensemble of models** that turn those inputs into an estimate, rather than a single algorithm trusted on its own.

The methodology builds on **OpenAVMKit (https://github.com/larsiusprime/openavmkit)**, the leading open-source toolkit for land valuation (maintained by the Center for Land Economics). Using and contributing to open methodology keeps Fabrica aligned with the state of the art in land valuation and with the wider research community working on the same problem.

passages.title: FabricaAVM
passages.text:
Every estimate carries a **confidence level**. It reflects how much relevant, good-quality comparable data was available for that specific parcel: denser, cleaner local data yields higher confidence, while remote or thinly-traded areas yield lower confidence. Confidence is meant to be acted on, lower confidence calls for wider margins and more independent diligence, and in lending it leads to more conservative terms.

This valuation confidence is distinct from the token's Property checks, which test the token, its owners and the property against county records, lien data and other sources. One is about *what the land is worth*; the other is about *the integrity of the token-to-property link*.

passages.title: FabricaAVM
passages.sectionTitle: Quality principle: closed sales, not asking prices
passages.text: FabricaAVM is driven by recorded, closed-sale data. Listing or asking prices can reflect market sentiment but are not used as primary inputs, because asking prices systematically overstate value and would distort lending decisions. This is a deliberate quality commitment that separates a model suitable for underwriting from one suitable only for rough guidance.

passages.title: FabricaAVM
passages.text:
Every FabricaAVM estimate is accompanied by a full valuation report, generated automatically and attached to the token. Rather than a single number, the report shows how the estimate was reached, which is what a lender underwriting a loan or an owner weighing an offer needs to see.

Each report covers:

* the property's characteristics, including location, lot size, zoning, access, topography, and surrounding-area context;
* a map of the parcel together with the comparable sales the estimate drew on, and a table of those comparables;
* the model's output and confidence, including which parcel characteristics pushed the estimate up or down; and
* a methodology and limitations section that names the data sources behind the estimate.

The report is regenerated whenever the model re-runs for a parcel, so it always reflects the current estimate, and it is retrievable through the API for applications that want to offer it alongside their own data. In the Fabrica app it can be downloaded directly from a property's price details. Like every FabricaAVM output, it is an estimate to inform evaluation, not a licensed appraisal.

passages.title: FabricaAVM
passages.text:
FabricaAVM is in production and improving continuously. Its accuracy and coverage are not uniform, and the model is honest about where it is weak:

* **Non-disclosure jurisdictions.** Some states do not publicly record sale prices, so data-driven estimates there are inherently less reliable.
* **Sparse or unique parcels.** Remote areas, unusual shapes, or one-of-a-kind properties have fewer comparables and lower confidence.
* **Market movement and staleness.** Estimates reflect available data at the time they were produced and are refreshed as new sales appear.
* **Withheld estimates.** When the available data or the model fit does not support a confident result, FabricaAVM returns no valuation rather than publishing a number it cannot stand behind. A withdrawn estimate also clears any earlier value for that parcel, so a stale figure is not left standing in its place.

For these reasons FabricaAVM is one signal among several (see Valuation signals and underwriting), and estimates are starting points for evaluation, not appraisals.

passages.title: FabricaAVM
passages.text: FabricaAVM estimates are available through the API and as EIP-712 signed price quotes for onchain consumption. See the Price Oracle and the valuation API reference for endpoints and the signing scheme. Each minted token also exposes a link to its latest valuation report, so an application can offer the report for download without regenerating it. When the model cannot produce a confident result, the API and the signed quote report no valuation rather than a degraded estimate, so integrators should handle that case explicitly.

passages.title: Valuation
passages.text:
>- How Fabrica values tokenized land: multiple independent signals, a published confidence level, and a signed onchain reference price.

Accurate valuation is the foundation of everything downstream of ownership: pricing a sale, deciding how much to lend against a parcel, and giving owners a credible sense of what they hold. Fabrica treats valuation as a first-class part of the protocol, surfaced on every property page, written into token metadata, and published as a signed onchain reference price.

passages.title: Valuation
passages.text:
Most automated valuation models are built for houses, where sales are frequent and comparable. Raw land is the opposite case, and it is where general-purpose models are weakest:

* **Sparse comparables.** Many parcels rarely trade, and nearby sales can be scarce or stale.
* **Land is not improved property.** The value sits in location, size, access, topography, and zoning, not in a building that can be measured room by room.
* **Noisy source data.** A large share of recorded transactions are not arms-length (family transfers, bulk deals, gifts), and listing or asking prices are not the same as closed sale prices. Treating them as equal is a common cause of overvaluation.

These are real, well-studied problems. Fabrica's approach is built around them rather than around them being solved.

passages.title: Valuation
passages.text:
Fabrica does not rely on a single black-box number. Several independent valuation signals are produced and shown for each property, each with its own context, so that buyers, sellers, lenders, and researchers can see where they agree and where they diverge:

| Signal | What it is |
|--------|-----------|
| **FabricaAVM** | Fabrica's in-house automated valuation model, purpose-built for raw land, with a confidence level per estimate. |
| **Third-party signal** | A land valuation signal from a leading third-party land valuation provider, published alongside Fabrica's own so users can compare independent estimates. |
| **Assessed value** | The local tax assessor's value, useful for tax context (usually well below market). |
| **Last recorded sale** | The most recent county-recorded sale price, for historical context. |

For lending, these are triangulated rather than trusted individually. Independent signals that agree raise confidence; signals that diverge are a flag to be conservative. See Valuation signals and underwriting for how this works.

passages.title: Valuation
passages.text:
* **Property pages** on the Fabrica marketplace.
* **Token metadata**, so estimated value and confidence travel with the token to external marketplaces such as OpenSea and any application that reads the metadata.
* **A signed onchain reference price.** Fabrica's estimated value is published as an EIP-712 signed quote through a public endpoint, consumable by lending pools, vault curators, and analytics tools. The same data that powers the property page powers the oracle. See Price Oracle for the signing scheme and integration details.

passages.title: Valuation
passages.text:
> Valuation signals are inputs for evaluation, not official appraisals.

Land valuation is inherently imprecise, estimates vary between providers, and remote or unique parcels are harder to value accurately. Buyers and lenders should review comparable sales, consider a property's specific characteristics, and obtain a formal appraisal when the stakes warrant it. The published confidence level is there precisely so that low-confidence estimates are treated with appropriate caution.

passages.title: Property Valuation
passages.text:
>- What the value figures on a Fabrica property page mean, and where to read the methodology behind them.

Every Fabrica property page, and the token's metadata, shows a few value figures so buyers, sellers, and lenders can size up a parcel. This page explains what each one means. For the methodology behind them, see how Fabrica values land, the FabricaAVM, and the signals it triangulates.

passages.title: Property Valuation
passages.text:
| Figure | What it is | How to read it |
|--------|-----------|----------------|
| **Estimated value** | On the property page, the highest of the available sources that qualifies (see below). In token metadata, the API and the price oracle, Fabrica's AVM estimate combined conservatively with a third-party land signal | A modeled estimate, shown with a **confidence level** where the source carries one. Lower confidence means treat it with more caution. |
| **Assessed value** | The local tax assessor's value | Useful for tax context; usually well below market and updated on irregular schedules. |
| **Last sale price** | The most recent county-recorded sale | Historical context; may be stale, and some transfers (gifts, foreclosures) are not arms-length. |

These figures are written into the token's metadata, so they travel with the token to external marketplaces such as OpenSea and any application that reads it.

passages.title: Property Valuation
passages.text:
The property page shows one estimated value in its Marketplace card and lists every source behind it, each with its own value and, where it has one, its own confidence. The headline is the highest source whose confidence is at least 50%. County values carry no confidence and always qualify; a source below the minimum stays in the list, marked as not used; and the last recorded sale never sets the headline, because one deed can convey several parcels and the county attaches the whole price to each of them. When no source qualifies, the card shows no estimate.

The `estimatedValue` written into token metadata, returned by the API and signed by the price oracle is more conservative: it takes the lower of the AVM estimate (when its confidence is usable) and the third-party land estimate, falls back to the county's assessed parcel value when neither is available, and is never the last sale. Prices and estimates are shown in whole dollars.

passages.title: Property Valuation
passages.text:
> Value figures are inputs for evaluation, not official appraisals.

Land valuation is inherently imprecise, estimates vary between providers, and remote or unique parcels are harder to value. Review comparable sales, weigh the property's specific characteristics, and obtain a formal appraisal when the stakes warrant it. The published confidence level exists precisely so low-confidence estimates are treated with appropriate caution. For how lending underwrites against these figures, see Valuation signals and underwriting.

passages.title: Property Valuation
passages.text:
Fabrica's estimated value is also published as an EIP-712 signed price quote through a public endpoint, so lending pools, vault curators, and analytics tools can consume a verifiable reference price. The same data that powers the property page powers the oracle.

* **For owners:** the oracle is intended to be funded by a planned yearly fee on the property side (not charged today), similar to a tax assessment or a title-insurance premium.
* **For developers and integrators:** see Price Oracle for the endpoint, signing scheme, and onchain integration.

passages.title: Valuation signals and underwriting
passages.text:
>- Fabrica shows several independent valuation signals and triangulates them for lending rather than trusting any single estimate.

Fabrica deliberately surfaces more than one valuation signal for each property and remains open to additional valuation systems over time. No single model is treated as ground truth. The value of multiple signals is in their agreement and disagreement: independent estimates that converge raise confidence, while estimates that diverge are a signal to be cautious.

passages.title: Valuation signals and underwriting
passages.text:
* **FabricaAVM.** Fabrica's in-house model for raw land, with a confidence level per estimate.
* **Third-party signal.** A land valuation model from a leading third-party land valuation provider. Fabrica publishes this signal alongside its own on property pages, so users can compare two independent estimates side by side. Keeping a parallel third-party signal visible reflects a deliberate openness to multiple valuation systems rather than a single proprietary number.
* **Assessed value.** The county tax assessor's value. Useful for tax context, but typically well below market and updated on irregular schedules.
* **Last recorded sale.** What a buyer actually paid, where a recent arms-length sale exists.
* **Lending pool valuation.** For pool-based lending, the pool applies its own valuation and risk filters on top of the available signals (see Pool-Based Lending).

passages.title: Valuation signals and underwriting
passages.text:
Lending does not act on a single estimate. An underwriting view triangulates the available signals and sets conservative loan-to-value accordingly:

* When independent signals agree, confidence is higher and terms can be set with a normal margin.
* When signals diverge, or when confidence is low (for example a remote parcel with few comparables), the system stays conservative, widening the margin or declining.

This is intentional. Several imperfect, independent estimates that can disagree are safer to underwrite against than one estimate trusted blindly. It is also why Fabrica keeps a third-party signal in view next to its own.

The lending venues consume these signals differently:

* **Pool-Based Lending** (pool-based, the primary live integration) uses estimated value as a starting point and applies additional risk filters to determine automated loan terms.
* **Peer-to-peer** lenders evaluate properties individually and set their own terms; the signals inform but do not determine their offers.

passages.title: Valuation signals and underwriting
passages.text: Because the signals are published on property pages, written into token metadata, and available as a signed onchain reference price (see Price Oracle), capital providers can build their own underwriting policies on top of them, and researchers can study land-valuation behavior across a real, growing set of tokenized parcels. Live protocol and lending statistics are available on the Dune dashboard (https://dune.com/fabrica/dashboard).

passages.title: Build your own validator
passages.text:
How to build and register a validator that verifies and maintains Fabrica property tokens.

Validators are a core component of the Fabrica ecosystem, responsible for verifying property claims, maintaining NFT good standing, and providing metadata services. Third parties can build their own validators to serve specific geographies, property types, or compliance requirements.

passages.title: Build your own validator
passages.text:
A validator must provide the following core functions:

1. **Property Validation**: Verify that the NFT claim matches recorded property documents at the relevant jurisdiction
2. **Metadata Generation**: Provide current metadata for property tokens, aggregating data from multiple sources
3. **Property checks**: Run and maintain Property checks and publish their numeric encoding
4. **Compliance Monitoring**: Ensure ongoing compliance with local regulations and reporting requirements

passages.title: Build your own validator
passages.text:
Validators implement a smart contract that conforms to the Fabrica validator interface (`IFabricaValidator`). The onchain interface is intentionally small, a metadata and operating-agreement resolver, not a transfer gate:

- `defaultOperatingAgreement()`, the validator's default operating agreement URI
- `operatingAgreementName(uri)`, a human-readable name for a given operating agreement
- `uri(tokenId)`, the token metadata URI the validator serves

The validator's address is recorded on each token and resolved to a name through the Validator Registry. Validation, scoring, and any approve/reject decisions happen in the validator's offchain services (below); the protocol does not call the validator to gate a holder's transfers.

passages.title: Build your own validator
passages.text:
Validators typically need to provide:

| Service | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Metadata API** | Serve NFT metadata following standard conventions |
| **Media Server** | Generate dynamic images/animations representing properties |
| **Scoring API** | Return the numeric encoding of Property checks and the individual check results |
| **Valuation API** | Provide property value estimates from third-party sources |

passages.title: Build your own validator
passages.text:
At minimum, validators should perform these validation checks:

- Proof of title verification
- Legal description matching
- Holding entity verification
- Owner KYC/AML status
- OFAC/sanctions screening
- Coordinate validation

See Property checks for what each check tests and how the results are encoded.

passages.title: Build your own validator
passages.text:
To integrate your validator with the Fabrica ecosystem:

1. Deploy your validator smart contract
2. Register with the Validator Registry
3. Implement the required API endpoints
4. Pass Fabrica's validator certification process

passages.title: Build your own validator
passages.text: Building a validator requires technical expertise in blockchain development, real estate title processes, and compliance systems. Contact us at [info@fabrica.land](mailto:info@fabrica.land) to discuss your validator project and receive guidance on the certification process.

passages.title: Property checks
passages.text:
What each property check tests, where its data comes from, and how the results are encoded as a 5-digit number

**Property checks** are the tests a validator runs on each property token: at issuance, on transactions, and periodically. Each check tests one thing about the token, its owners, or the property, and draws on a stated data source: county records, lien data, identity-verification records, ownership and transfer history, or Fabrica requirements. Not every check is a comparison with county records.

Property checks are a starting point for your own research, not a title search or title insurance.

> Property checks were formerly called the Provenance Score (and, in earlier versions of these docs, the confidence score). The feature and its identifiers are unchanged.

> Property checks are a work in progress and continue to evolve as Fabrica refines its validation approach.

passages.title: Property checks
passages.text:
Validators also publish the results as a 5-digit number: **the numeric encoding of Property checks**. Existing identifiers keep their names for compatibility:

* `score`: the numeric encoding of Property checks
* `confidenceScore`: the numeric encoding of Property checks
* `explain_property_checks` (MCP tool): explains the numeric encoding by group, digit by digit. Individual check results must be read separately for the token
* `minScore` (search parameter): the minimum numeric encoding a property must have to be returned

The numeric encoding groups the results differently from the Property checks checklist in the Fabrica app, and it does not show every individual result. It is not the same list, and it is not a percentage, grade or rating.

The fastest read is the leading digit: a value starting with **7** indicates a property in normal standing, while any other leading digit signals the token-property link is compromised or under review and should be treated with caution. The rest of this page explains how each digit is composed.

passages.title: Property checks
passages.text:
The numeric encoding uses a **positional digit system** where each digit represents a group of checks:

| Position       | Group              | Max | What the group covers                                       |
| -------------- | ------------------ | --- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ten-Thousands  | `recoveryStatus`   | 7   | Recovery and integrity status of the token-property link    |
| Thousands      | `pastTitleAndLoad` | 5   | Title, legal description, liens and taxes for the property  |
| Hundreds       | `ownership`        | 3   | Identity-verification records and contact for the owners    |
| Tens           | `onChainHistory`   | 4   | Theft reports, flagged addresses, fees and transfer timing  |
| Ones           | `basicValidation`  | 2   | Foundational documents and metadata the token must carry    |

The maximum possible value is **75,342**.

**Example:** A value of `72101` breaks down as:

* `recoveryStatus` = 7 (Normal)
* `pastTitleAndLoad` = 2
* `ownership` = 1
* `onChainHistory` = 0
* `basicValidation` = 1

The most significant digits (leftmost) represent the most critical ownership-related checks.

passages.title: Property checks
passages.text:
The most significant digit reflects the recovery status of the property. Unlike the other digits, which are computed from Property checks, this digit is set administratively based on recovery events.

| Value | Status             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

| ----- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| 7     | Normal             | Default state. No recovery activity.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

| 6     | Recovery Pending   | A §10.2 Notice of Lost Token Control has been recorded by the Beneficiary to recover access. Token-property link intact; Quiet Period running.                                                                                                    |

| 5     | Stolen             | The token has been reported as stolen via an unauthorized transfer.                                                                                                                                                                               |

passages.title: Property checks
passages.text:
| 4     | Distressed         | The Property is at material risk of loss to a third party through involuntary process (tax sale, judicial foreclosure of a pre-existing lien, eminent domain, or equivalent). The Trust still holds title and the Beneficiary may still cure. Reversible upon cure. |

| 1     | Void               | The token has been permanently dissociated from the Property and the Trust following an Alternative Dissolution Event or involuntary loss of title. **Irreversible.**                                                                              |

A value starting with `7` indicates a property in normal standing. Any other leading digit signals that the token-property link is compromised or under review, and applications should treat the token with caution regardless of the other digits.

passages.title: Property checks
passages.text:
Like every recovery status, **Distressed** is set administratively: a validator assigns it after confirming that an involuntary process has been initiated against the Property that, if uncured, will result in loss of title. Status updates are not instantaneous; they follow the validator receiving and processing the evidence. Examples include:

* The county has issued a tax certificate, tax sale notice, or equivalent post-delinquency instrument
* A lienholder has commenced judicial foreclosure proceedings against the Property
* A condemnation or eminent domain action has been filed

While in the Distressed state, the Property is still held by the Trust and the Beneficiary may take action to cure (pay back taxes, satisfy the lien, etc.). After a successful cure, the validator can return the token to Normal (7). If the process completes and title transfers to a third party of record, the validator moves the token to Void (1).

Applications surfacing a Distressed token to its Beneficiary should display a clear warning of the underlying risk and a path to cure.

passages.title: Property checks
passages.text:
The thousands, hundreds and tens digits count the passing checks in their group. The ones digit (`basicValidation`) encodes two cumulative requirement levels, described below. The recovery digit is an administratively assigned status, described above. What each check tests and where its data comes from:

**`pastTitleAndLoad` (thousands)**

| Check | What it tests | Data source |
| ----- | ------------- | ----------- |
| `proofOfTitleValid` | The proof of title referenced by the token has been checked and confirmed | The recorded deed |
| `claimMatchesLegalDescription` | The claim in the token matches the legal description on record | County records, through a third-party property data provider |
| `holdingEntityMatchesOwnerNameAtAssessor` | The token's holding entity matches the owner name at the county assessor | County assessor records, through a third-party parcel data provider |
| `noLiensFound` | No voluntary liens (such as a mortgage) with an open estimated balance were found. In the application a mortgage shows as "On record" (a claim the owner agreed to, usual for a home), not as an item to review, and it does not change the property's verdict; the check still earns no point in the numeric encoding | Lien data from a third-party property data provider |
| `propertyTaxesCurrent` | Property taxes are up to date | County tax records |

**`ownership` (hundreds)**

passages.title: Property checks
passages.text:
| Check | What it tests | Data source |
| ----- | ------------- | ----------- |
| `currentOwnersKycd` | Every current holder has an identity-verification record | Identity-verification records |
| `allTransfersKycd` | Every recipient of a past transfer has an identity-verification record | Transfer history and identity-verification records |
| `ownerHasVerifiedContact` | The majority owner has a verified email or phone on file | Fabrica account records |

**`onChainHistory` (tens)**

| Check | What it tests | Data source |
| ----- | ------------- | ----------- |
| `notReportedAsStolen` | The token is not on Fabrica's flagged-token list, and OpenSea does not flag it as suspicious (when OpenSea returns a result) | Fabrica's flagged-token list and the OpenSea API |
| `currentOwnersNotInDarklist` | No current holder's address appears on the flagged-address list Fabrica uses | MyEtherWallet's public address darklist, with a copy embedded in the validator as a fallback |
| `feesInGoodStanding` | Platform fees are in good standing (the deferred setup fee authorization is intact) | Fabrica requirements and onchain approvals |
| `transferCooldownMet` | The required post-transfer cooldown period has elapsed | Onchain transfer history |

**`basicValidation` (ones)**

passages.title: Property checks
passages.text:
| Check | What it tests | Data source |
| ----- | ------------- | ----------- |
| `holdingEntityDeclared` | A holding entity (trust/LLC) is declared | Token metadata |
| `formationDocumentAvailable` | The holding entity's formation document (operating agreement) is linked | Token metadata |
| `deedAvailable` | A proof of title document is linked | Token metadata |
| `legalDescriptionAvailable` | The token's claim (legal description) is defined | Token metadata |
| `coordinatesValid` | The property's geographic coordinates are valid | Token metadata |

The `basicValidation` digit is 1 when `holdingEntityDeclared`, `legalDescriptionAvailable` and `coordinatesValid` all pass, and 2 when `deedAvailable` and `formationDocumentAvailable` also pass.

passages.title: Property checks
passages.text:
Applications can read the numeric encoding from the API (`score`) or the MCP server (`explain_property_checks`) as one input to their own research before transacting.

When reading it:

* Check the recovery status digit first (ten-thousands). A value other than `7` indicates the token-property link is compromised or under review.
* Check the next digits for ownership-critical status: title and liens (thousands) and owner verification (hundreds).
* In the thousands, hundreds and tens positions, a higher digit means more checks in that group passed. The ones digit is a requirement level (0, 1 or 2), and the leading digit is a status, not a count.
* Applications can parse individual digits to make decisions based on specific groups of checks, and should read the individual check results where a decision depends on one check.

passages.title: Fabrica US validator
passages.text:
Fabrica (the company) provides a validator for properties in the U.S.

Fabrica's US validator holds **20+ regulatory licenses**. It has operations across all 50 states with varying degrees of functionality, and 3,000+ US counties covered, the result of normalizing jurisdiction-specific rules into a single coherent system.

The validator provides:

1. a media server that generates dynamic images and animations to visually represent the NFTs, under the domain https://media.fabrica.land (https://media.fabrica.land)
2. a metadata server that provides current information about the real property, aggregated from several data sources and exposed using standard NFT metadata conventions for marketplaces under the domain https://metadata.fabrica.land (https://metadata.fabrica.land)
3. an API that provides the Property checks results for the NFT and their numeric encoding. Each NFT is run through a series of tests during its lifetime (at issuance, transactions, periodically and triggered by external events)
4. a price estimation API that returns an estimated value of the property, using data from third parties

passages.title: Validator Registry
passages.text: How the registry resolves validator names to contract addresses across chains.

passages.title: Validator Registry
passages.text: The Validator Registry is a core component of the Fabrica ecosystem that maps each validator's contract address to a human-readable name, so applications can display a token's validator by name instead of a raw address.

passages.title: Validator Registry
passages.text:
A property token stores its validator as a contract address. The registry resolves that address to a human-readable name via its `name(address)` function, providing several benefits:

1. **Improved Readability**: Applications can show a validator's name rather than its cryptographic address
2. **Stable Display**: The onchain validator name travels with the token as a trait, resolved from the address
3. **Cross-Chain Compatibility**: The registry on each chain resolves that chain's validator addresses to names

passages.title: Validator Registry
passages.text:
The Validator Registry maintains the following information for each validator:

* **Name**: Human-readable identifier (e.g., "fabrica-us-validator")
* **Address**: Contract address on each supported blockchain
* **Metadata**: Additional information about the validator's capabilities
* **Status**: Active, deprecated, or pending status

passages.title: Validator Registry
passages.text:
When a property token needs to interact with its validator:

1. The token stores its validator's contract address (set via `updateValidator`)
2. An application reads that address and calls the registry's `name(address)` function
3. The registry returns the validator's human-readable name, which the token also exposes as an onchain trait

passages.title: Validator Registry
passages.text:
The registry currently includes the following validators:

| Name                                              | Description                         | Supported Networks                      |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| fabrica-us-validator | Primary validator for US properties | Ethereum Mainnet, Sepolia, Base Sepolia |

passages.title: Validators Overview
passages.text: How validators verify property claims and maintain NFT integrity

passages.title: Validators Overview
passages.sectionTitle: NFTs and Claims are Verified by Validators
passages.text:
> Validators make properties interoperable across the ecosystem

Validators play a critical role in supporting the reliability and legal standing of property NFTs. They bridge the gap between onchain tokens and real-world property records.

passages.title: Validators Overview
passages.text: Validators perform three essential functions:

passages.title: Validators Overview
passages.text:
Validators inspect NFTs and cross-check the proof of title with local land registries using multiple validation channels:

* **Web3 Validation**: Checking onchain and IPFS data for consistency
* **Local Jurisdiction Records**: Verifying legal property descriptions and title
* **Property Valuation**: Consulting third-party valuation sources

passages.title: Validators Overview
passages.text:
Validators help maintain the ongoing validity of the link between the digital token and the real property, including:

* Supporting reporting requirements
* Monitoring for changes in county records
* Flagging compliance issues

passages.title: Validators Overview
passages.text:
Validators create and update metadata for each property, drawing from:

* User-provided information
* External datasets (GIS, maps, satellite imagery)
* Local jurisdiction data

Validators perform these checks offchain to protect the legal value and compliance of property NFTs. They do not gate or reverse a holder's transfer of an already-issued token; their onchain surface is limited to serving the operating agreement and token metadata (the `IFabricaValidator` interface). Validation, Property checks, and any approve/reject decisions are the validator's offchain services. (Token issuance itself happens onchain via the token contract's `mint()`, not through the validator interface.)

***

passages.title: Validators Overview
passages.text:
Fabrica employs a comprehensive validation system that continuously verifies property information. Validation occurs at key moments:

* During issuance
* On transactions
* Periodically
* When triggered by external events

passages.title: Validators Overview
passages.text: Checks onchain and IPFS data for updated information about the property and recalculates the numeric encoding of Property checks. This includes verification of token base data from the blockchain and token definition/configuration from IPFS.

passages.title: Validators Overview
passages.text: Retrieves and verifies the legal description of the property from third-party land registry APIs, comparing it with the token definition stored in IPFS to ensure continued accuracy.

passages.title: Validators Overview
passages.text:
Updates property valuation information from trusted third-party providers to maintain current market value data.
***

passages.title: Validators Overview
passages.text:
Multiple validators can operate in the same region, using different validation strategies and service levels. This diversity allows for:

* Competition and market pricing
* Independent opinions on the same NFT
* A choice of guarantees or insurance for users

***

passages.title: Validators Overview
passages.text:
While token issuance is permissionless (anyone can technically issue tokens), validators must be registered for their Property checks to be recognized by the ecosystem.

Currently, validator registration is managed by Fabrica. Organizations interested in becoming validators should contact [hello@fabrica.land](mailto:hello@fabrica.land).

In the future, validator registration will transition to decentralized governance, allowing the community to approve and manage validators independently.

For technical requirements, see Build Your Own Validator.

passages.title: What does Fabrica cost?
passages.text: Fabrica's fees are simple, and you will always see them in the app before you commit to anything. Here is the complete list.

passages.title: What does Fabrica cost?
passages.text:
There is no charge to add a property. You authorize a one-time setup fee (currently $500 for most areas, shown in the app before you authorize) that is collected only when you first sell the property, borrow against it, or use it in another app. It is waived if you remove the property without using it.

The fee covers what it takes to set your property up: online notarization, county recording, identity verification, and creating your digital ownership record. Authorizing it costs nothing today. You will see the full breakdown in the Setup fee dialog before you agree.

passages.title: What does Fabrica cost?
passages.text:
Fabrica charges 1% of the sale price, paid from the seller's proceeds. The buyer pays exactly the listed price.

For example: you list your property for $100,000. A buyer pays $100,000. Fabrica keeps $1,000 (1%), and you receive $99,000. The listing screen shows this exact breakdown, including "On sale you'll receive:", before you list.

If you have not yet sold the property, borrowed against it, or used it in another app, the deferred setup fee is collected at the same time.

passages.title: What does Fabrica cost?
passages.text: Fabrica charges no origination fee on loans. Interest is set by the lending pool and shown before you confirm. The interest rate ("Interest at X% APR") and the You repay by amount on the borrow screen are exactly what you will owe. If you have not yet sold the property, borrowed against it, or used it in another app, the deferred setup fee is collected with your first loan.

passages.title: What does Fabrica cost?
passages.text: There is no platform fee to remove a property. Recording costs are handled through the process, and Fabrica guides you through it. If you never sold the property, borrowed against it, or used it in another app, the setup fee you authorized is waived.

passages.title: What does Fabrica cost?
passages.text:
If you pay by bank transfer, card or wire, or cash out to your bank, the payment processor's fee is shown on the option before you confirm. Fabrica does not set it, and paying with the funds in your account has no processing fee.

If you have a question about a specific fee, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more: Fees in depth (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/fees)

passages.title: What is Fabrica?
passages.text: Fabrica lets you sell your land, or borrow against it, online. No months of paperwork, no waiting on closings. Once your property is set up on Fabrica, you can list it for sale, accept offers, or borrow against it, all online and without waiting on traditional processes.

passages.title: What is Fabrica?
passages.sectionTitle: How it works, in one paragraph
passages.text: When you add a property, Fabrica helps you place it in its own legal trust. The trust holds the record title at the county, and a digital Property Token represents ownership of that trust. Transfer the token, and you transfer the property. You own your property through your own trust. You are the beneficiary, and by default you are also your own trustee. Fabrica never holds title to your property and cannot control it. Everything, including transfer, recovery, and removal, works even if Fabrica disappears.

passages.title: What is Fabrica?
passages.text: Yes. Your deed is drafted, notarized, and recorded at the county, the same way any property transfer works. The trust structure is open source, so anyone can read exactly how it works. In California, Board of Equalization tax counsel stated in a 2022 informational analysis that "a transfer of the digital Token is, in substance, a transfer of the underlying real property itself." That is a California property-tax view, not a legal ruling or a rule for every state, but it shows regulators taking the structure at face value.

passages.title: What is Fabrica?
passages.text: You do not need to know anything about crypto to use Fabrica. You sign in with your email, and payments can go through your bank account. Behind the scenes, the Property Token lives on Ethereum, a public digital ledger, which is what makes it possible to sell right away or borrow against it.

passages.title: What is Fabrica?
passages.text:
Fabrica has been doing this for over 7 years. More than 580 property tokens have been minted onchain. Fabrica holds 20+ regulatory licenses. Fabrica has operations across all 50 states with varying degrees of functionality, with 3,000+ counties covered.

For an overview of Fabrica, the protocol and live properties, see about.fabrica.land (https://about.fabrica.land).

passages.title: What is Fabrica?
passages.sectionTitle: What you can do on Fabrica
passages.text:
- Sell. List your property for sale in US dollars and get paid when it sells.

- Borrow. Take a loan against your property, funded by a DeFi lending pool, with the terms shown before you confirm.

- Buy. Browse listed properties at fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land) and buy with your bank account or a crypto account.

- Keep full ownership. Your rights, and your obligations like property taxes, stay exactly yours.

One thing to know before you start: Fabrica focuses on land, meaning vacant or raw parcels. If your property has structures on it, message us in the chat and tell us about your case.

Ready to try it? Go to fabrica.land/go (https://fabrica.land/go) and look up your parcel.

If you get stuck, message us any time through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more: How Fabrica works, in depth (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/getting-started) · The rise of onchain land (https://blog.fabrica.land/the-rise-of-onchain-land)

passages.title: How can I sign up for Fabrica?
passages.sectionTitle: How can I sign up for Fabrica?
passages.text:
Signing up is easy. Go to fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land) and click Log in in the top right corner. You can sign in with your email or a social account. Your secure Fabrica account is created automatically and protected by passkeys on your device, so there is no seed phrase or crypto setup to worry about. If you already use a crypto wallet, you can connect it during login instead.

Once you're logged in, you'll be asked for some basic information to facilitate property-related services.

passages.title: How can I sign up for Fabrica?
passages.sectionTitle: Signing in from a new device
passages.text:
The first time you log in from a new device, Fabrica sends a verification link to your email. Open the link, and you'll be returned to whatever you were doing. This is normal and protects your account.

If you get stuck, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

passages.title: How do I add my property to Fabrica?
passages.sectionTitle: How do I add my property to Fabrica?
passages.text: Adding your property takes a few minutes of your time. We handle the paperwork in the background, and you can watch the progress every step of the way.

passages.title: How do I add my property to Fabrica?
passages.text:
- Go to fabrica.land/go (https://fabrica.land/go), or click "Add a property" at the bottom of the property list on the fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land) homepage (it is on your profile page too).

- Select your State, then your County.

- Type your parcel number into the "APN (Parcel Number)" field and click "Search".

- Prefer to browse? You can also find your land on the map and click the parcel directly.

- When your parcel comes up, click "Upgrade your property" to start.

If that parcel is already on Fabrica, "Upgrade your property" takes you to its property page instead.

passages.title: How do I add my property to Fabrica?
passages.text:
- From the homepage map. On fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land), click your parcel on the map. A small card shows its parcel number, county and owner of record and asks "Do you own this property?". Click "Claim it" (you log in if you aren't yet), the card reads "Setting up your property…", and your property page opens.

- From an unclaimed property page. Some parcels already have a page on Fabrica marked Unclaimed, for example from a postcard or a buyer's offer. If it's yours, click "Claim it" next to the owner line (or "Claim this property" in the Instant Liquidity card). After you log in, the page reads "Claiming this property…" and then opens as your owner view, with no trip to fabrica.land/go.

There is no address search. The APN (Assessor's Parcel Number) is the ID your county uses for your land. You'll find it on your property tax bill or on your county assessor's website.

You don't need to be signed in to find your parcel. If you pick a parcel first and then log in, the process resumes right where you left off.

passages.title: How do I add my property to Fabrica?
passages.text:
After you start, we ask a few questions about who currently owns the property, and you authorize a one-time setup fee. There is no charge to add a property. The fee (currently $500 for most areas, shown in the app before you authorize) is collected only when you first sell the property, borrow against it, or use it in another app, and it is waived if you remove the property without using it.

From there, we prepare your documents, you sign them in a short online notary session, and the deed is recorded with your county. You can sign as soon as your documents are ready, or wait: signing and recording can happen at closing, when your property sells. Signing early is what lets buyers buy right away, and what makes borrowing available. Recording typically takes a few days, though some counties complete within hours. You can follow along on the status bar on your property page, and click "See details" there to see every step.

passages.title: How do I add my property to Fabrica?
passages.sectionTitle: You can list for sale right away
passages.text: You don't have to wait for the setup to finish before testing the market. As soon as your property page exists, you can list it for sale: the listing appears on the marketplace and can start receiving offers while the paperwork completes in the background. Completing the setup is required to accept an offer, close a sale, or take a loan.

passages.title: How do I add my property to Fabrica?
passages.sectionTitle: If your area isn't covered yet
passages.text:
If you see "Not available in your area yet", we're not in your county quite yet, but we're expanding quickly and will reach out the moment your property is eligible.

If you get stuck, message us through the chat bubble in the corner and we'll help.

Learn more: How adding a property works (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/on-ramp) · From deed to onchain land in 10 minutes (https://blog.fabrica.land/from-deed-to-onchain-land-in-10-minutes)

passages.title: How do I buy a property on Fabrica?
passages.sectionTitle: How do I buy a property on Fabrica?
passages.text: Buying land on Fabrica takes minutes, not months. You can pay with the funds in your Fabrica account or with any other payment option the checkout shows for that purchase, and it shows you the fee and the date for each one. Here is the whole process.

passages.title: How do I buy a property on Fabrica?
passages.text:
Start at fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land). The homepage is a map of US land: move the map and the list of properties for sale follows it. You can also browse by place: every property page links to its county and state, and each of those pages shows the properties for sale there. Click any property to see photos, a description, the records, its history, and the Marketplace card with the Asking price and, under it, the Estimated value row.

If the property backs a loan, the card tells you: "This property backs a loan from a DeFi lending pool. The sale pays that loan off at closing, so you don't take it over." If a listing can't be bought right now, the card shows a "Buying paused" chip with the reason, for example that the seller must pay off the loan first. You can still send an offer.

passages.title: How do I buy a property on Fabrica?
passages.text:
- On the property page, click Buy now. The Buy property window opens.

- Review the price. The price you see is exactly what you pay. Fabrica's marketplace fee comes out of the seller's proceeds, not yours. If the seller has a loan and the listing can be bought, the window shows how the price splits: Purchase price, Pays off the seller's loan, Marketplace fee and Seller receives. If it can't be bought right now, the property page shows Buying paused with the reason.

- Check the one confirmation box. It says the purchase is final, that you accept the terms and the property's trust agreement, and that you become beneficiary and trustee of the property's trust. In plain English: the trust that holds the deed becomes yours, so the property becomes yours.

- Under Pay by, click Choose how to pay and pick one. Each option shows its processing fee and the date the property becomes yours:

Account funds: stablecoins (digital dollars) already in your Fabrica account. No processing fee, and the property is yours right away. If you logged in with an external crypto wallet, you also pay a small Ethereum network processing fee.

- Bank transfer: "From a bank you link." You connect a bank account in your name, and the property becomes yours once the payment clears, usually by the expected date shown.

- Card: a debit or credit card. "The card limit includes the fee."

- Wire: "For larger amounts. You send it from your bank."

passages.title: How do I buy a property on Fabrica?
passages.text:
An option that is switched off right now is not shown. An option whose limit is below the price is still shown, but you can't pick it, and it says so, for example "Up to $N per purchase. This price is above the limit." Each purchase uses one payment method; you can't split a purchase between your account and your bank.

- Click Buy for $X (account funds) or Continue to payment (bank transfer, card or wire). The first time you pay from a bank, by wire or with a larger card payment, you verify your identity once, in the same window. Then you review the payment and click Pay $X, or Get wire details for a wire.

- That's it. With account funds or a card, the app confirms the property is yours. With a bank transfer, you see "Your bank payment is on its way", the property page shows Sale pending until the payment clears, and the property becomes yours once the payment clears, usually by the expected date shown. With a wire, send it from your bank with the Reference shown, before the Send by date; the property page shows "Waiting for your wire" and the property becomes yours once the wire arrives. We email you if anything needs your attention.

You will get a confirmation email either way, and the property will appear under My properties in your account menu. Paying from a bank is covered in detail in "Buying with a bank account or card" (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/16280914) in this collection.

passages.title: How do I buy a property on Fabrica?
passages.sectionTitle: What if the property isn't for sale, or the price isn't right?
passages.text: You can send the owner an offer on almost any property, even one that is not listed. See "How do I make an offer on a property?" (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/8546032-how-can-i-place-bids-on-fabrica) in this collection.

passages.title: How do I buy a property on Fabrica?
passages.sectionTitle: Buying as an LLC or with others
passages.text:
If you want an LLC to hold the property, set up your Fabrica account as the LLC. Buying from that account puts ownership of the token, and control of the trust, under the LLC directly; no extra steps needed. There is more detail in "When I buy on Fabrica, what do I actually own?" (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/16280918-when-i-buy-on-fabrica-what-do-i-actually-own) in this collection.

If you get stuck, message us through the chat bubble in the corner. We're happy to walk you through it.

Learn more:

- Buying on Fabrica (developer docs) (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/buying)

- Buy land, pay with your bank account (blog) (https://blog.fabrica.land/buy-land-pay-with-bank-account)

passages.title: Who can buy property on Fabrica?
passages.sectionTitle: Who can buy property on Fabrica?
passages.text:
Almost anyone. Fabrica is open to all users, with one exception: people on government sanctions lists, or located in sanctioned territories, cannot buy.

You don’t need to live in the US, and you don’t need crypto experience. You can sign up with just an email address and pay from a bank account or card. Identity verification happens along the way as part of the normal process, for example through the payment processor when you pay by bank, so there is no separate paperwork step to complete before you can start.

One note for international buyers: owning US property can have tax implications in both the US and your home country. Fabrica can’t give tax or legal advice, so talk to a tax professional who knows cross-border property ownership before you buy.

If you’re not sure whether you can buy, message us through the chat bubble in the corner and ask.

Learn more:

- KYC and AML (developer docs) (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/kyc-and-aml)

passages.title: How do I verify a property before buying?
passages.sectionTitle: How do I verify a property before buying?
passages.text: Every property page gives you tools to check what you are buying. Use them. Here is what each one tells you, and what it doesn't.

passages.title: How do I verify a property before buying?
passages.text: The Property checks card lists what the checks found, grouped as "Key checks", "Claims on the property" and "Good to know". Among them: whether the deed is on file and recorded with the county, whether the county shows property taxes as paid, whether a lien records search found an open mortgage, whether anyone has reported the property as stolen, and whether the people who have held it verified their identity. Each check is titled by its result and names its source. A mortgage the owner took out shows as "Mortgage on record", a fact to know rather than a failure. A chip next to the property name sums up the result, and if the checks pause sales and loans, a banner at the top of the page says why. Property checks are a starting point for your own research, not a title search or title insurance. "What are property checks?" (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/16280935) explains every check.

passages.title: How do I verify a property before buying?
passages.text:
The Records card holds the property's legal record, one row each:

- Legal description, the formal text that defines exactly which land is included. Open the row to read it in full.

- Deed into the trust, the recorded deed that put the property into its trust, with its source. The deed's row opens the document itself.

- The trust agreement, named after the property's trust, which sets out the owner's rights. The row opens the agreement, and you can download it.

- The token's ID, with a link to view it on Etherscan, a public record of Ethereum activity.

Below the rows, the chips Property, Trust and Token point at how the three fit together: the deed puts the property into the trust, and ownership of the property goes with the token, through the trust.

passages.title: How do I verify a property before buying?
passages.text:
If more than one Fabrica property makes a genuine claim on the same parcel (the same county parcel number and holding trust), you will see a clear warning card titled "Important: 1 other claim on this parcel" (or "N other claims"). It names the shared parcel number, says how many claims point at that piece of land, and reminds you that only one can hold the deed: as it puts it, "Buy the wrong one and you may not own the land". Its links take you to the legal description and to the Records card, so you can check the deed and the owner before you buy.

You will see this flag in more than one place: on the property page, as a "Duplicate claim" ribbon on the property's card in the marketplace, as a marker on the map, and again inside the Buy property window before you pay. Wherever it appears, take it seriously and confirm the deed and ownership before going further.

A verified property is not flagged just because look-alike copies exist elsewhere. The warning is reserved for real competing claims, so when you do see it, it is worth your attention.

passages.title: How do I verify a property before buying?
passages.sectionTitle: Do I need a title company or title insurance?
passages.text:
Title insurance is not included by default, and there is no traditional closing with a title company when you buy on Fabrica. Property checks are a starting point for your own research, not a title search or title insurance. You decide what additional title research or insurance you need for your purchase.

The trust structure itself has been cleared for title insurance by First American (https://blog.fabrica.land/title-insurance-after-tokenization), one of the largest title insurers in the country, but that is not the same as a policy on a specific parcel. If you want title insurance for a specific purchase, message us in the chat and we will help you look into it.

passages.title: How do I verify a property before buying?
passages.text:
Fabrica is not a real-estate broker and does not advise on whether a price is fair. The estimated value shown in the Marketplace card is a starting point, not an appraisal. Check the county records, look at the land, and get professional advice where it matters to you.

If you have questions about a specific property, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more:

- How Property checks are encoded (developer docs) (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/confidence-scoring-system)

- Title insurance after tokenization (blog) (https://blog.fabrica.land/title-insurance-after-tokenization)

passages.title: How do I list my property for sale?
passages.sectionTitle: How do I list my property for sale?
passages.text: Listing takes a few minutes. You set the price, review the fees, and confirm. Buyers can then purchase at your price.

passages.title: How do I list my property for sale?
passages.text: Log in and open your property page. You can find it under My properties in the account menu at the top of fabrica.land.

passages.title: How do I list my property for sale?
passages.text:
- On your property page, click Put for sale. The List property for sale window opens.

- Enter your price in the Price: field. Prices are in US dollars. You'll also see the price per acre, so you can sanity-check your number.

- Review the Total fees: section. Expand it to see the Marketplace fee. Fabrica charges 1% of the sale price, paid from the seller's proceeds. The buyer pays exactly the listed price. For example, if you sell for $100,000, you receive $99,000. When the exact fee can't be fixed yet, the rows read Estimated total fees: and Estimated marketplace fee.

- Check On sale you'll receive: (or Estimated amount you'll receive on sale:). This is the amount that lands in your account when the property sells.

- Continue to the confirmation step. Read it carefully: Sales are final. If your price is below the property's estimated value, you'll check an extra box confirming you understand. You'll also accept the terms, then click List for sale.

- Approve the listing steps as they appear: Allow property transfers (the app explains: "Lets the marketplace transfer this and your other Fabrica properties when they sell. Each sale still needs your signature."), then Sign the listing. Each step tells you when to confirm in your account. When you see "Great news: your property is listed", you're done; View listing takes you back to the page.

passages.title: How do I list my property for sale?
passages.text:
- Listings run for 180 days. Once listed, the Marketplace card shows Your asking price and "Listed until" the end date, with a quiet Cancel listing link beside it. You can cancel any time before a sale.

- Sales settle in stablecoins (digital dollars). You can cash the money out to your bank afterward.

- You set the price. The estimated value on your property page is a starting point, not an appraisal, and Fabrica does not advise on pricing.

- You can list before your property's setup is finished. If your property page still shows "Unclaimed", list it anyway: the listing appears on the marketplace and you can gather offers while the paperwork completes. Finishing the setup is what lets you accept an offer and close the sale.

- If your property has an active loan, you can still list it. The sale pays off the loan automatically at closing. See "Selling a property that has a loan on it" (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/16280943-selling-a-property-that-has-a-loan-on-it) for details.

If you get stuck, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more: Selling on Fabrica (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/selling) and Trading (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/trading) in our docs.

passages.title: Offers on your property, and how to accept them
passages.sectionTitle: Offers on your property, and how to accept them
passages.text: Buyers can send an offer on your property even if it isn't listed for sale. Here's how offers work and how to accept one.

passages.title: Offers on your property, and how to accept them
passages.text:
When a buyer uses Send offer, they set an amount and how long the offer stays valid, from 1 to 60 days. The offer is backed by stablecoins (digital dollars), so the money is real and ready.

You'll see offers in the Marketplace card on your property page under "Offers (N)", one row per offer with the buyer's name, the amount and when it expires, for example "Expires Nov 2" or, in amber, "Expires today at 5:00 PM". Buyers can withdraw an offer before you accept it, and offers expire on their own after the chosen period, so don't sit on one you like for too long.

passages.title: Offers on your property, and how to accept them
passages.text:
- Open your property page and find the offer you want in the offers list.

- Click Accept offer. The window shows the offer, the Marketplace fee: and what you'll receive (labelled as estimates when the exact fee can't be fixed yet), and the setup fee if it is still due.

- Check the box confirming that sales are final, click Confirm sale, then approve the steps as they appear: Allow property transfers, then Accept the offer. Each step tells you when to confirm in your account.

- That's it. You'll see "Great news: you sold the property!", and we'll email you a confirmation.

passages.title: Offers on your property, and how to accept them
passages.text:
The offer amount, minus Fabrica's fee, goes to your account. Fabrica charges 1% of the sale price, paid from the seller's proceeds. The buyer pays exactly the offer amount. There is no extra charge for receiving or accepting offers.

Accepting an offer completes the sale, and sales are final. See "What happens when your property sells" (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/8546153-what-are-my-tax-obligations) for proceeds, cashing out to your bank, and the county paperwork that follows.

Two caveats. If your property page still shows "Unclaimed" (setup isn't finished), you can receive offers, but you can accept one only once your property is fully set up: the offers list says "You can accept an offer once your property setup is complete.", and you'll get an email prompting you to finish setup when an offer arrives. And if the property has a loan on it, the list says "Pay off your loan to accept an offer." You can keep the property listed while the loan is open; see "Selling a property that has a loan on it" (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/16280943-selling-a-property-that-has-a-loan-on-it).

If you get stuck, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more: Trading (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/trading) in our docs.

passages.title: How do I cancel a listing?
passages.sectionTitle: How do I cancel a listing?
passages.text: You can take your property off the market any time before it sells.

passages.title: How do I cancel a listing?
passages.text:
- Open your property page. You can find it under My properties in the account menu.

- In the Marketplace card, under Your asking price, click the Cancel listing link next to "Listed until" and the date.

- Confirm in the Cancel listing window: click Continue to Cancel, then approve the Cancel the listing step in your account. You'll see "Your listing is canceled" when it is done.

passages.title: How do I cancel a listing?
passages.text:
- Canceling is free. There is no fee or penalty for taking a listing down.

- You can cancel any time before a buyer completes a purchase or you accept an offer. Once a sale completes, it is final and can't be reversed.

- Listings also expire on their own after 180 days if nobody buys.

- Canceling a listing doesn't affect offers. Buyers can still send offers on an unlisted property, and you can accept or ignore them.

- You can relist whenever you like with Put for sale, at the same price or a new one.

If you get stuck, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

passages.title: How do I remove my property from Fabrica?
passages.sectionTitle: How do I remove my property from Fabrica?
passages.text:
You can take your property off Fabrica at any time. We call this the off-ramp. At the end, your token is retired, a fresh deed is recorded at the county in the name you choose, and the trust dissolves. There is no platform fee for removal, and if you never sold the property, borrowed against it, or used it in another app, the setup fee you authorized is waived too.

One note before you start: you cannot remove a property while it has an active loan. Pay off the loan first.

passages.title: How do I remove my property from Fabrica?
passages.text:
- Open your property page and, in the Owner Toolbox, click Remove Property. You will need an email on your account.

- Tell us who takes title. The dialog asks "Who will take title to the property and how": yourself as an individual, more than one person, or an entity. You will also enter a mailing and tax address for the new owner.

- We prepare your documents. Fabrica drafts the deed and any county forms, and a person reviews them. You will get an email titled "Removing Your Property" when the process starts, and another when your documents are ready to sign.
