passages.title: How do I borrow against my property?
passages.sectionTitle: How do I borrow against my property?
passages.text: Once your property is on Fabrica, you can borrow against it without waiting on traditional processes. There is no application, no negotiation, and no lender to call you back. The loan comes from a DeFi lending pool, a shared fund that runs on its own rules, and the terms are shown on screen before you commit to anything.

passages.title: How do I borrow against my property?
passages.text:
A loan offer needs at least these three things:

- The lending pool has funds available.

- Your property passes the Property checks the lending pool looks at (the deed check and the Fabrica fees check must pass).

- Your property taxes are verifiably current. If the tax status is unknown, borrowing is blocked too.

Other eligibility and valuation requirements also apply, so these three alone do not guarantee an offer.

If your loan amount looks low or shows $0, or the Instant Liquidity card shows a message saying borrowing isn't available instead of the sliders, see "Why is my loan amount low or zero?" (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/16280912-why-is-my-loan-amount-low-or-zero) in this collection.

passages.title: How do I borrow against my property?
passages.text:
- Open your property page and find the Instant Liquidity card. Only you see your borrowing figures there; visitors to your page see a short note that the owner can borrow against the property, without the numbers.

- Use the Amount and Duration sliders to pick how much you want to borrow and for how long. The durations available on the Duration slider are the terms the lending pool currently offers; they can change as the pool changes.

- Review the terms shown: You receive, the interest rate ("Interest at X% APR") and You repay by with the due date and the full repayment. This is exactly what you would owe. There is no separate Fabrica origination fee. Interest is set by the lending pool and shown before you confirm.

- Note the line "The property will be held as collateral until repaid." More on what that means below.

- Click Borrow. The Borrow against your property window opens: accept the terms, then approve the steps as they appear, Approve the property transfer and Start the loan. If your property is listed for sale, a third step, Keep your listing buyable, also appears: it lets a sale of the listed property pay off this loan.

When it completes you will see Loan Funded! and the money arrives in your account as stablecoins (digital dollars). Click Cash Out right there, or Cash out on your profile later, to send it to your bank account.

passages.title: How do I borrow against my property?
passages.text: One thing to know: the setup fee you authorized while adding the property is collected the first time you sell the property, borrow against it, or use it in another app. If this loan is the first of those, the fee is collected now. It is a one-time fee, and it was never charged before because you had not used the property yet.

passages.title: How do I borrow against my property?
passages.text:
While the loan is open, your property token sits with the lending pool instead of in your account. This is custody only. You are still the beneficial owner of the property, you keep your rights to use and enjoy the land, and you get the token back automatically when you pay off the loan. You remain responsible for property taxes during the loan.

If you get stuck, open the chat bubble in the corner and we'll help.

Learn more: How pool lending works (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/lending-pool) · Shirley's story: borrowing against tokenized land (https://blog.fabrica.land/tokenize-land-get-funds-in-minutes)

passages.title: Can I add a property with a mortgage?
passages.sectionTitle: Can I add a property with a mortgage?
passages.text:
Technically, yes. A property with an outstanding mortgage or deed of trust can be added to Fabrica. But while the mortgage is in place, the property cannot be used for a loan on Fabrica, and it cannot be sold through Fabrica either. Because of that, in practice most owners wait until the mortgage is cleared before adding their land.

If you’re close to paying off a loan on your land, that is usually the simplest path: add the property as soon as it’s paid off. Once your property is on Fabrica, you may be able to borrow against it directly through the platform’s Instant Liquidity feature.

Not sure whether something on your title counts? Message us through the chat bubble in the corner, or email hello@fabrica.land, and we’ll take a look with you.

passages.title: Can I cancel adding my property?
passages.sectionTitle: Can I cancel adding my property?
passages.text: Yes. You can cancel any time before your deed goes to the county for recording, and you'll owe nothing.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Can I cancel adding my property?
passages.text:
On your property's page, find the status bar that tracks your setup and click the three-dot menu at its right edge. Choose "Remove property". You'll see an "Are you sure?" confirmation explaining that you can start again anytime but will lose your current progress. Click "Yes, remove it" to confirm.

If the property is owned by more than one person, the cancel option is available to the primary owner on the process.

Changed your mind later? Search for the parcel at fabrica.land/go (https://fabrica.land/go) as you did the first time. A canceled setup starts over from the beginning, as does one that our document review had to reject.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Can I cancel adding my property?
passages.text: Nothing. There is no charge to add a property, and the one-time setup fee you authorized is collected only when you first sell the property, borrow against it, or use it in another app. When you cancel, the property is removed unused, so the fee is waived. No money has left your account at any point.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Can I cancel adding my property?
passages.text:
Once your deed has been submitted to the county, the cancel option goes away, because a real document is being recorded in public records. The process will complete, and if you still want out, you can then remove the property using "Remove Property" on your property page. There's no platform fee for removing a property either, and the unused setup fee is still waived.

If you're not sure which stage you're at, message us through the chat bubble in the corner and we'll check for you.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Ownership types: individual, with someone else, or through an entity
passages.sectionTitle: Ownership types: individual, with someone else, or through an entity
passages.text: Early in the process, a dialog called "Current Ownership" asks how you own the property today. Pick the option that matches your current deed. The documents we prepare have to match how title is actually held, so this step matters.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Ownership types: individual, with someone else, or through an entity
passages.text: You own the property alone, in your own name. We'll just need your full legal name exactly as it appears on your deed.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Ownership types: individual, with someone else, or through an entity
passages.text:
You own the property together with one or more co-owners. You'll also pick the "Form of ownership":

- "as joint tenants": co-owners hold the property together, and when one owner dies their share generally passes to the surviving owners.

- "as tenants in common": each owner holds their own share, which they can pass on separately.

You'll add details for each co-owner so everyone can be included in the documents.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Ownership types: individual, with someone else, or through an entity
passages.text:
The property is owned by an LLC, corporation, or similar entity. We'll ask for:

- The entity's name

- Its type (for example, an LLC)

- The state where it's registered

- The people authorized to sign for it, with each signer's name, email, and role
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Ownership types: individual, with someone else, or through an entity
passages.text:
Below the ownership choice, the same dialog asks a few questions that go onto your deed and county forms. Everyone sees one required dropdown: "How do you hold title, as shown on your current deed?" Pick the wording your current deed uses after your name, for example "a single woman", "a married man, as his sole and separate property", or "a widower". If your deed shows your name alone, or the property is owned by a company or by co-owners, choose the first option, "Name only (also for companies and co-owners)". In most states, when you are the sole individual owner, the phrase you pick is printed after your name on the new deed, so it should match your current deed exactly.

Some states ask more. In California, for example, you also provide a phone number for the county forms, pick "What type of property is this?" (for example "Single-family residence" or "Unimproved lot"), answer "Is this property your principal residence?", and can enter the date you moved in. If the parcel has a building on it, California also asks "Is there a loan secured by this property?" and, if so, the lender's name. These answers fill the county's change-of-ownership form; a lender's name is collected for that form and is not printed on your deed.

When you've filled in your details, click "Continue".
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Ownership types: individual, with someone else, or through an entity
passages.sectionTitle: Not sure how you hold title?
passages.text: Check your current deed. It states exactly who owns the property and in what form. If it's still unclear, a local title company or real estate attorney can tell you quickly. We can't give legal advice, but we're happy to help you through the form itself. Message us through the chat bubble in the corner.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Signing and notarization
passages.text: When your paperwork is ready, you'll sign it with a notary, usually entirely online. The session takes about 10 minutes. Here's what to expect.

passages.title: Signing and notarization
passages.text:
A dialog titled "Your documents are ready" lists what you'll be signing, with a Read link for each:

- Trust agreement: as the dialog puts it, it "sets out your rights and responsibilities as the beneficiary of the trust that holds your property." You are the beneficiary, and by default you are also your own trustee.

- Deed: "Transfers your property into its own trust. The trust holds the title and the token controls the trust, so you keep your ownership rights."

- Local forms: tax and county forms that go along with the recording, "filled in for you."

The dialog also sums up how signing works: you join a video call with an online notary, show a photo ID, and sign everything in one session. Take your time reading the documents. When you're ready, click "Continue to signing". The online notary session opens in a new tab. If the session isn't ready yet, the dialog says so and asks you to check back in a few minutes.

passages.title: Signing and notarization
passages.sectionTitle: What you need for the session
passages.text:
The session runs in your web browser, and the notary needs to see and hear you. Have ready:

- A device with a camera and a microphone. A smartphone can work.

- A government-issued photo ID.

If you are not sure whether your device will work, message us in the chat before your session and we will help you check.

passages.title: Signing and notarization
passages.text:
- The notary verifies your identity: an ID check plus a few questions only you should be able to answer.

- You sign the documents on screen while the notary watches, just like an in-person signing.

That identity check also verifies your Fabrica account. There's no separate step where you upload documents.

Four states require a witness to be present during notarization: Georgia, Florida, Connecticut, and Louisiana. If your property is in one of those states, the witness step is part of the session.

passages.title: Signing and notarization
passages.sectionTitle: If your county only records on paper
passages.text: A few counties don't accept electronic recording from Fabrica. If yours is one of them, we tell you during the document review and the online signing step is skipped. Instead, we send you the documents and instructions, you sign them in front of a notary in person, and you take the signed deed to your county recorder's office yourself. Once the county has recorded it, send the stamped deed back to us and your setup continues from there.

passages.title: Signing and notarization
passages.text: If you're adding several properties, the paperwork can be batched so you sign everything in one single notary session. As the dialog says: "Signing for more than one property? They all go in the same session." See "Can I add multiple properties at once?" (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/8848747-can-i-add-multiple-properties-at-once) in this collection.

passages.title: Signing and notarization
passages.text:
We submit the deed to your county for recording. That typically takes a few days, though some counties complete within hours. You'll get an email when everything is done.

If you get stuck, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more: How adding a property works (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/on-ramp) · From deed to onchain land in 10 minutes (https://blog.fabrica.land/from-deed-to-onchain-land-in-10-minutes)

passages.title: What is the setup fee? (No charge today)
passages.sectionTitle: What is the setup fee? (No charge today)
passages.text: There is no charge to add a property to Fabrica. During setup, a dialog called "Setup fee" asks you to authorize a one-time setup fee, currently $500 for most areas and always shown in the app before you authorize. Nothing is charged today. We collect it once, the first time you sell the property, borrow against it, or use it in another app, and it is waived if you remove the property without using it.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: What is the setup fee? (No charge today)
passages.text:
At the top you see the amount, for example "$500.00", with a "$0 today" label and the line "One-time fee for adding this property".

Under "When it’s charged", the dialog lists three moments:

- "Today": "Nothing is charged. You authorize us to collect it later."

- "When you first sell it, borrow against it, or use it in another app": "We collect it once, at that time."

- "If you remove the property unused": "The fee is waived. You never pay it."

Using it in another app means putting your property's digital ownership record to work in a service other than Fabrica.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: What is the setup fee? (No charge today)
passages.text:
Under "What it covers", the dialog lists everything included:

- Online notarization

- County recording

- Identity verification

- Digital ownership record
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: What is the setup fee? (No charge today)
passages.text:
Click "Authorize fee". There is no box to check. Under the button, the dialog notes: "By authorizing, you accept the Terms of Service." It also has a "How the fee works" link, which brings you to this article.

Your account may ask you to confirm the request. If you decline it there, or something goes wrong, the dialog tells you that nothing was charged and offers "Try again" and "Close".
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: What is the setup fee? (No charge today)
passages.text: Technically, you're granting a spending allowance in USDC, a stablecoin (a digital dollar), not making a payment. Nothing leaves your account when you authorize. The fee is collected once per property, the first time you sell it, borrow against it, or use it in another app. If you never do any of those and later remove the property, you never pay it.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: What is the setup fee? (No charge today)
passages.text:
If your authorization ever lapses, we'll email you to renew it. Without it, your property won't be visible on the marketplace and you won't be able to take out loans against it. You can re-approve any time with "Authorize Fee" in the Owner Toolbox on your property page, or through the link in the email. Both open the same "Setup fee" dialog, with your property shown at the top.

When it goes through, the dialog shows "Fee authorized" and "Nothing was charged. We’ll collect it only when you first sell it, borrow against it, or use it in another app." If you had already authorized the fee, the dialog shows the date you did it and tells you there's nothing else to do.

Questions? Message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more: Fees on Fabrica (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/fees)
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: What happens after I submit my property?
passages.sectionTitle: What happens after I submit my property?
passages.text: Once you start adding your property, most of the work happens on our side. Here's what's going on behind the scenes, how long each part usually takes, and what you'll hear from us along the way.

passages.title: What happens after I submit my property?
passages.text:
Your property page shows a slim status bar near the top. Most of the time it stays quiet, with a note like: "We're getting your property ready in the background: photos, description, title history. Nothing for you to do right now." Progress shows as a row of dots (for example, "3 of 5"), and clicking "See details" opens the full checklist. The exact steps vary by property and county, but you'll typically see steps like:

- "Who currently owns the property?"

- "Preparing your property"

- "Writing a description based on property features"

- "Generating AI pictures tailored to the location"

- "Verifying the property's ownership history"

- "Drafting deed and tax documents"

- "Legal documents are being reviewed" (which becomes "Deed and tax documents are ready")

- "Payment authorization" (shown as "Pay on first use")

When something needs you, the bar says so plainly, for example "1 step needs you: approve the setup fee." with a button that takes you straight there. Those steps usually take about a minute each. If a step runs into a problem on our side, the bar shows "Something needs attention:" with the step, so nothing is ever silently stuck.

You can safely close the page at any point. Everything keeps moving on our side, and we email you whenever a step needs you.

passages.title: What happens after I submit my property?
passages.sectionTitle: You can list for sale while setup continues
passages.text: Your property page is live as soon as you submit, and you can list your property for sale right away. Buyers can see the price and send you offers while the paperwork completes in the background. Completing the setup is what lets you accept an offer, close a sale, or take a loan.

passages.title: What happens after I submit my property?
passages.text: Some steps are fast and automated: writing the property description takes under a minute, and the pictures take a few minutes. Others involve real people. Verifying your property's ownership history can take up to about a day, especially in counties with sparse online records, where our team does the research by hand. Every deed is reviewed by a person before you sign, which usually takes a few hours. In the rare case that review finds a problem we can't resolve, the process is canceled rather than left hanging, so reach out through the chat if that happens.

passages.title: What happens after I submit my property?
passages.text:
Signing, notarization, and county recording usually happen at closing, when your property sells. In the checklist those steps carry an "at closing" tag, which means they're waiting on purpose, not stuck. You can also complete them earlier: when your documents are ready, the status bar reads "Your paperwork is ready. Sign now to let buyers buy right away and to enable borrowing, or wait for a buyer." Signing early means a buyer can purchase right away, without waiting for paperwork at closing.

Signing itself is a short online notary session, about 10 minutes. Then we submit the deed to your county for recording. In the few counties that only record paper deeds, you sign in person and record the deed at the county yourself; see Signing and notarization (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/16280906-signing-and-notarization). Processing time varies by location. It typically takes a few days, though some counties complete within hours, and remote counties without online records can take longer.

After recording, your property is fully set up in your Fabrica account. Fabrica pays the network processing costs for this, not you.

passages.title: What happens after I submit my property?
passages.text:
- "[Your property] is live on Fabrica" when the process begins.

- "Your documents for [your property] are ready to sign" when your documents are prepared, with copies attached.

- "[Your property] has been added to your Fabrica account" once recording is done and everything is in place.

If you get stuck at any step, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more: How adding a property works (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/on-ramp) · The property lifecycle (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/property-lifecycle)

passages.title: Can I refinance or extend my loan?
passages.sectionTitle: Can I refinance or extend my loan?
passages.text:
Often, yes. When the lending pool can support it, your property page shows a Refinance button in place of (or alongside) Borrow.

Refinancing replaces your current loan with a new one at the terms the pool offers today. You set the new amount and duration with the same sliders, and the new terms are shown before you confirm: You receive today (or You pay today, if the new loan is smaller than what you owe), the interest rate ("Interest at X% APR") and You repay by with the due date and the full repayment. The durations you can pick on the Duration slider are whatever terms the pool currently offers. Nothing changes until you accept the new terms in the Refinance loan window and approve its steps; when you see "Great news: your loan is refinanced", the new loan has replaced the old one.

There is no set limit on how many times you can refinance: you can typically do it again and again, as long as the pool will fund a new loan each time.

Two things to know:

- Availability is not guaranteed. The Refinance option depends on the same checks as a new loan: pool funds, your property's Property checks, current property taxes and the other loan requirements. If it is not showing, see "Why is my loan amount low or zero?" in this collection.

- Watch your email near the due date. As your loan approaches maturity, our reminder emails will offer an extension when one is available. That is often the easiest way to get more time.

passages.title: Can I refinance or extend my loan?
passages.sectionTitle: Can I refinance or extend my loan?
passages.text:
If you cannot refinance and cannot repay by the due date, read "What if I can't repay my loan?" in this collection now rather than later. Acting before the due date gives you the most options.

If you get stuck, open the chat bubble in the corner and we'll help.

Learn more: Pool lending (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/lending-pool)

passages.title: Repaying your loan
passages.text: You can pay off your loan at any time before the due date. Here is how, and exactly what you will pay.

passages.title: Repaying your loan
passages.sectionTitle: How to pay off your loan
passages.text:
- Open your property page. While the loan is open you will see a Your loan card. It shows Payoff today (on loans that charge interest only for the time elapsed), the full amount next to Due and the due date, and the APR.

- Click Pay off loan. The Repay loan window opens with the breakdown: Amount borrowed, Interest and Total today.

- Under Pay by, choose how to pay. Account funds uses the stablecoins (digital dollars) in your Fabrica account, with no processing fee, and your property comes back right away. Some loans also offer Card, which pays the whole payoff by debit or credit card for a processing fee; if your loan doesn't support it, the option says "Card isn't available for this payoff." If your account is short, the window tells you by how much; add funds to your account, then click Check account funds again.

- Click Repay $X (or Pay by card) and approve the steps as they appear: Allow the payment, then Repay the loan. When it goes through you'll see "Great news: your loan is paid off".

One important timing note: loan due dates have no grace period. If your due date is close, don't wait on money that is still on its way to your account; pay from your balance, or message us through the chat bubble and we will help you pick the fastest path.

When the payment completes, your property is back in your account. As the window puts it, "The token is back in your account and nothing is held as collateral anymore." You can transfer, remove, or borrow against the property again.

passages.title: Repaying your loan
passages.sectionTitle: What you actually pay: check your loan type
passages.text:
Be careful here, because loans differ and we want you to know before you pay:

- Prorated loans charge interest only for the time that has actually passed. If your loan card shows a Payoff today figure, that is exactly what you would pay today, and paying early saves you money.

- Fixed-term loans owe the full repayment amount no matter when you pay. Repaying early gets your property back sooner, but it does not reduce the cost.

Your loan card tells you which kind you have. If there is no Payoff today figure, assume the full amount shown next to the due date is owed. For a loan that accrues interest, the payoff quote is priced a short time ahead, so it covers the interest that accrues while your payment goes through (it never exceeds the full repayment); if you leave the window open for a while, the app refreshes the amount and asks you to review it again before paying.

passages.title: Repaying your loan
passages.text:
There is no grace period at the due date. If the loan is not fully repaid by then, it defaults. Set your own reminder well before the deadline. We send reminder emails, but emails can land in spam, and the responsibility to repay on time is yours. See "What if I can't repay my loan by the due date?" (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/8602900-what-happens-if-i-don-t-repay-my-loan-by-the-due-date) in this collection for what happens after a default.

If you get stuck, open the chat bubble in the corner and we'll help.

Learn more: Pool lending (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/lending-pool)

passages.title: Why is my loan amount low or zero?
passages.sectionTitle: Why is my loan amount low or zero?
passages.text: This is the question we hear most about borrowing, so here is the honest answer. The Instant Liquidity card shows the most the lending pool will offer against your property right now. When that number is low, or $0, one of the checks below is the reason.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Why is my loan amount low or zero?
passages.sectionTitle: When borrowing is blocked, the card tells you why
passages.text:
When borrowing is blocked entirely, the Instant Liquidity card on your property page shows a short explanation instead of the borrowing sliders. There are two messages you might see:

- "Heads up: borrowing isn't available for this property yet. Its property taxes haven't been verified as current. Check back once they're verified." This is the tax check described just below, and it is the most common blocker.

- "Heads up: this property isn't eligible for borrowing at this time. Check back later." This is the general message when the block is something other than taxes, usually one of the other checks on this page.

These explanations are shown only to you as the owner. Visitors to your property page are not shown your tax status.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Why is my loan amount low or zero?
passages.sectionTitle: Your property must be fully added first
passages.text: You may see a borrowing-power figure while your property is still being added. That preview is real, but taking a loan requires the property to be fully added, with its token issued. Finish the setup and the borrowing option activates.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Why is my loan amount low or zero?
passages.sectionTitle: Property taxes must be verifiably current
passages.text: This is the most common blocker. The pool will not lend against a property with unpaid taxes, and it also will not lend when the tax status cannot be verified. So "unknown" blocks borrowing just like "unpaid" does. If you have recently paid your taxes, it can take time for the county's public records to reflect it. Paying your taxes, and making sure the county shows them as paid, is the single best way to open up borrowing.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Why is my loan amount low or zero?
passages.sectionTitle: The deed and fee checks must pass
passages.text: The lending pool also looks at two of your property's Property checks: "Deed checked against the county" and "Fabrica fees in good standing". Both have to pass. If you never completed the fee authorization, or it lapsed, borrowing stays blocked until it is fixed. You can authorize it from the Owner Toolbox on your property page with Authorize Fee.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Why is my loan amount low or zero?
passages.text: The pool lends against a cautious estimate of your property's value, not the highest one. It takes the minimum of two independent valuation models. Very low-value properties get sharply reduced loan capacity on top of that. This protects both you and the lenders from loans that the land cannot support.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Why is my loan amount low or zero?
passages.text: A past default or liquidation might reduce the amount the pool offers you, depending on how it was resolved. Repaying on time doesn't earn you a bonus, but it keeps your borrowing capacity intact.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Why is my loan amount low or zero?
passages.text: Fabrica does not use a fixed loan-to-value percentage, so there is no rule of thumb to apply to your property's value. The app shows your exact borrowing power for each property: "Unlock up to $N" when you add it, and the Instant Liquidity card on the property page after that. Because the valuations are conservative, that number is often lower than you would expect. Clearing the blockers above is what raises it.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Why is my loan amount low or zero?
passages.sectionTitle: The pool itself may be low on funds
passages.text:
Loan offers depend on how much money (stablecoins, digital dollars) the lending pool has available. If the pool is low, offers shrink for everyone. This usually resolves on its own as the pool refills.

If none of this seems to explain your number, open the chat bubble in the corner and we'll look at your specific property.

Learn more: How property valuation works (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/valuation) · How pool lending works (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/lending-pool)
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: How do auctions work on Fabrica?
passages.sectionTitle: How do auctions work on Fabrica?
passages.text: Auctions on Fabrica happen for one reason: a loan on the property defaulted, and the property is being sold at a public auction to repay it. Regular listings are never auctions. If you see an Auction card on a property page, this is what is going on and how to bid.

passages.title: How do auctions work on Fabrica?
passages.text: The property is real land held in its own trust, the same as any other Fabrica property. The winning bidder becomes the owner: the token transfers to you, and with it the trust and the recorded deed. The auction proceeds pay off the defaulted loan, and anything above the debt and costs goes back to the previous owner.

passages.title: How do auctions work on Fabrica?
passages.text:
- On the property page, find the Auction card. It shows the Current Bid and a countdown clock.

- Click Place Bid. The Place a bid window opens.

- Enter your bid. Each bid must be at least 2% above the current one; the app shows you the minimum ("Minimum bid is $X").

- Bids are in USDC, a stablecoin (a digital dollar), so you need enough USDC in your account. The app walks you through Allow the bid amount and Place your bid. When you see "Great news: your bid is in!", your bid is placed, and the card lists each bid as a short sentence with the bidder's name and amount.

If you don't hold USDC, message us through the chat bubble before you plan to bid and we will help you get your account funded. Do this early: once bidding starts, the clock doesn't wait for a bank transfer.

How long the auction runs depends on the lending pool behind the loan: legacy pools ran 24-hour auctions, and newer pools run 2-week auctions. The countdown on the Auction card shows the time remaining. When the clock runs out, the highest bidder wins and becomes the owner. There is no Fabrica fee for bidding or winning an auction.

passages.title: How do auctions work on Fabrica?
passages.text:
- The current owner remains the owner until the auction closes. When it closes, the winning bidder becomes the new owner. The former owner can keep the property only by being the winning bidder, so you may see the owner bidding in their own auction.

- Auction sales are final. Do your homework on the property before you bid, the same as any purchase: read the records, look at the Property checks, and see "How do I verify a property before buying?" (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/8542447-how-can-i-verify-the-ownership-of-a-property-listed-for-sale) in this collection.

If you get stuck, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more:

- Loan defaults (developer docs) (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/loan-defaults)

passages.title: Buying with a bank account or card
passages.sectionTitle: Buying with a bank account or card
passages.text: You don't need crypto to buy land on Fabrica. In the Buy property window, when Pay by shows a bank option (bank transfer, card or wire), you can pay the way you already pay for everything else. Here is what to expect.

passages.title: Buying with a bank account or card
passages.text:
The checkout can offer three ways to pay from a bank, each with its own fee, limit and timing, shown on the option itself:

- Bank transfer: "From a bank you link." You connect your bank account in a few taps, and the account must be in your name.

- Card: a debit or credit card. "The card limit includes the fee."

- Wire: "For larger amounts. You send it from your bank." You get the details to wire the money, and send it from your own bank.

Next to each option you see the processing fee (or "No processing fee") and "Expected by" with a date, the day the property becomes yours. An option that is switched off right now is not shown. An option whose limit is below the price is still shown, but you can't pick it, and it says so ("Up to $N per purchase. This price is above the limit."). Payments are processed by Coinflow, our payment provider, and any processing fee is theirs, not Fabrica's.

passages.title: Buying with a bank account or card
passages.text: The first time you pay by bank transfer or wire (and for larger card payments), the window asks you to verify your identity. As the app puts it: "Coinflow, our payment provider, checks these details; we keep only whether you're verified. Most people only need this form." You enter your name, home address, date of birth and the last four digits of your Social Security number. Outside the US, you can verify with a photo of your ID and a selfie instead. This is a one-time step, and it also covers cashing out later.

passages.title: Buying with a bank account or card
passages.text:
- Under Pay by, choose your option and click Continue to payment.

- Bank transfer: connect your bank. Card: enter the card details; your bank may ask you to confirm the payment ("Your bank wants to confirm it's you."). Wire: pick or enter the bank you will send it from.

- Review the payment. The review shows the amount, the fee and the total, then click Pay $X. For a wire, click Get wire details instead.

- For a wire, the next screen shows the Reference, Amount, Recipient, Routing and Account to use, and a Send by date. Use Copy all details, include the reference exactly, and send the wire from an account in your name. As the app warns: "Wires without it are returned." The details are in your email too.

passages.title: Buying with a bank account or card
passages.text: With a card, the property is yours once the payment goes through. With a bank transfer, you see "Your bank payment is on its way": the property stays the seller's until your bank clears the payment, usually by the expected date shown ("It can take a few business days to clear."). The property page shows Sale pending in the meantime, with the day you'll become the owner. Then the token moves to you, and the property with it. No action is needed from you; we email you when it is in your portfolio, or if anything needs your attention. A wire shows "Waiting for your wire" on the property page until it lands.

passages.title: Buying with a bank account or card
passages.sectionTitle: If a payment is declined or returned
passages.text:
Declines usually come from your own bank or card issuer: daily limits, fraud holds on an unusual purchase, or insufficient funds. The app tells you what happened and what to do next, for example "Heads up: your card was declined. Try another card or pay by bank transfer." If a bank account can't be used because its name doesn't match your verified identity (joint and business accounts often need the account holder's own name), try another account or pay by wire. If a bank transfer is returned after you started it, we email you about it and the property stays listed, so you can try again. Still stuck? Message us through the chat bubble in the corner and we will figure it out with you.

Learn more:

- Buy land, pay with your bank account (blog) (https://blog.fabrica.land/buy-land-pay-with-bank-account)

- Buy now, pay later (blog) (https://blog.fabrica.land/buy-now-pay-later)

passages.title: Can I trade my land for someone else's land?
passages.sectionTitle: Can I trade my land for someone else's land?
passages.text:
There is no direct land-for-land swap on Fabrica today. The way to do it is two sales: you sell your property and buy theirs. Each sale settles in stablecoins (digital dollars), so the money side is simple and immediate.

A few things to know if you are planning a swap:

- Each property added to Fabrica has its own one-time setup fee, so a swap involving a property that is not on Fabrica yet means adding it first.

- If both owners already have their properties on Fabrica, the two sales can happen back-to-back, which gets you close to a swap in practice.

- If the values differ, the money from your sale covers the difference naturally.

If you are planning a specific swap, message us in the chat bubble in the corner and we will help you think through the steps for your situation.

passages.title: Can I buy in installments or with financing?
passages.sectionTitle: Can I buy in installments or with financing?
passages.text:
Most purchases on Fabrica are paid in full, either with stablecoins (digital dollars) or through your bank account at checkout.

Installment and financed purchases exist in specific cases, but they are not something you can set up on your own in the app today. If a listing interests you and you would need payment terms to buy it, message us in the chat bubble in the corner with a link to the property. We will look at that specific listing and tell you honestly what is possible.

There is also a grounded alternative that works today: buy the property, then borrow against it. Loans are funded by a lending pool, and the terms are shown before you confirm. See "How do I borrow against my property?" (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/11149960-how-do-i-take-a-loan) in this help center.

Learn more: Buy now, pay later on the blog (https://blog.fabrica.land/buy-now-pay-later) · How pool lending works (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/lending-pool)

passages.title: How do I research the land before I buy?
passages.sectionTitle: How do I research the land before I buy?
passages.text: A little research before you buy can save you from surprises after. Here is what the property page gives you, and where to look beyond it.

passages.title: How do I research the land before I buy?
passages.text: Every property page shows an interactive map with the parcel drawn on it, and the Description card's fact strip gives the Size, the Location (the county and state, each a link to the properties for sale there), the Assessor parcel number and the Coordinates, with an Open in Google Maps link that opens the spot. This works even for land with no street address, which is common for raw land. Use the map to see exactly where the parcel sits, what surrounds it, and how the terrain looks.

passages.title: How do I research the land before I buy?
passages.text:
Some listing photos may be AI-generated illustrations based on the location, not photographs taken on the parcel. So do not judge the land by its pictures alone. Always check three things:

- the map and coordinates,

- the Legal description (open its row in the Records card on the property page to read it in full),

- the county's own records.

The parcel shapes drawn on the map are indicative. The recorded legal description is what governs the actual boundaries.

passages.title: How do I research the land before I buy?
passages.sectionTitle: Road access, zoning, and what you can build
passages.text:
Fabrica is a platform, not a real-estate broker, so we do not advise on whether a parcel fits your plans. The county has the answers:

- Look up the parcel with the county assessor for size, taxes, and ownership history.

- Check the county planning or zoning office for zoning, road access, and building rules.

A quick call or web search for "{county name} assessor" and "{county name} planning department" usually gets you there.

Questions land buyers commonly put to the county and other public sources:

- Access. Is there legal access (a recorded easement or public road frontage), and is there a physical road you can actually drive?

- Flood and wetlands. Is any part of the parcel in a flood zone or mapped wetlands?

- Zoning and building rules. What is the zoning, and is there a minimum build size or limits on campers and mobile homes?

- Utilities. How far away are power and water, and would the land need a well and septic?

- HOA or POA. Does the parcel belong to an owners' association with dues or rules?

- Back taxes and liens. Are property taxes current, and are any liens recorded against the parcel?

The answers come from the county and public records, not from us; Fabrica does not evaluate parcels for you.

passages.title: How do I research the land before I buy?
passages.text:
The estimated value on the page is a starting point, not an appraisal. It comes from third-party data sources and models. Do your own diligence on what the land is worth to you.

If you get stuck, message us in the chat bubble in the corner. Learn more: How property valuation works (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/property-valuation) · Questions from landowners (https://blog.fabrica.land/questions-from-landowners)

passages.title: When I buy on Fabrica, what do I actually own?
passages.sectionTitle: When I buy on Fabrica, what do I actually own?
passages.text: The land. Really. Here is how the pieces fit together.

passages.title: When I buy on Fabrica, what do I actually own?
passages.text:
Every property on Fabrica sits in its own trust, and that trust holds the recorded deed at the county. The Property Token represents ownership of the trust. When you buy, the token moves to your account and the trust becomes yours: you become the beneficiary, and by default you are also your own trustee. That is what the checkbox at checkout means when it says you will become a "beneficiary and trustee" of the trust. Transfer the token, transfer the property.

Fabrica never holds title to your property and cannot control it. Everything, including transfer, recovery, and removing the property from Fabrica, works even if Fabrica disappears.

passages.title: When I buy on Fabrica, what do I actually own?
passages.text:
Yes. The deed is recorded at the county, in the trust's name, like any other deed. And California State Board of Equalization tax counsel, in a 2022 informational analysis for property-tax purposes, stated that "a transfer of the digital Token is, in substance, a transfer of the underlying real property itself." That is a California view, not a legal ruling and not a rule for all 50 states, but it says clearly what the design does.

As the owner, you have full owner rights:

- Possession, control, and enjoyment of the land

- The right to sell it, lease it, or borrow against it

- All income the property generates

- You are treated as the owner for tax purposes

passages.title: When I buy on Fabrica, what do I actually own?
passages.text: Owning through a trust doesn't change what landowners owe. Property taxes, insurance, code compliance, and any liens or HOA dues are your responsibility from the day you buy. Take taxes seriously: if they go unpaid and the county sells the property at a tax sale, the trust dissolves automatically and the token becomes void. Unpaid taxes also block borrowing against the property.

passages.title: When I buy on Fabrica, what do I actually own?
passages.sectionTitle: Buying through an LLC or with other people
passages.text:
Entity ownership is part of how Fabrica works. If you set up your Fabrica account (your wallet) as an LLC, buying from that account puts ownership of the token, and with it control of the trust, under the LLC directly. No special steps at checkout and no need to contact us first: the account that buys is the account that owns. The same goes for removing a property from Fabrica later; title can be taken by the entity.

If you are thinking about co-owning with others, this story is a good starting point: How to buy land onchain with your friends (blog) (https://blog.fabrica.land/how-to-buy-land-onchain-with-your-friends).

passages.title: When I buy on Fabrica, what do I actually own?
passages.sectionTitle: Can I buy a fraction of a property?
passages.text: Not through the Fabrica app: checkout sells the whole property, represented by one token. If a group of friends or partners wants to buy together, the straightforward way is through something you set up yourselves, like your own LLC or a shared account, which then holds the token. The story linked above, How to buy land onchain with your friends (https://blog.fabrica.land/how-to-buy-land-onchain-with-your-friends), walks through how one group did it.

passages.title: When I buy on Fabrica, what do I actually own?
passages.text: The token is designed as direct ownership of a specific property, not as an investment product or a share in a pooled venture. You are buying the land itself, through your own trust. If you want the deep dive on this question, see the securities analysis (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/securities-analysis) in our docs.

passages.title: When I buy on Fabrica, what do I actually own?
passages.text:
Fabrica cannot give legal or tax advice. For questions about your specific situation, talk to a licensed professional.

Learn more:

- The Fabrica Trust (developer docs) (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/fabrica-trust)

- Property obligations (developer docs) (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/property-obligations)

passages.title: What happens after I buy?
passages.text: The moment your purchase completes, the property is yours. A few things then happen behind the scenes, and a few things become your job. Here is the honest list.

passages.title: What happens after I buy?
passages.text: Your new property appears under My properties in your account menu. From there you can view it, add photos, put it up for sale later, or borrow against it.

passages.title: What happens after I buy?
passages.text: After a transfer, the county where the property sits gets a change-of-ownership filing. In many places this is automated. If your county needs extra information from you, we will email you (look for "Action Required: Transfer Paperwork"). Please respond to those emails promptly so the filing isn't delayed.

passages.title: What happens after I buy?
passages.text: Official mail sent to the property or its trust gets scanned and emailed to you. Read it and act on it, because it can include tax bills and county notices. Questions about a piece of mail? Write to hello@fabrica.land.

passages.title: What happens after I buy?
passages.text: Tax responsibility passes to you at purchase. Don't wait for a notice to find you: look up the property's tax status with the county assessor and make sure you know when payments are due. Unpaid property taxes have serious consequences, including losing the property at a tax sale, so this is the one item on this list not to put off.

passages.title: What happens after I buy?
passages.sectionTitle: If we ask you for information after the purchase
passages.text: Some counties need details from the new owner to finish their transfer paperwork. If yours does, you will get an email from Fabrica with the subject "Action Required: Transfer Paperwork" and a short form to complete. This email is legitimate: it exists because the county requires it, and completing it promptly keeps the county's records about your property correct. We will never ask you for passwords or payment in that email, just the ownership details the county needs. If you want to double-check any request you receive, message us through the chat bubble before responding.

passages.title: What happens after I buy?
passages.text:
You will receive a confirmation email for the purchase. If you paid by bank transfer, the sale completes once your payment clears, usually by the expected date the checkout showed you, and we will email you if anything needs your attention along the way.

If anything looks off after your purchase, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more:

- Property obligations (developer docs) (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/property-obligations)

passages.title: For title professionals: insuring and closing a property held in a Fabrica trust
passages.sectionTitle: For title professionals: insuring and closing a property held in a Fabrica trust
passages.text: If you are a title agent, escrow officer, or underwriter looking at a property held in a Fabrica trust, this page summarizes the structure in title terms and the documentation available to you. Properties held this way have been covered by title insurance after going through the Fabrica Trust structure, including a policy underwritten by First American, and the structure itself has been cleared for title insurance.

passages.title: For title professionals: insuring and closing a property held in a Fabrica trust
passages.text:
Each property is held by its own state-law trust. The trust is nominee-style: one property per trust, with the trust holding record title and the beneficiary holding all beneficial interest. The transfer into the trust is a change in the method of holding title, not a change in beneficial ownership, and it is not a financing transaction. No lien or encumbrance is created by the trust itself.

The beneficiary is the current holder of the property's token, and under the trust agreement the beneficiary is also the trustee unless a different trustee has been appointed. Trusteeship follows beneficial ownership automatically. Fabrica is not a party to the trust and never appears in the chain of title.

The trust agreement is open source and versioned, so your underwriting team can read the exact instrument governing a given property.

passages.title: For title professionals: insuring and closing a property held in a Fabrica trust
passages.text:
- The full trust agreement for the specific property

- A notarized Certification of Trust naming the current trustee and beneficiary (in California, per the Probate Code certification practice)

- A Statement of Authority or equivalent instrument where the state uses one

- A trustee affidavit covering trust termination when the property is being deeded out

- The recorded deeds in and out of the trust

Signings connected to these instruments are completed with remote online notarization, with the signer's trustee capacity stated in the acknowledgment. If your underwriter prefers language tailored to the trust agreement, we are glad to work through it together; underwriters have drafted satisfactory affidavit language directly from the agreement text before.

passages.title: For title professionals: insuring and closing a property held in a Fabrica trust
passages.text:
Does the trust cloud title? No. The chain shows a deed into the trust and, at exit, a deed out. Quiet title is not required; the standard documentation above has satisfied underwriting review.

Who has authority to sign? The current trustee, which by default is the beneficiary. The Certification of Trust identifies them.

Is this a crypto asset in the chain of title? No. The chain of title contains ordinary recorded deeds. The token operates at the trust-beneficiary level and never appears in county records.

Reach the team directly at hello@fabrica.land. We respond quickly to closing-critical questions.

Learn more: The Fabrica Trust (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/fabrica-trust), Title insurance after tokenization (https://blog.fabrica.land/title-insurance-after-tokenization)

passages.title: Property taxes, reassessment, and ownership changes
passages.sectionTitle: Property taxes, reassessment, and ownership changes
passages.text: This article is for assessors evaluating whether a transfer involving a Fabrica Trust is a change in ownership for reassessment purposes.

passages.title: Property taxes, reassessment, and ownership changes
passages.sectionTitle: Transfers into or out of an owner's own trust
passages.text:
When an owner places their own property into a trust on the platform, or removes it, the transaction is structured as a change in the form of ownership, not a change in beneficial ownership. The same person who held the property before the transfer is the beneficiary of the trust after it. The beneficiary appoints the trustee and, by default, serves as their own trustee. Fabrica is not a party to the trust and never holds title.

The standard documentation package for these transfers includes:

- A certification of trust naming the beneficiary.

- In California, a Preliminary Change of Ownership Report (PCOR).

- The full trust agreement, available on request.

passages.title: Property taxes, reassessment, and ownership changes
passages.text:
When the Property Token is sold or otherwise transferred to a new owner, beneficial ownership of the trust changes. In that case, standard change-in-ownership notice applies and is reported to the county under the applicable state's rules, through the normal channels your office already uses.

In a 2022 informational analysis, California State Board of Equalization tax counsel stated that "a transfer of the digital Token is, in substance, a transfer of the underlying real property itself." That analysis is specific to California property tax and is not a legal ruling. Each jurisdiction applies its own rules, and nothing in this article predicts how any particular state or county will treat a given transfer.

passages.title: Property taxes, reassessment, and ownership changes
passages.text:
If your office is reviewing a specific parcel, email hello@fabrica.land with the parcel number and your question. You will get a direct answer, including the documentation described above where it helps.

Learn more: the Fabrica Trust (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/fabrica-trust) and property obligations (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/property-obligations) at docs.fabrica.land.

passages.title: Recording Fabrica deeds
passages.text: This article is for recorders and recording clerks who receive deeds involving a Fabrica Trust.

passages.title: Recording Fabrica deeds
passages.text:
Deeds are submitted through standard e-recording channels where your county supports them. Where a county requires paper or wet-ink submission, documents are prepared and submitted that way instead. The goal is to fit your county’s existing process, not to ask for a new one.

Supporting instruments are attached per your county’s requirements. Depending on the jurisdiction, a package may include a statement of authority, a certification of trust, and the applicable state tax or transfer forms.

passages.title: Recording Fabrica deeds
passages.text: The trust’s name contains an alphanumeric identifier. This is a valid trust name: the identifier encodes the specific trust’s entry in the trust registry, so each property’s trust is uniquely and verifiably named. It can look unusual on first review, but it is not a typo and not an error. Deeds name the trust as grantee or grantor; depending on the state, the deed may also name the trustee explicitly, or the trust may be recorded without a named trustee, following local practice. The beneficiary of the trust appoints the trustee and, by default, serves as their own trustee; Fabrica is not a party to the trust.

passages.title: Recording Fabrica deeds
passages.text: If a package is missing something your county requires, or an instrument needs correction, resubmission is prompt. Reject the document through your normal process, or email the team directly, and a corrected package follows.

passages.title: Recording Fabrica deeds
passages.text:
Recorders can reach the team at hello@fabrica.land. Include the document reference or parcel number and the reason for rejection or the requirement to satisfy, and you will get a direct response.

Learn more: the Fabrica Trust (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/fabrica-trust) and legal wrappers (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/legal-wrappers) at docs.fabrica.land.

passages.title: Tax bills, notices, and reaching the owner
passages.sectionTitle: Tax bills, notices, and reaching the owner
passages.text: This article is for treasurers, tax collectors, clerks, and code enforcement staff who need to get a bill or notice in front of the person responsible for a property held in a Fabrica Trust.

passages.title: Tax bills, notices, and reaching the owner
passages.sectionTitle: How mail to the trust reaches the owner
passages.text: Bills and notices addressed to the trust’s mailing address are scanned and delivered to the current owner of the property. The owner is the beneficiary of the trust and, by default, its trustee. Your office does not need to do anything different: mail sent to the address on record reaches the responsible party.

passages.title: Tax bills, notices, and reaching the owner
passages.text: The trust does not change who is responsible. The owner remains fully responsible for property taxes, assessments, and compliance with local requirements, exactly as any other property owner would be. Fabrica is not a party to the trust and is not the taxpayer.

passages.title: Tax bills, notices, and reaching the owner
passages.text: For anything with a deadline, such as a delinquency notice, a hearing date, or an enforcement action, email hello@fabrica.land with the parcel number and a copy of the notice. It is routed to the responsible owner promptly. This is the fastest path when timing matters.

passages.title: Tax bills, notices, and reaching the owner
passages.text:
Nothing about the trust changes a county’s normal collection or enforcement remedies. Liens, penalties, tax sales, and every other tool available to your office apply to a property held in a trust the same way they apply to any other property.

Learn more: property obligations (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/property-obligations) and the mail service (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/mail-forwarding) at docs.fabrica.land.

passages.title: Verifying ownership and trustee authority
passages.text: This article is for assessors, legal-entity units, and title clerks who need to confirm who owns a property held in a Fabrica Trust, or who currently has authority to act as its trustee.

passages.title: Verifying ownership and trustee authority
passages.text: Each property is held by its own state-law trust. The trust holds record title, and a digital Property Token represents ownership of the trust. The beneficiary of the trust is the current holder of that token. The beneficiary appoints the trustee and, by default, serves as their own trustee. Fabrica is not a party to the trust, never holds title, and cannot control the property.

passages.title: Verifying ownership and trustee authority
passages.sectionTitle: Why the trustee of record can appear out of date
passages.text: Under the trust agreement, trusteeship follows beneficial ownership. When the token transfers, the new owner becomes the beneficiary and, by default, the trustee. County records reflect this at the next recording event, so where your state names a trustee in recorded instruments, the trustee named in the most recent one can lag behind the current trustee between recordings. This lag has no effect on title: record title remains with the trust throughout, and the trust agreement itself determines who the current trustee is.

passages.title: Verifying ownership and trustee authority
passages.text:
If your office needs to confirm the current trustee or beneficiary, Fabrica facilitates:

- A notarized Certificate or Certification of Trust naming the current trustee and beneficiary explicitly.

- The full trust agreement. The agreement is open source and versioned, so your office can review the exact text governing a given trust.

Deeds prepared through the platform name the trust. In some states the trustee is also named explicitly on the deed; in others the trust is recorded without a named trustee, following local practice. If your county requires a correction instrument to align the record with the current trustee, one is prepared and recorded promptly.

passages.title: Verifying ownership and trustee authority
passages.text:
Email hello@fabrica.land with the parcel number and what your office needs. Requests from county offices are prioritized.

Learn more: the Fabrica Trust (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/fabrica-trust) and legal wrappers (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/legal-wrappers) at docs.fabrica.land.

passages.title: Moving money in and out of your Fabrica account
passages.sectionTitle: Moving money in and out of your Fabrica account
passages.text: Here's the short version: you usually don't need to put money into Fabrica before you start. When you buy a property, the checkout shows the payment options available for that purchase, which can include paying from your bank. Money only sits in your Fabrica account when you've received it there, for example after selling a property or taking a loan.

passages.title: Moving money in and out of your Fabrica account
passages.text:
When you click Buy now, the Pay by row in the Buy property window lets you choose how to pay:

- Account funds: stablecoins (digital dollars) already in your Fabrica account. No processing fee.

- Bank transfer, Card or Wire: pay from your bank, with no pre-funding and no crypto involved. Each option shows its fee and the date the property becomes yours. The options you see are the ones available for that purchase.

passages.title: Moving money in and out of your Fabrica account
passages.text:
When you sell a property or take a loan, the money arrives in your Fabrica account as stablecoins. From there you can send it to your bank: open your profile and click Cash out next to your balance. You choose the amount, the bank it goes to and a speed; every speed shows the fee and the date the money is expected. The first time, you verify your identity once and connect a bank in your name. "What happens when your property sells" (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/8546153-what-happens-when-your-property-sells) walks through it step by step.

If you use a crypto wallet, you can also send your stablecoins to any wallet you control.

passages.title: Moving money in and out of your Fabrica account
passages.text: Your profile has a Payment methods button next to Cash out. It lists the banks and cards you've connected, shows whether your identity is verified, and lets you add a bank or remove one. A card is saved when you pay with it.

passages.title: Moving money in and out of your Fabrica account
passages.text:
There's no direct bank-deposit option today; you can't wire money into your Fabrica balance from a bank. In practice you rarely need to, because purchases can be paid straight from your bank. If you do want a balance (for example, to make offers, which are made in USDC), you can:

- Send stablecoins from a crypto account or exchange you already use, or

- Log in with your own crypto wallet and simply use its balance directly.

passages.title: Moving money in and out of your Fabrica account
passages.text:
Your available balance appears next to Cash out on your profile, and when you're about to use it, for example as "$X available" under Account funds in the Buy property window. One thing to know: your account can have several linked addresses (see Account in the account menu), and funds live under the specific address you sent them to. If a deposit seems missing, switch to the address you actually sent it to.

If anything doesn't add up, message us through the chat bubble in the corner and we'll find it together.

passages.title: Do I need crypto to use Fabrica?
passages.sectionTitle: Do I need crypto to use Fabrica?
passages.text: No. You can add, sell, buy, and borrow against property on Fabrica without owning any cryptocurrency or downloading any crypto apps.

passages.title: Do I need crypto to use Fabrica?
passages.text:
- Sign in with email. Click Log in and use your email or a social account. Fabrica creates a secure account for you automatically, protected by passkeys on your device. Nothing to install, no seed phrase to guard.

- Pay from your bank. When you buy a property, the checkout's Pay by options can include a bank transfer, a card or a wire, each with its fee, limit and the date the property becomes yours shown on the option. The options you see are the ones available for that purchase.

- Cash out to your bank. When you sell or take a loan, the money arrives in your Fabrica account and you can send it to your bank with Cash out on your profile.

passages.title: Do I need crypto to use Fabrica?
passages.text: Money on Fabrica moves as stablecoins (digital dollars). The one Fabrica uses is called USDC. Prices are shown in US dollars, and Fabrica counts one USDC as one dollar. You will see the name in a few places, but you never need to buy it yourself or understand how it works. Think of it as the dollars in your Fabrica account.

passages.title: Do I need crypto to use Fabrica?
passages.text:
Only if you choose to:

- You already have a crypto wallet. You can connect it at login instead of using email. External wallets need to be on Ethereum Mainnet.

- You pay directly from a crypto wallet. Buying with Account funds from an external wallet uses its USDC balance, and you pay a small Ethereum network processing fee (called "gas") on the transaction. The same applies to a few wallet actions, like approving the setup fee from an external wallet or transferring a property between your own wallets.

- You use your own wallet for everyday actions. If you signed in with an external crypto wallet, some actions can need a small amount of ETH to cover processing fees. The app tells you when that is the case. Accounts that sign in with email never deal with this.

If you stick with email login and bank payments, you will never see any of that. Fabrica pays the network fees for minting your property and other platform steps.

passages.title: Do I need crypto to use Fabrica?
passages.text:
Already comfortable with wallets? Then Fabrica works the way you would hope. You can hold your property token directly in your own wallet and use it across the wider crypto ecosystem. A Fabrica property is a standard Ethereum token, so it benefits from the same interoperability as any other token you hold.

If you get stuck, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more: Buy land, pay with your bank account (https://blog.fabrica.land/buy-land-pay-with-bank-account)

passages.title: Glossary: the terms you'll see on Fabrica
passages.sectionTitle: Glossary: the terms you'll see on Fabrica
passages.text: You do not need special vocabulary to use Fabrica, but a few terms come up often. Here is what they mean in plain English.

passages.title: Glossary: the terms you'll see on Fabrica
passages.text: An assessor's parcel number, or APN, is the ID your county's tax assessor gives your property. Different counties may call it different names, but it is the number that pins down exactly which parcel is yours. You can find it on your property tax bill or on your deed. If you cannot find it, your county assessor's office can look it up, and many have online portals. Fabrica uses the APN to find your property when you add it.

passages.title: Glossary: the terms you'll see on Fabrica
passages.text: The formal, written description of your property's boundaries, found in your recorded deed. It might reference a subdivision and lot, or use measurements and landmarks ("metes and bounds"). Either kind is fine, as long as it accurately describes your property. Fabrica pulls this from county records when preparing your documents.

passages.title: Glossary: the terms you'll see on Fabrica
passages.text: The legal document that transfers ownership of real property. Deeds are recorded at the county, which is what makes ownership public and official. Fabrica drafts, notarizes, and records real deeds. Nothing about the process skips the county.

passages.title: Glossary: the terms you'll see on Fabrica
passages.text: A legal container for holding property. Trusts have been used for centuries for things like privacy and estate planning. On Fabrica, each property sits in its own trust: the trust holds record title at the county, and your Property Token represents ownership of the trust. Transfer the token, and you transfer the property.

passages.title: Glossary: the terms you'll see on Fabrica
passages.text: The two roles in a trust. The beneficiary is who the trust exists for, the true owner of what it holds. The trustee is who administers it. On Fabrica, you are the beneficiary, and by default you are also your own trustee. Fabrica never holds title to your property and cannot control it.

passages.title: Glossary: the terms you'll see on Fabrica
passages.text: The stablecoin Fabrica uses: a digital dollar. Prices on Fabrica are shown in US dollars, Fabrica counts one USDC as one dollar, and money moves as USDC behind the scenes. If you use bank payments and Cash out, you never need to handle it yourself.

passages.title: Glossary: the terms you'll see on Fabrica
passages.text:
In a traditional sale, an escrow company holds the money while paperwork crawls along. On Fabrica there is no escrow: the buyer becomes the owner and the seller gets paid in the same transaction, at the same moment. That is why sales are final once they complete.

If a term you ran into is not here, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more: Full glossary (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/glossary)

passages.title: Where is Fabrica available?
passages.text:
If your land is in the United States, chances are good you can add it to Fabrica today. Fabrica has operations across all 50 US states with varying degrees of functionality, and covers 3,000+ counties. Fabrica holds 20+ regulatory licenses.

To be plain about the limit: only property located in the United States can be added today. Land outside the US is not supported. If you live abroad and want to buy US land on Fabrica, that is a different question, and the answer is friendlier: see "Who can buy property on Fabrica?" (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/8542426-who-can-buy-property-on-fabrica) in the buying collection.

passages.title: Where is Fabrica available?
passages.text: The fastest way to find out is to try it. Go to fabrica.land/go (https://fabrica.land/go), pick your state and county, enter your APN (Parcel Number), and click Search. You can also click your parcel directly on the map. If your parcel comes up, you are good to go.

passages.title: Where is Fabrica available?
passages.sectionTitle: What if my area isn't supported yet?
passages.text: Some counties are not covered yet. If yours is one of them, you will see a message that says "Not available in your area yet." Our team is alerted automatically, and we will reach out the moment your property is eligible. We are expanding quickly, and new areas come online regularly.

passages.title: Where is Fabrica available?
passages.text:
In counties without online property records, our team does the title research by hand. Your property can still be added, but expect a longer timeline than in counties where records are online. We will keep you posted by email as your property moves through the process.

If you are not sure whether your property qualifies, message us through the chat bubble in the corner and include the county and parcel number if you have them.

Learn more: How adding a property works (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/on-ramp)

passages.title: Why does Fabrica ask for my personal information?
passages.sectionTitle: Why does Fabrica ask for my personal information?
passages.text: Fabrica requests the minimum personal information needed to make your transactions work. You share only what a given step actually requires, and most of the time that is just your contact details.

passages.title: Why does Fabrica ask for my personal information?
passages.text:
Identity verification (Know Your Customer, or KYC) happens only when you add a property to Fabrica. That is because a notary must verify your identity to confirm you actually own the property being added. The check happens during the online notary session, the same session where you sign your deed, and takes about 10 minutes.

While your property is being added, additional information may be requested depending on the county and state where the property is located. Real deeds and tax paperwork get recorded at the county in this process, so the names on them have to be right.

When you move money from your Fabrica account to your bank, the payment vendor may ask for additional information for their own KYC checks.

passages.title: Why does Fabrica ask for my personal information?
passages.sectionTitle: What about my Social Security number?
passages.text: Fabrica generally does not request or store your Social Security number. In the few counties that require it for recording, it is transmitted to the county and not stored on Fabrica’s systems.

passages.title: Why does Fabrica ask for my personal information?
passages.sectionTitle: What your contact details are used for
passages.text:
Your contact details, mostly your email, are used to:

- Deliver mail received for your property (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/16280934-what-happens-to-mail-sent-to-my-property-or-trust)

- Send you loan reminders

- Notify you about offers and the progress of your transactions

If you have questions about a specific request for information, message us through the chat bubble in the corner or email hello@fabrica.land.

Learn more: KYC and AML at Fabrica (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/kyc-and-aml)

passages.title: How do I edit my property's photos and description?
passages.sectionTitle: How do I edit my property's photos and description?
passages.text: Updating your property page takes a minute. Good photos and an accurate description help buyers understand what they are looking at. The one exception: editing is paused while the property is under a loan (more below).

passages.title: How do I edit my property's photos and description?
passages.sectionTitle: Add, caption, reorder or remove photos
passages.text:
- Open your property page while logged in (find it under My properties in the account menu).

- Click the camera button in the corner of the photo gallery, next to the photo-count button when there are several photos. Its label is Manage photos (on a property with no photos yet, Add photos), and it opens the "Property photos" window.

- Click "Choose photos" (or "Add photos or videos"), or drop files anywhere in the window. Photos (JPEG, PNG, HEIC, WebP) and videos up to 100 MB each are accepted. A file that can't be used is named in a "Heads up" notice with the reason, and the rest are still added.

- Type a caption under any photo in the "Add a caption" field (up to 255 characters).

- Drag photos to reorder them. The first photo is the cover buyers see first, and "Make cover" on any photo moves it to the front.

- To remove a photo, click the remove button on it. It stays in the grid marked "Will be removed when you save", and "Undo remove" brings it back.

- The footer sums up your changes. Nothing changes on your property until you click "Save changes".

passages.title: How do I edit my property's photos and description?
passages.text:
The window switches to "Saving your photos" and shows each step: uploading your files with a progress bar, preparing the update, and saving it to your property record. On a fully set-up property there is one extra step, "Confirm the update", where your account asks you to approve the change as it does for other property actions. Keep the window open while files upload. Once the update is confirmed you can close it, and we let you know when your photos are live. At the end you'll see "Great news: your photos are updated".

If something goes wrong, your edits stay in the window and nothing on your property changes. The message names the problem, for example "One of your files is too large", with a "Try again" button. If you declined the confirmation, "Confirm update" sends it again without uploading your files twice. If it keeps failing, message us through the chat bubble with a link to the property.

passages.title: How do I edit my property's photos and description?
passages.text:
