- On your property page, find the Description card and click Edit in its header. If your property has no description yet, the card shows "Tell buyers about this property" with a Write a description button instead.

- Make your changes in the text field. Plain text works, and links become clickable.

- Click Save changes to keep them, or Cancel to discard. Save changes stays disabled until you have actually changed something.

On a fully set-up property, saving updates your property's public record, so your account asks you to confirm the update first: the card reads "Confirm the update in your account. We'll save it right after." and then "Saving your changes." When it is done you'll see "Great news: your description is updated." If you decline the confirmation or something goes wrong, the card says "Your changes weren't saved." and keeps your text, with a Try again button.

Keep the description factual. Describe what the land is and what is on it. Avoid promises about value or future use. Long descriptions fold after a few lines, and visitors click Show more to read the rest.

passages.title: How do I edit my property's photos and description?
passages.sectionTitle: Can I edit while my property has a loan or a listing?
passages.text: You can edit while your property is listed for sale. While the property is under a loan, though, editing photos and the description is not available, along with transferring and removing the property. Listing for sale is the action that remains available under a loan. Pay off the loan and editing is restored.

passages.title: How do I edit my property's photos and description?
passages.text:
During onboarding, Fabrica may generate a starting description and illustrative images for your property. You are free to replace them with your own photos and words, and real photos are usually more convincing to buyers.

If you get stuck, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

passages.title: What to tell your attorney, title company, or lender about your Fabrica trust
passages.sectionTitle: What to tell your attorney, title company, or lender about your Fabrica trust
passages.text: Sooner or later a professional will ask how your Fabrica property is held: an attorney drafting your will, a title company handling a sale, a lender reviewing your assets. This page gives you the plain answer to hand them. Feel free to share it, along with the trust agreement itself.

passages.title: What to tell your attorney, title company, or lender about your Fabrica trust
passages.text: Each property sits in its own trust, and that trust holds record title at the county. You own your property through your own trust. You are the beneficiary, and by default you are also your own trustee. Fabrica never holds title to your property and cannot control it. The digital Property Token represents ownership of the trust: transfer the token, transfer the property.

passages.title: What to tell your attorney, title company, or lender about your Fabrica trust
passages.text:
- The trust agreement is open source and versioned. Anyone can read the exact document that governs your property, and your property's own signed copy is on its property page: open the Legals card, then the Documents menu.

- Deeds are recorded normally at the county recorder's office. The trust appears in the public record like any other titled owner.

- The trust is governed by California law, while conveyancing follows the law of the state where the property sits.

- California State Board of Equalization tax counsel stated in a 2022 informational analysis that "a transfer of the digital Token is, in substance, a transfer of the underlying real property itself." That is a California property-tax view, not a legal ruling or a 50-state rule, but it is a useful reference point for how the structure is read.

passages.title: What to tell your attorney, title company, or lender about your Fabrica trust
passages.sectionTitle: For your title company or lender
passages.text: A conventional closing out of the trust is always possible. The off-ramp process records a fresh deed into the owner's name at the county, after which the property is held the ordinary way and the trust dissolves. So nothing about the trust prevents a traditional sale, refinance, or title work: the property can always be moved back to a plain recorded deed first.

passages.title: What to tell your attorney, title company, or lender about your Fabrica trust
passages.text: For tax purposes, you are treated as the property's owner. Questions about how to report the trust on your returns, or whether it needs its own tax ID, are for your tax professional. We can't advise on that, and this article isn't tax advice.

passages.title: What to tell your attorney, title company, or lender about your Fabrica trust
passages.text:
The fastest way to get a professional comfortable is to let them read the actual paperwork. Share this article, the trust agreement from your property page, and the deep dives below. If they still have questions, ask us in the chat and we will help you find the answer.

If your professional is a title agent, escrow officer, or underwriter, point them to our dedicated page: "For title professionals: insuring and closing a property held in a Fabrica trust" in the officials section of this help center. It covers the structure in title terms, the document checklist, and signing requirements.

Learn more:

- The Fabrica trust (developer docs) (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/fabrica-trust)

- Legal wrappers (developer docs) (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/legal-wrappers)

passages.title: What happens to mail sent to my property or trust?
passages.sectionTitle: What happens to mail sent to my property or trust?
passages.text: Counties and other parties sometimes send mail addressed to your property or to the trust that holds it: tax bills, assessment notices, change-of-ownership paperwork, HOA letters.

passages.title: What happens to mail sent to my property or trust?
passages.sectionTitle: We scan it and email it to you
passages.text:
When mail arrives for your property or trust, Fabrica scans it and emails a copy to the email address on your account. You do not need to set anything up; this happens automatically as part of the service.

The scan is what we deliver. If you need the physical original of a letter, ask us in the chat and we will look into forwarding it to you where possible.

passages.title: What happens to mail sent to my property or trust?
passages.text:
Treat these emails like the paper mail they contain. Tax bills and county notices often have deadlines, and missing them can lead to penalties, liens, or worse. When a scanned letter arrives:

- Open it and read what it asks for.

- If it is a tax bill, pay the county directly (see “Your property taxes” (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/8809464-who-pays-property-taxes) in this collection).

- If you are not sure what a letter means or what to do, ask us.

passages.title: What happens to mail sent to my property or trust?
passages.text: If you take your property off Fabrica, update your mailing address directly with the county so future tax bills and notices reach you, instead of going to the old property address.

passages.title: What happens to mail sent to my property or trust?
passages.text:
Email hello@fabrica.land with the property link and the scanned document, or message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more: Mail forwarding (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/mail-forwarding)

passages.title: What are property checks?
passages.text:
Property checks show you whether anything has come up on a property before you buy it, lend against it or borrow on it. Every Fabrica property page has a Property checks card listing each check, what it found and where the information comes from.

Property checks were formerly called the Provenance Score.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: What are property checks?
passages.sectionTitle: What you see on the page
passages.text:
- Next to the property name, a chip sums up the result, for example "1 to review" or "Paused". When the key checks and the claims all pass, you see a shield icon instead. Either one jumps to the card.

- The Property checks card shows a count in its header, such as "11 of 12 pass", then opens with a short verdict, such as "All 12 checks pass" or "1 item to review", and one line per group. See all 12 checks shows each check, its status and its source.

- If the checks pause sales and loans, a banner at the top of the page says "Sales and loans are paused on this property", gives the reason and links to See property checks.

Each check is titled by what it found. A check that passes reads, for example, "Property taxes paid"; the same check that does not pass reads "Unpaid property taxes", and one with no result yet reads "Property taxes" with the tag "Not checked yet".
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: What are property checks?
passages.text:
Key checks. The most serious checks. A failure here can pause sales and loans.

- Link to the property is normal: no known recovery, theft claim, tax sale or foreclosure event has been reported on the property.

- Deed checked against the county: a deed linking the title to the property's Fabrica record is on file, notarized and recorded. Source: the county recorder.

- No theft reports: the property is not on Fabrica's list of flagged properties, and OpenSea, a large marketplace for digital assets, has not marked it as suspicious.

- Owner not on a fraud list: the owner's account is not on public lists of accounts tied to scams.

Claims on the property. These affect what the property is worth and whether it can back a loan.

- Property taxes paid: the county tax collector shows no unpaid property taxes.

- No mortgage found: a lien records search found no open loan secured by the property. It does not cover tax, court or contractor liens.

- Fabrica fees in good standing: Fabrica fees on the property are paid, or approved for collection when the property is first sold, borrowed against, or used in another app. A pass does not mean a deferred fee, such as the setup fee, has already been collected.

Good to know. About the people and paperwork, rarely a reason to walk away: whether the current and past owners verified their identity, whether the owner confirmed an email or phone number, whether the property moved between accounts in the last 7 days, and whether its records (location, trust name, legal description, deed, trust agreement) are complete.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: What are property checks?
passages.text: "Not checked yet" means there is no result yet. It is not a failure.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: What are property checks?
passages.sectionTitle: A mortgage is reported, not judged
passages.text: Most homes have a mortgage, and the owner agreed to it. When the lien search finds one, the row reads Mortgage on record with a blue "On record" tag instead of a failure: "An open mortgage is recorded against this property, as with most homes. It's paid off before the property is sold or borrowed against on Fabrica." It is left out of the "N of N pass" count, which then adds "1 on record", and it does not change the verdict. Claims put on the property without the owner's say, such as unpaid taxes, still count as items to review.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: What are property checks?
passages.sectionTitle: What they mean for buying and borrowing
passages.text:
- Paused sales and loans. If the link to the property is not normal, the deed has not been confirmed, or the property's checks fall below the minimum required, the property can't be bought, sold or borrowed against until that changes.

- Borrowing. The Instant Liquidity card can explain problems with three checks: the deed, property taxes and Fabrica fees. Passing these checks does not by itself guarantee that borrowing is available. Taxes that are unpaid, or not yet confirmed with the county, block borrowing.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: What are property checks?
passages.text:
At the top of the card, owners see a short list headed "N things you can do" (or "Nothing to do"), because buyers and lenders see these checks on your property:

- Keep property taxes current. The check passes once the county shows them as paid, which can take a while.

- Use Confirm email so notices about your property reach you.

- If your identity is not verified, Get help opens the chat.

- If the Fabrica fees check is not passing, use Authorize Fee in the Owner Toolbox.

- A recent transfer clears on its own 7 days later.

If you believe a check is wrong, message us with your property link.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: What are property checks?
passages.text:
Property checks compare the property's Fabrica record with county records, lien data and other sources. They are a starting point for your own research, not a title search or title insurance.

For lenders and developers, the card also shows a 5-digit code: the numeric encoding of Property checks. It groups the results differently from the checklist, so it is not a percentage or a grade.

If you get stuck, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more: How to read the code (developer docs) (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/confidence-scoring-system) · Validators (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/validators)
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: How do I transfer a property between my own wallets?
passages.sectionTitle: How do I transfer a property between my own wallets?
passages.text:
If you hold your property in one account address and want to move it to another address you also own, use Transfer Property. This moves the token between your own wallets. It does not change who owns the property: both addresses are yours, so you remain the owner throughout.

A "wallet" here is just an account address on Ethereum. If you signed up with your email, Fabrica created one for you automatically. You might also have an external wallet app you prefer to hold things in.

passages.title: How do I transfer a property between my own wallets?
passages.text:
- The transfer only works between wallets that are linked to your Fabrica account and verified as yours. You cannot use it to send the property to someone else.

- To link another wallet: as the dialog says, "open the account menu at the top right of your screen, choose Account, and link another account there."

- If you signed in with your email, there is nothing to pay: Fabrica covers the processing fee. If you are transferring from an external crypto wallet, you will need a small amount of ETH to cover processing fees, and the dialog tells you so. ETH is Ethereum's own currency, used to pay the network's small processing charge.

- If the property is under a loan, transfers are disabled. The app will tell you: "Please pay off the loan to enable property transfer."

passages.title: How do I transfer a property between my own wallets?
passages.text:
- Open your property page while logged in.

- In the Owner Toolbox, click Transfer Property. The dialog explains what happens: "Moves the token, and the property with it, to another account you own. No paperwork: the trust follows the token."

- Pick the linked account you want to move the property to.

- Confirm the transfer in your account and wait for it to complete. If it is still confirming, you can leave the page; the property moves once it completes. If the network did not pick up the transfer, nothing moved, and you can send it again.

passages.title: How do I transfer a property between my own wallets?
passages.text:
- Selling or gifting to another person: that is a sale or a private transfer, covered in the selling articles.

- Recovering from a lost wallet: if you lost access to an address, see "I lost access to my account. Is my property gone?" (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/16280942-i-lost-access-to-my-account-is-my-property-gone) instead.

If you get stuck, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

passages.title: What is a trust agreement upgrade?
passages.sectionTitle: What is a trust agreement upgrade?
passages.text: Your property is held by your own trust, and the trust agreement is the legal document that defines how it works. Fabrica improves this document over time, and as an owner you can adopt the newest version for your property.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: What is a trust agreement upgrade?
passages.text: On your property page, open the Records card. The trust agreement row names your trust and the version it runs on. When a newer version exists, an Upgrade agreement link appears under the rows; it is shown only to the property's holder. Click it to open the Upgrade Trust Agreement flow, which moves your trust to the latest version of the agreement.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: What is a trust agreement upgrade?
passages.text:
Each new version of the trust agreement refines the legal machinery around your ownership: clearer language, better protections, and rules for situations earlier versions did not spell out. For example, recent versions added explicit handling for what happens to the trust if a property is lost to a county tax sale.

What does not change:

- You stay the beneficiary of your trust, and by default your own trustee.

- Fabrica still never holds title to your property and cannot control it.

- Your rights as owner (possession, control, sale, borrowing) are unchanged.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: What is a trust agreement upgrade?
passages.text:
No. Upgrading is optional, and your property keeps working on the version it has. We recommend it, though: the newest agreement is the most complete and best-protected version, and it is the one new properties get.

The trust agreement is open source, so you can read every version yourself and see exactly what changed.

If you have questions before upgrading, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more: The Fabrica trust (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/fabrica-trust) · OTA for your land (https://blog.fabrica.land/ota-for-your-land)
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Where are my property documents?
passages.text: Everything important about your property lives in two places: on your property page and in your email. Here is where to look for each document.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Where are my property documents?
passages.text:
Open your property and find the Records card. It holds one row for each part of your property's legal record:

- Legal description, the formal text that defines exactly which land is included. Open the row to read it in full, or copy it.

- Deed into the trust, the recorded deed that put the property into your trust. The row opens the document itself.

- Your trust agreement, named after your trust. The row opens the agreement, and a button next to it downloads a copy.

- Any other files attached to your property.

- Your token's ID, with a link to view it on Etherscan, a public record of Ethereum activity.

Below the rows, the Property, Trust and Token chips show how the three fit together: the deed puts the property into the trust, and ownership of the property goes with the token, through the trust.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Where are my property documents?
passages.text: When recording at the county completes, we email you the recorded deed and your trust agreement. Search your inbox for the property name if you cannot find them.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Where are my property documents?
passages.text: Your deed is a public record. The county recorder keeps it permanently, so you can always request a copy directly from the county where the property sits. This is true whether or not Fabrica exists. Your ownership record does not depend on us.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Where are my property documents?
passages.sectionTitle: Documents from a property you sold or removed
passages.text:
There is no self-serve archive for past properties today. If you need a document from a property you sold or removed, message us in the chat bubble in the corner and we will retrieve it for you.

If you get stuck, message us in the chat bubble in the corner. Learn more about the trust in the Fabrica trust docs (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/fabrica-trust).
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: When would I remove my property from Fabrica?
passages.sectionTitle: When would I remove my property from Fabrica?
passages.text: Removing a property (the off-ramp) puts the deed back in your name, or in the name of anyone you choose, and takes the property off Fabrica. It is always your call. Here are the most common reasons people do it.

passages.title: When would I remove my property from Fabrica?
passages.text:
- A traditional sale. You want to sell through a real-estate agent and a title company, and they want title held in your name the usual way.

- Traditional financing. A bank or mortgage lender is refinancing or lending against the property and requires the deed in your name.

- Personal preference. You simply want to hold the property the way you did before. That is a perfectly good reason.

passages.title: When would I remove my property from Fabrica?
passages.text: While a property is off Fabrica, you lose the online rails: listing it for sale on the marketplace, receiving offers, borrowing against it through the lending pool, and transferring it in minutes. Selling or borrowing goes back to the traditional pace and paperwork.

passages.title: When would I remove my property from Fabrica?
passages.text: Everything that matters. You owned the property through your own trust while it was on Fabrica, and after removal you own it directly, with a fresh deed recorded at the county. Nothing about your ownership is reduced by removing it.

passages.title: When would I remove my property from Fabrica?
passages.text: Yes. You can add the property again any time by starting a new setup at fabrica.land/go (https://fabrica.land/go).

passages.title: When would I remove my property from Fabrica?
passages.text:
There is no Fabrica fee to remove a property. If you never sold it, borrowed against it, or used it in another app while it was on Fabrica, the setup fee you authorized is waived. Counties charge their own recording costs, and Fabrica guides you through them.

If you are weighing it and want to talk it through, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more: Off-ramp (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/off-ramp)

passages.title: Disputes and refunds: how do they work?
passages.text:
Purchases on Fabrica settle in one step: the buyer becomes the owner and the seller is paid in the same transaction. There is no escrow holding funds that can be unwound later, which is why the checkout asks you to confirm that sales are final before you buy. Once a sale completes, it cannot be reversed by Fabrica or anyone else.

That makes diligence before you buy the real protection. Every property page gives you the tools: the Records card with the full legal description, the deed into the trust and the trust agreement, the Property checks card, and any disclosure documents the checkout asks you to acknowledge. Read them. If a listing shows a duplicate-claim warning banner, take it seriously and verify before buying.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Disputes and refunds: how do they work?
passages.text: Bank payments are different from completed sales. If a card or bank payment fails or is returned, the purchase simply does not complete, and we email you about it. You do not lose money on a payment that never cleared. If something looks stuck, contact us.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Disputes and refunds: how do they work?
passages.text:
Talk to us first. Message us through the chat bubble at fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land) or email hello@fabrica.land, and include the property link plus what happened. Many issues turn out to be questions we can resolve directly.

For genuine disputes about a property or a transaction, the trust agreement sets out a formal dispute-resolution process, which the docs explain in detail. Fabrica is not a law firm and cannot give legal advice, so for a serious disagreement, involve your own attorney. We will cooperate with the facts, including onchain records.

Learn more: Dispute resolution (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/dispute-resolution)
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: What happens to my property when I die?
passages.sectionTitle: What happens to my property when I die?
passages.text: Your property on Fabrica is part of your estate, just like any other real estate you own. It passes to your heirs. Nothing about the token changes that.

passages.title: What happens to my property when I die?
passages.text:
You own the property through your own trust, and your interest in that trust is what your heirs inherit. The trust agreement provides for this directly: when an estate goes through probate (the court process that settles a person’s affairs), the probate documents are what move ownership to the heirs. That means your family does not need your passwords, your email, or your wallet keys to inherit the land. Ownership can be transferred based on the estate’s legal documents.

If the heirs want to keep using Fabrica, the property continues as normal under their ownership. If they would rather hold the deed directly, they can remove the property, which records a fresh deed in their name at the county.

passages.title: What happens to my property when I die?
passages.text: Whoever handles the estate should contact us early: the chat bubble at fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land) or hello@fabrica.land. Have the property link and the estate paperwork ready. We will confirm what the county and the trust require and guide the transfer from there.

passages.title: What happens to my property when I die?
passages.text:
A short conversation with an estate-planning attorney now saves your family real effort later. Tell them the property is held in a trust and share the trust agreement with them; it is open source, so they can read every word. Fabrica cannot give legal or tax advice, so lean on a professional for the planning itself.

Learn more: Death and estate planning (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/death-and-estate-planning)

passages.title: I lost access to my account. Is my property gone?
passages.sectionTitle: I lost access to my account. Is my property gone?
passages.text: No. Lost logins, and even lost wallet keys, never mean lost land. The answer depends on how you signed in, so find your situation below.

passages.title: I lost access to my account. Is my property gone?
passages.sectionTitle: If you log in with your email
passages.text:
Most owners sign in with an email address or a social login. There is no password to lose: Fabrica emails you a verification link when you log in from a new device, and your account is secured with a passkey behind the scenes. As long as you can receive email at your address, you can get back in.

If you have lost access to the email address itself, contact us through the chat bubble at fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land) or write to hello@fabrica.land and we will help you sort it out.

passages.title: I lost access to my account. Is my property gone?
passages.sectionTitle: If you used your own crypto wallet and lost the keys
passages.text:
This is the scenario the trust was built for. Losing the keys to a wallet that holds your Property Token does not lose the property, because your ownership is anchored in a trust whose deed is recorded at the county, not in the wallet.

The trust agreement includes a built-in recovery path called Token Recovery:

- A Notice of Lost Token Control is recorded with the county where the property sits.

- A 90-day Quiet Period follows. This public window protects everyone against false claims.

- If no valid challenge appears, a Deed of Distribution puts title directly in your name.

It is self-service and needs no court order. You end up owning the property directly, and you can add it back to Fabrica afterward if you want.

passages.title: I lost access to my account. Is my property gone?
passages.text:
Contact us as soon as you notice a problem, through the chat bubble or hello@fabrica.land. Have your property link ready if you can. We will confirm which situation you are in and walk you through the next step.

Learn more: Token Recovery (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/token-recovery) · Lost keys, no lost land (https://blog.fabrica.land/lost-keys-no-lost-land)

passages.title: Selling a property that has a loan on it
passages.sectionTitle: Selling a property that has a loan on it
passages.text: Yes, you can list your property for sale while it has an active loan. The sale settles your loan automatically, and you keep whatever is left.

passages.title: Selling a property that has a loan on it
passages.text:
- Click Put for sale on your property page, like any other listing.

- The List property for sale window shows your loan payoff alongside the price. Your price must at least cover the payoff. If it doesn't, you'll see: "Heads up: this price wouldn't cover your loan payoff. Enter at least $X." (or "Heads up: based on estimated fees, this price wouldn't cover your loan payoff…" when the fee is still an estimate).

- During listing you'll approve an extra step, Allow the loan payoff. As the app puts it: "This lets the sale pay off your loan automatically at closing."

- When the property sells, the proceeds first pay off the loan in full. You receive the rest, minus Fabrica's 1% marketplace fee, which is paid from the seller's proceeds.

So if you owe $8,000 on the loan and sell for $50,000, the loan is paid off at closing and the remainder comes to you. No separate payoff errand, no risk of forgetting.

Once listed, the Marketplace card on your property page reminds you: "The sale pays off your loan at closing. Payoff today: $X."

How the payoff behaves depends on your loan. Some loans accrue interest over time, so the payoff keeps growing until the sale actually completes. For those, the listing screen shows two figures: the net amount you would receive today, and the amount if the property sells by your loan's due date. Other loans are fixed-term: you owe a set repayment amount no matter when it is paid, so the payoff does not grow and you will see a single net figure.

passages.title: Selling a property that has a loan on it
passages.sectionTitle: Keep your price above the payoff
passages.text: If your loan accrues interest, set your price with enough room above the payoff, because the payoff grows over time. If interest ever catches up to your price, the app tells you the date it will happen with a note like: "Heads up: as loan interest grows, this price will stop covering your payoff around [date]." After that date your listing stays visible, but no one can buy it until you either re-list at a higher price or pay off the loan. Pricing comfortably above the payoff avoids this entirely. Fixed-term loans do not grow this way, so this warning does not apply to them. Either way, if you are unsure which kind you have, the Your loan card on your property page shows your exact figures.

passages.title: Selling a property that has a loan on it
passages.text:
- You can list the property for sale. If it sells, the sale pays off your loan at closing and you receive the rest.

- You can't accept an offer until the loan is paid off. Buyers can still send offers, and your offers list says: "Pay off your loan to accept an offer."

- You can't edit the property's photos or description, transfer the property between wallets, or remove it from Fabrica until the loan is paid off. While the loan is active, the property is held as collateral, so these actions are paused.

- Paying off the loan early with Pay off loan is always an option if you'd rather sell unencumbered, and it restores all of the above.

passages.title: Selling a property that has a loan on it
passages.text:
Buyers see one line in the Marketplace card: "This property backs a loan from a DeFi lending pool. The sale pays that loan off at closing, so you don't take it over." They never see your payoff figures. If the listing can't be bought right now, they see a "Buying paused" chip with the reason, for example that the seller must pay off the loan before it can be bought, or that the asking price doesn't cover the payoff. On your side, the card says the same in your words, such as "Heads up: your asking price is below the loan payoff, so buyers can't buy it. Raise your price to sell it." Setting a price that comfortably covers the payoff keeps your sale as smooth as possible.

If you get stuck, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more: Lending pool (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/lending-pool) in our docs.

passages.title: Where does my listing appear?
passages.text: When you list your property for sale, you get more than one storefront.

passages.title: Where does my listing appear?
passages.text: Your listing appears on fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land), on the map and in the property cards that buyers browse.

passages.title: Where does my listing appear?
passages.text:
Listings may also be distributed to partner land marketplaces, such as LandSearch. When a buyer inquires through one of those channels, you get an email and can reply directly. There is no extra charge for this distribution; it is part of listing on Fabrica.

We expand distribution over time, so where listings appear can change. If you have a question about your own listing, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

Learn more: Selling (developer docs) (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/selling)

passages.title: I can't find my parcel. What now?
passages.sectionTitle: I can't find my parcel. What now?
passages.text: Adding a property starts at fabrica.land/go (https://fabrica.land/go): choose your State, choose your County, type your "APN (Parcel Number)", and click "Search". If that is not working, nothing is wrong with your land; a failed search is almost always a numbering mix-up or a coverage gap. Here is how to get unstuck.

passages.title: I can't find my parcel. What now?
passages.text:
The APN (Assessor's Parcel Number) is the ID your county assessor uses for your land. There is no address search on Fabrica, so the APN is the key. You can find it:

- On your property tax bill.

- On your deed.

- On your county assessor's website, usually searchable by owner name or address.

Type it exactly as the county lists it. If you see "No parcel found for that APN in this county. Please check the number and try again.", double-check the number and make sure you selected the right county. Parcel numbers are only unique within a county.

passages.title: I can't find my parcel. What now?
passages.text:
You can skip the APN entirely: zoom into the map on the same page and click your parcel directly. This also helps if you see "Found the parcel but could not determine its location. Try clicking it on the map instead."

If you see "Could not look up that parcel. Please check the APN and try again.", it is usually a temporary lookup problem. Wait a moment and retry, or use the map.

passages.title: I can't find my parcel. What now?
passages.text: If this message appears, your county is not set up on Fabrica yet. Our team is alerted automatically, and we will reach out the moment your property is eligible.

passages.title: I can't find my parcel. What now?
passages.sectionTitle: The shape on the map looks wrong
passages.text: The parcel outlines on the map are indicative, drawn from county map data. They are good enough to find and click your parcel, but they are not the legal boundary. What governs is the recorded legal description at the county. If your parcel was recently split, combined, or had a boundary adjustment, the map can take time to catch up, because county map data updates on its own schedule. If your parcel recently changed and the map does not reflect it, message us in the chat and we will help.

passages.title: I can't find my parcel. What now?
passages.text:
Some rural counties do not have online property records. We can still work with them, but our team does the title research by hand, so those properties take longer to process.

If you get stuck, message us in the chat bubble in the corner. Learn more in the property setup docs (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/on-ramp).

passages.title: I hit an error while adding my property. What now?
passages.sectionTitle: I hit an error while adding my property. What now?
passages.text: First, the important part: nothing is lost. Your progress saves as you go and continues on our side, so an error on the screen does not undo the steps you have completed. Most of these fix themselves with a retry or a short wait.

passages.title: I hit an error while adding my property. What now?
passages.sectionTitle: "Could not look up that parcel. Please check the APN and try again."
passages.text: Double-check the APN against your tax bill or the county assessor's record, then retry. If the number is right and the lookup still fails, try clicking your parcel directly on the map instead of typing the APN.

passages.title: I hit an error while adding my property. What now?
passages.sectionTitle: An error while we gather property information
passages.text: Sometimes an error appears while we are researching your property, for example while verifying its ownership history. When that happens, our team sees the same error you do, and we usually fix it on the data side. Try again later, or message us in the chat bubble if you want us to look right away.

passages.title: I hit an error while adding my property. What now?
passages.text: This is not an error with your property. It means we have not configured your area yet. We are expanding quickly, and we will reach out the moment your property is eligible.

passages.title: I hit an error while adding my property. What now?
passages.text: Your property page always shows live status. The status bar near the top of the page tells you if a step needs you or if something needs attention, and clicking "See details" opens the full checklist of steps. Steps tagged "at closing" are waiting on purpose, not stuck.

passages.title: I hit an error while adding my property. What now?
passages.sectionTitle: The "Upgrade your property" button does nothing
passages.text:
Sign out, sign back in, and try again. If the button still does not respond, message us in the chat bubble in the corner and we will finish the step with you.

If you get stuck at any point, message us in the chat bubble in the corner. Learn more in the property setup docs (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/on-ramp).

passages.title: How do I contact support?
passages.text: Two ways, both reaching real people on the Fabrica team.

passages.title: How do I contact support?
passages.text: Click the chat bubble in the corner of any page on fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land). This is the quickest way to get help, and it keeps the conversation attached to your account so we can see what you see.

passages.title: How do I contact support?
passages.text: Write to hello@fabrica.land. Email is best for anything with attachments, like mail you received about your property or documents you want us to look at.

passages.title: How do I contact support?
passages.text:
You will get a faster, better answer if your first message includes:

- A link to the property page (or the APN and county).

- What you were trying to do, and what happened instead.

- The exact text of any error message, or a screenshot.

passages.title: How do I contact support?
passages.text: We read every message and a real person replies. It is not always instant, especially outside US business hours, but you will hear back. If your question involves county paperwork or title research, the full answer can take longer, and we will tell you when that is the case rather than leave you guessing.

passages.title: Why isn't my listing showing up on the marketplace?
passages.sectionTitle: Why isn't my listing showing up on the marketplace?
passages.text: You listed your property for sale, but it is not appearing on the marketplace. Your listing is not lost, and nothing is wrong with your ownership. There are three common reasons, and each has a fix.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Why isn't my listing showing up on the marketplace?
passages.sectionTitle: 1. The fee authorization needs a refresh
passages.text:
When you added your property, you authorized Fabrica's one-time setup fee (it is only collected when you first sell the property, borrow against it, or use it in another app). Technically this is a spending allowance, and it can lapse. If it has, your property will not be visible on the marketplace and you will not be able to take out loans against it until you re-approve.

To fix it: open your property page and look for "Authorize Fee" in the Owner Toolbox. If we emailed you about it, the link in that email takes you straight there. Approving takes under a minute and nothing is charged.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Why isn't my listing showing up on the marketplace?
passages.sectionTitle: 2. The property is not fully set up yet
passages.text: If you listed a property that is still finishing its setup (the page says "Unclaimed" or the setup is still in progress), your listing is live on the marketplace and can receive offers. What it cannot do yet is close: accepting an offer or completing a sale requires the setup to be finished, so buyers will not see a "Buy now" button until then. Finish the setup steps, then use the "Confirm your listing to let buyers buy right away." link on your property page if it appears, and the listing becomes fully active.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: Why isn't my listing showing up on the marketplace?
passages.text:
Listed properties must clear an internal quality check before they appear on the marketplace. The check looks at things like whether the title checks out and whether the property is in good standing. Keeping your property taxes current and your fee authorization active is the best way to stay above the bar.

One more thing to check: listings run for 180 days. If yours is older than that, it has expired, and you can simply list again with "Put for sale".

If none of this explains it, message us in the chat bubble in the corner with a link to your property.
passages.updatedAt: updated a week ago at build

passages.title: My offer or purchase is still pending. Is something wrong?
passages.sectionTitle: My offer or purchase is still pending. Is something wrong?
passages.text: Usually nothing is wrong. Here is what the waiting states mean and when to expect news.

passages.title: My offer or purchase is still pending. Is something wrong?
passages.sectionTitle: If you bought with a bank payment
passages.text: Bank transfers are not instant. After "Your bank payment is on its way", the payment clears with your bank, usually by the expected date the checkout showed you. While it clears, the property page shows Sale pending and the day you'll become the owner. You will get a confirmation email when the purchase completes, and we will email you sooner if anything needs your attention. If you are waiting on sale proceeds as a seller, the same clearing time applies, and the page shows the date you can expect to get paid. A wire shows "Waiting for your wire" until it lands.

passages.title: My offer or purchase is still pending. Is something wrong?
passages.sectionTitle: If you bought with account funds or a card
passages.text: These purchases settle in one step: the confirmation screen tells you the property is yours. With account funds the confirmation email arrives right away; with a card it arrives once the payment is fully settled, which can take a little longer. If the purchase dialog seems frozen mid-step, refresh the page and check your portfolio on your profile before retrying: if the property is there, the purchase went through.

passages.title: My offer or purchase is still pending. Is something wrong?
passages.text:
An offer is not a purchase yet. The seller has to accept it.

- Your offer stays open for the period you chose with "Offer Valid For" (1 to 60 days). If it expires without being accepted, nothing happens and no money moves.

- You can withdraw an open offer any time: your offer shows as "Your offer" in the property's offers list with a "Withdraw" button.

- If you offered on a property that is still completing its setup (an "Unclaimed" page), the owner can accept an offer only once the property is fully set up. Your offer waits in the meantime.

You will get an email if your offer is accepted, and the funds only move at that point.

If something has been pending longer than the timelines above, message us in the chat bubble in the corner with a link to the property. Learn more in the buying docs (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/buying).

passages.title: My payment was declined or seems stuck
passages.sectionTitle: My payment was declined or seems stuck
passages.text: In most cases nothing is wrong with your account: bank transfers are simply slower than they feel, and a declined card is usually your own bank being cautious. Payments from a bank, card or wire are handled by Coinflow, our payment provider, inside the Buy property window. Here is what to do when a payment does not go through, or seems to be taking forever.

passages.title: My payment was declined or seems stuck
passages.text:
- Card payments can be declined by your bank, especially for large or unusual purchases. The app says "Heads up: your card was declined. Try another card or pay by bank transfer." Check for a text or app alert from your bank asking you to approve the charge, then try again. If your bank's confirmation step didn't complete, you'll see "Heads up: your bank didn't confirm the payment. Try again or use another card."

- Each option has a limit. If the price is above an option's limit, the option tells you ("Up to $N per purchase. This price is above the limit.") and the app points you to Wire when that fits.

- The bank account must be in your name. If the name on a bank account doesn't match your verified identity, it can't be used for bank transfers. Joint and business accounts usually need the account holder's own name. Try another account, or pay by wire.

- For larger purchases, use a wire. Pick Wire under Pay by, and the app gives you the details to send from your bank, with a Send by date. Include the reference exactly: wires without it are returned, and if the details expire you start a new payment to get fresh ones.

- Processing fees, if any, are the payment processor's and are shown on the option before you pay.

If a bank transfer fails or is returned after the fact, we email you about it, and the property stays listed so you can try again from another account.

passages.title: My payment was declined or seems stuck
passages.text:
A bank transfer is not instant. After you see "Your bank payment is on its way", the payment clears with your bank, usually by the expected date shown ("It can take a few business days to clear."). During that time the property page shows Sale pending and the day you'll become the owner. That is normal, not an error. We will email you if anything needs your attention, and you will get a confirmation email when the purchase completes. If the date passes, the page says so ("Heads up: the payment is taking longer than expected.") and asks you to contact us.

A wire shows "Waiting for your wire" on the property page until it lands. If you already sent it, it shows up once it arrives; if not, send it by the date shown or the request expires.

If you are the seller in a bank-funded sale, the app shows when to expect your money ("You'll get paid by" a date), and payment arrives once the transfer clears.

passages.title: My payment was declined or seems stuck
passages.sectionTitle: If a cash out fails or stalls
passages.text:
The same reassurance applies in the other direction. If a cash out to your bank can't be completed, nothing is lost: the money comes back to your Fabrica account, and the app tells you so. If the app couldn't get your approval, it says "Nothing left your account." Try the cash out again, and if it keeps failing, message us in the chat and we will look at it with you.

If something has been stuck longer than the app told you to expect, message us in the chat bubble in the corner with a link to the property. Learn more about payment options on the blog (https://blog.fabrica.land/buy-land-pay-with-bank-account).

passages.title: A transaction failed or seems stuck. What do I do?
passages.sectionTitle: A transaction failed or seems stuck. What do I do?
passages.text: First, the reassuring part: a failed transaction does not move your money or your property. When something goes wrong, the app stops before anything happens and shows a message inviting you to try again. Your funds stay put. In almost every case, the fix is simply to retry.

passages.title: A transaction failed or seems stuck. What do I do?
passages.sectionTitle: Signing fails while listing for sale
passages.text: Retry from "Put for sale" on your property page. If you logged in with an external crypto wallet, it must be set to Ethereum Mainnet. If you saw a "Wrong network" message, see the article "I got a "Wrong network" error. What do I do?" (https://help.fabrica.land/en/articles/16280955-i-got-a-wrong-network-error-what-do-i-do) in this help center, switch networks, and retry.

passages.title: A transaction failed or seems stuck. What do I do?
passages.sectionTitle: Approval fails while making an offer
passages.text: Retry the "Allow the offer amount" step in the offer flow. This step lets the seller collect your USDC (a stablecoin, a digital dollar) only if they accept, and it is safe to run again after a failure.

passages.title: A transaction failed or seems stuck. What do I do?
passages.text:
Two messages come up during removal:

- "Connect the account that held this property's token. Only that account can authorize the deed transfer." You are signed in with a different account or address than the one that completed the removal step. Sign in with the right one and retry.

- "Authorization expired. Please sign again." The signature timed out. Sign again and the step continues.

passages.title: A transaction failed or seems stuck. What do I do?
passages.sectionTitle: A request is taking longer than expected
passages.text: If signing or confirming seems to hang, the app will now tell you it is "taking longer than expected" rather than spinning forever. Usually an earlier request is still open in your wallet. Dismiss that older request, then start the step again and approve it promptly when your wallet asks. If you logged in with your email or a social account, just try the step again; if it keeps happening, come back to this help center or message us.

passages.title: A transaction failed or seems stuck. What do I do?
passages.text:
Transactions can sit in a confirming state for a few minutes while the Ethereum network processes them. Give it a little time before retrying.

If something is still stuck after a retry, message us in the chat bubble in the corner and include a link to the property. We will take it from there.

passages.title: I got a "Wrong network" error. What do I do?
passages.sectionTitle: I got a "Wrong network" error. What do I do?
passages.text: If you see a message that starts with "Heads up:" and says your account is on a different network than the one Fabrica runs on, here is what is going on and how to fix it in about a minute. The full message reads something like "Heads up: your account is connected to Base, but we run on Ethereum Mainnet. Switch your account to Ethereum Mainnet, then try again. Visit help.fabrica.land if this keeps happening." It names the network your account is actually on when it can tell, and says "a different network" when it cannot.

passages.title: I got a "Wrong network" error. What do I do?
passages.text: Fabrica runs on Ethereum Mainnet, the main Ethereum network. If you logged in with an external crypto wallet, that wallet can be set to other networks too, and some wallets start on a different one by default. Coinbase Wallet, for example, often starts on Base, Coinbase's own network. Your account and Fabrica are simply not on the same network yet. Nothing is wrong with your account or your property.

passages.title: I got a "Wrong network" error. What do I do?
passages.text:
Many screens now show a button right in the dialog to fix this for you. If you see Switch and continue (or Try again), click it and approve the network switch when your wallet asks. That usually settles it. If your wallet cannot switch on its own, or you would rather do it by hand, switch the network in your wallet:

- Open your wallet app or browser extension.

- Find the network selector. In most wallets it is the network name shown near the top of the screen (it may say "Base" or something other than "Ethereum").

- Tap or click it and choose Ethereum (sometimes shown as "Ethereum Mainnet").

- Go back to Fabrica and retry what you were doing. The error should be gone.

The exact taps vary a little between wallets and versions:

- Coinbase Wallet (phone app or browser extension): tap the network name at the top, then pick Ethereum from the list.

- MetaMask: click the network menu at the top of the extension or app, then select Ethereum Mainnet.

If your wallet's screens look different, search its own help for "switch network".

passages.title: I got a "Wrong network" error. What do I do?
passages.text:
You should never be asked to switch networks. Signing in with your email or a social account creates a Fabrica account that is pinned to the right network for you, so there is nothing to switch. If you would rather not deal with networks at all, email login is the simplest path.

If something goes wrong on our side while preparing your account, you may see a different message: "Heads up: we couldn't get your account ready to continue. Please try again. Visit help.fabrica.land if this keeps happening." That one is not asking you to change any setting. Wait a moment and retry what you were doing. Inside a dialog, the same situation reads "Heads up: we couldn't get your account ready for this step." followed by "Please try again. If this keeps happening, chat with us below."

If you get stuck, message us in the chat bubble in the corner and we will walk you through it.

passages.title: Getting a notarized proof of ownership
passages.sectionTitle: Getting a notarized proof of ownership
passages.text: Sometimes a third party wants formal, notarized evidence of who owns your property: a title company, an assessor’s office, a lender, or a court. Fabrica can prepare that for you as a notarized Certification of Trust, a standard document that names you as the owner and trustee of your property’s trust.

passages.title: Getting a notarized proof of ownership
passages.text:
- A title company or escrow officer is reviewing your property

- A county office asks who is behind the trust on record

- A lender outside Fabrica wants ownership verified

- Any legal or administrative process that asks for “proof of ownership”

passages.title: Getting a notarized proof of ownership
passages.text:
- Ask us through the chat bubble on any page, and tell us which property it’s for.

- We prepare the certification and email you a link to sign it in a short online notary session. Have your photo ID ready; the session takes about 10 minutes.

- When the session is complete, the notarized document arrives by email, ready to hand to whoever asked for it.

Only the property’s majority owner can request and sign a proof of ownership.

If the person asking is a title professional or county office, you can also point them to the officials section of this help center, which explains the trust structure in their terms.

Learn more: The Fabrica Trust (https://docs.fabrica.land/docs/fabrica-trust)

passages.title: Do you allow fractional ownership?
passages.text:
The honest answer has three parts.

The smart contracts support it. Fabrica’s property token is built on a standard that natively supports splitting a token into multiple units, so fractional ownership is technically possible at the contract level.

The web application does not expose it. There is no button for it. Everything you can do on fabrica.land (buying, selling, borrowing) treats each property as a single whole token with a single owner.

The trust agreement contains only basic language for it. The legal framework for multiple beneficiaries is minimal. It has not been built out for groups of unrelated owners, and important questions (how decisions get made, how disputes get resolved) are not covered.

So: if you are technically capable and understand the tradeoffs, you can use fractional ownership at your own risk, and only for owning property together with friends or family.

Do not use it to offer investment interests in a property to others. Selling fractions of a property as an investment could fall under securities laws, which carry serious legal consequences. Fabrica’s token is designed as direct ownership of land, not as an investment product.

For most groups, a simpler route is setting up your own LLC or shared account that holds the whole token. See How to buy land onchain with your friends (blog) (https://blog.fabrica.land/how-to-buy-land-onchain-with-your-friends).

Questions? Message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

passages.title: Do Fabrica properties qualify for 1031 exchanges?
passages.sectionTitle: Do Fabrica properties qualify for 1031 exchanges?
passages.text:
Per our understanding, yes. A 1031 exchange (named after Section 1031 of the tax code) lets you defer capital gains tax when you sell one investment property and buy another like-kind property. Because a property on Fabrica is real property held in your own trust, and you are treated as the owner for tax purposes, properties held in a Fabrica trust can fully benefit from 1031 like-kind exchange treatment.

That said, 1031 exchanges come with strict rules: deadlines, the use of a qualified intermediary, and requirements about how the proceeds are handled. Fabrica cannot give tax advice, and how the rules apply depends on your situation. Before you sell with a 1031 exchange in mind, verify the details with your tax advisor.

If you have questions about how selling works on Fabrica, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.

passages.title: Can I use Fabrica from my AI assistant?
passages.sectionTitle: Can I use Fabrica from my AI assistant?
passages.text: Yes. If your AI assistant accepts outside data sources (Claude and Cursor do), you can connect it to Fabrica and ask about properties, loans and portfolios in plain English. Nothing to install: you paste one web address into the assistant's settings.

passages.title: Can I use Fabrica from my AI assistant?
passages.text:
Once connected, your assistant can look things up for you:

- Find properties. Search by state, acreage, Property checks results, whether a property is listed for sale, or whether it has a loan. Searches leave out properties that fabrica.land's marketplace would not show, the same bar the site applies; when you ask what one account owns, every property in that account is listed.

- Explain one property. Legal description, estimated value, Property checks and what they found, ownership history, loans, listing and offer activity, photos and documents.

- Show a map. Get the parcel boundary as a map image, or as boundary data for mapping tools.

- Check borrowing options. See how much a property could borrow from the DeFi lending pool and on what terms, plus any loan already on it.

- Review an account. What an account owns, its loans, open offers and repayment record, with a map of all its properties.

- Follow lending activity. See active, repaid and liquidated loans and the state of the DeFi lending pool.

- Read the history. Pull the activity feed for a property or an account: sales, transfers, loans, and when the property was added.

- Get the big picture. Platform-wide numbers, such as how many properties are on Fabrica and which states they are in.

passages.title: Can I use Fabrica from my AI assistant?
passages.text:
The assistant may show Property checks as a 5-digit code. That code is the numeric encoding of Property checks: it groups the results differently from the checklist on fabrica.land, and it is not a percentage or a grade. The connection itself no longer calls it a score or turns it into a percentage, though an assistant may still remember the older name "confidence score". Property checks are a starting point for your own research, not a title search or title insurance.

In assistants that can show interactive cards (Claude on the web and desktop, for example), property details appear as a card: the parcel map, the owner's photos, and key facts such as Property checks, estimated value, listing price and borrowing capacity. The card's buttons, such as "Make an offer", "Contact owner" and "View on Fabrica", open the property on fabrica.land. The card itself never buys, offers or signs anything.

passages.title: Can I use Fabrica from my AI assistant?
passages.text: The connection is read-only. Your assistant can look things up, but it cannot buy, sell, list, transfer, sign or borrow for you. Every action still happens on fabrica.land (https://fabrica.land), in your own account, with the same confirmations as always. The assistant never sees your login and does not need one: it reads the same public information you can see on fabrica.land.

passages.title: Can I use Fabrica from my AI assistant?
passages.text:
- Copy this address: https://mcp.fabrica.land/mcp

- In your assistant, open the settings for connectors or integrations and add a custom connector. In Claude, look for Connectors under Settings.

- Paste the address and save.

- Ask a question. For example: "Find land for sale in Nevada over 10 acres" or "How much could this property borrow?" with a link to the property page.

The address above connects to real properties. A second address, https://mcp-testnet.fabrica.land/mcp, connects to Fabrica's test environment, where the properties are practice data with no real-world meaning. Use it to try things out first, or add both as separate connections. The environment is fixed per address, so the test connection can never reach real properties.

passages.title: Can I use Fabrica from my AI assistant?
passages.text:
- Real land, real consequences. On the real-properties connection, the assistant is told up front that Fabrica properties are real parcels of US land, and that becoming an owner means taking on the trustee role, property taxes and the other responsibilities that come with land. Read a property's documents (the Documents menu on its page) before you act on anything.

- Not advice. What the assistant tells you is a summary of Fabrica's public data, not legal, tax or investment advice. Estimated values are a starting point, not an appraisal. Talk to a professional before you buy, sell or borrow.

- Same data, same limits. If something looks wrong on fabrica.land, it will look wrong to the assistant too. Message us and we will look into it.

For developers: the connector is Fabrica's MCP server (Model Context Protocol, the open standard assistants use to plug into data sources). Setup details, the full list of what it can look up, and how to run it on your own machine are in the public repository at github.com/fabrica-land/fabrica-mcp (https://github.com/fabrica-land/fabrica-mcp).

If you get stuck, message us through the chat bubble in the corner.
