passages.text:
Continuity of operation likewise does not excuse compliance with tax-law filing or reporting obligations triggered by death — including change-in-ownership reports and the timely claiming of any available exclusion — or with any other mandatory reporting obligation.

   3. **No present interest.** During the Beneficiary's life, no heir, devisee, prospective Key Successor, or other potential successor has any present right, title, or interest in the Trust, the Beneficial Interest, the Property Token, or the Property, other than the genuine, defeasible contingent equitable interest recognized under **Sections 2.26 and 12.5** and the narrow procedural standing described in **Sections 2.26 and 12.6**; and no right to notice of, and no standing to consent to or contest, any act of the Beneficiary, including any Transfer, encumbrance, designation, or dissolution. Nothing in this Section limits, clouds, or conditions the present Beneficiary's Owner Rights in any way; the Property Token remains the sole present instrument of ownership. No claim of any successor under this Section 7.6 may be asserted against a qualifying purchaser or protected secured party protected under **Section 11.4**.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text:
4. **Death during custody or designation.** If a Beneficiary dies while the Property Token is in Functional Contract custody — including while the Beneficiary is a Designated Owner under **Section 7.3(c)** whose collateral secures an outstanding obligation — this Section 7.6 operates on the Beneficiary's position and Owner Rights, not on the location of the Property Token: the successor determined under this Section succeeds to the deceased Beneficiary's position (including the position of borrower-of-record or owner of record on the Functional Contract's records, to the extent those records and applicable law permit), takes subject to the Functional Contract's terms and any security interest, and the Functional Contract's custody, enforcement, and disposition rights are unaffected by the death.

   5. **Taxes; fallback.** This Section 7.6 does not alter the tax treatment described in **Section 12.7**; during the Beneficiary's life no potential successor holds a taxable interest. **Section 10.3** remains available solely as the fallback procedure where no Key Successor exists — including where a Key Successor exists but, after notice, fails or refuses to exercise the Owner Rights for the account of the person entitled, which is treated as the absence of a Key Successor (**Section 10.3.1**).

7. **Acceptance and Disclaimer of Unsolicited Transfers.**

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: 1. **Presumptive defeasible vesting.** Consistent with **Sections 7.1 and 7.2**, beneficial ownership vests in the transferee upon a Transfer of the Property Token to the transferee's Account or Smart Wallet without any act of acceptance, and this Section adds no acceptance step to any Transfer. In the case of a Transfer that the transferee did not solicit, initiate, or agree to acquire (an "**unsolicited Transfer**"), the vesting is defeasible by disclaimer as provided in this Section. Holding the Property Token empowers the transferee immediately — all of the Owner Rights are exercisable from the moment of receipt — and imposes no obligation that survives a valid Onchain Disclaimer other than, where the disclaimer is made by recorded refusal, the limited custodial duties stated in **Section 7.7.2(c)**: pending acceptance or disclaimer, the presumptive transferee bears the incidents of ownership presumptively, as **Sections 6.1 and 12.7** provide, subject to retroactive divestment by a valid Onchain Disclaimer under clause 3. No incident of ownership becomes irrevocable except by the transferee's acceptance as provided in clause 4. The disclaimer right does not lapse by the passage of time, by silence, or by the transferee's ignorance of the Transfer; it ends only as provided in clause 4 or by operation of mandatory law. A transferee asserting an Onchain Disclaimer bears the burden of establishing that the Transfer was unsolicited; a Transfer shown by any signed record or onchain act to have been bargained for or agreed to is conclusively solicited.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text:
2. **Onchain Disclaimer.** A transferee of an unsolicited Transfer who has not accepted the Beneficial Interest under clause 4 may refuse the Beneficial Interest in whole (an "**Onchain Disclaimer**") by any of the following, each of which the parties designate as a signed record delivered to the Trustee and the transferor by its recording on the Blockchain Network, no offchain instrument, filing, or further delivery being required:

      - (a) **Return.** A Confirmed Transaction transferring the Property Token back to the Address from which it was received, or to another Account or Smart Wallet controlled by the transferor (where a transferor-controlled destination is identifiable, it is the preferred destination). This is the ordinary disclaimer. A good-faith return under this clause (a) is not an unauthorized Transfer by, and creates no liability of, the disclaimant to the true Beneficiary or any other person, even where the sending Address proves not to have been the true Beneficiary's — the remedies of **Section 7.5** run against the wrongdoer; and the disclaimant's selection among the receiving Address and other transferor-controlled destinations is a mode of return, not a direction of disposition within the meaning of clause 3.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: - (b) **Disclaimer Burn.** A Redeem of the Property Token executed before any acceptance under clause 4 and not in connection with any redemption demand, direction to the Trustee, or other exercise of Owner Rights (a "**Disclaimer Burn**"). A Disclaimer Burn is an irrevocable refusal of the whole Beneficial Interest; it is not an exercise of Owner Rights and is not a Dissolution Event or an instruction to convey under **Section 10.1**. Upon a Disclaimer Burn, the transferor (or the transferor's successor) is the continuing Beneficiary of a Trust whose Property Token has been destroyed, and may restore control of the Property and effect conveyance through **Section 10.2** (as modified by **Section 10.2.7**) or **Section 10.4**. Whether a Redeem was executed in connection with a redemption demand, direction, or other exercise of Owner Rights is determined by the signed records satisfying **Section 4.1**: production of a signed demand or direction made at or before the Redeem conclusively establishes the Redeem as an exercise of Owner Rights under **Sections 7.7.4 and 10.1**, and not a Disclaimer Burn.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text:
- (c) **Recorded refusal (fallback).** Only where both return and Redemption are impossible, are prohibited by applicable law, or are not reasonably available to the transferee, a Confirmed Transaction originated by the transferee's Account or Smart Wallet that records, in a form retrievable from the Blockchain Network and logically associated with the Property Token, the transferee's unequivocal refusal of the whole Beneficial Interest. A disclaimant proceeding under this clause (c) who continues to hold the Property Token holds it thereafter as a mere custodian for the rightful Beneficiary, without Owner Rights and without duties other than to refrain from dealing with the Property Token and to permit and reasonably cooperate with its retrieval; any later purported exercise or Transfer by the disclaimant is unauthorized and governed by **Sections 7.5 and 11.4**.

      An Onchain Disclaimer must refuse the entire Beneficial Interest received in the disclaimed Transfer; no partial disclaimer is permitted. Nothing in this Section precludes a disclaimant from also making a disclaimer satisfying the form, content, filing, or delivery requirements of an applicable statutory disclaimer regime; the parties intend an Onchain Disclaimer to operate as such a disclaimer to the maximum extent applicable law permits.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: 3. **Relation back.** An Onchain Disclaimer is effective retroactively to the moment of the disclaimed Transfer, under this Agreement and to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law: the Beneficial Interest is treated as never having vested in the disclaimant; the disclaimant is treated as never having been a Beneficiary or Trustee; and the incidents of ownership arising under this Agreement — including the responsibilities and entitlements of **Section 6.1** and the tax attribution of **Section 12.7** — are attributed as if the disclaimed Transfer had not occurred, so that the transferor (or, if the transferor has died, the transferor's successors under **Section 7.6**) remained the Beneficiary throughout. The transferor's succession arrangements under **Section 7.6** are unaffected by the disclaimed Transfer. An Onchain Disclaimer is a refusal to accept; it is not a transfer, assignment, or release of the Beneficial Interest by the disclaimant, and the disclaimant may not direct its destination. Relation back does not discharge the limited custodial duties stated in **Section 7.7.2(c)**: a disclaimant by recorded refusal who continues to hold the Property Token remains bound, for as long as that holding continues, to refrain from dealing with the Property Token and to permit and reasonably cooperate with its retrieval, notwithstanding that the disclaimant is treated as never having been a Beneficiary or Trustee; those duties are the only obligations under this Agreement that survive a valid Onchain Disclaimer.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: This relation back binds every person bound by this Agreement; as against persons not so bound it operates to the extent applicable law gives it effect, and it is in every case subject to mandatory law — including federal and state tax and tax-collection law, any statutory disclaimer regime of applicable law that conditions a disclaimer's effect on its being made within a reasonable or prescribed time (in California, Cal. Prob. Code § 279), sanctions law, judicial sales, insolvency and creditor law, and the finality of instruments recorded in the real property records — and to **Sections 4.3 and 11.4**. Relation back does not extend or revive any statutory refund, appeal, or limitation period.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: 4. **Acceptance; conclusive and retroactive to receipt.** The disclaimer right terminates upon the transferee's acceptance of the Beneficial Interest, which occurs upon the earlier of: (a) any voluntary exercise of Owner Rights by the transferee — including any Confirmed Transaction originated by the transferee's Account or Smart Wallet that transfers, lists, encumbers, lends against, fractionalizes, or otherwise deals with the Property Token; any direction to the Trustee; any redemption demand, including a Redeem executed in connection with a demand or direction that the Trustee convey the Property, which is acceptance and preserves in full the transferee's right to conveyance under **Section 10.1**; and any other exercise of rights under this Agreement — other than an act described in clause 2, an act reasonably necessary to preserve the Property Token or the Property pending refusal, or a listing or offer that is cancelled or expires without resulting in any Transfer or other consummated dealing, which is not acceptance, the disclaimer right subsisting notwithstanding it (a listing that results in a Transfer is acceptance, and **Section 4.3.2** protects any person who in good faith and for value relied on the listing); or (b) the transferee's express acceptance by Confirmed Transaction or other signed record satisfying **Section 4.1**. Acceptance is conclusive and confirms the vesting described in clause 1 retroactively to the moment of the Transfer: the transferee is, and is treated as having been from receipt, the Beneficiary for all purposes of this Agreement.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text:
An acceptance evidenced by a Confirmed Transaction is conclusive as to all persons. Conduct occurring offchain — including taking possession or use of the Property or receiving or directing its income — is likewise acceptance, but as against a person acting in good faith on the record of the Blockchain Network, **Section 4.3** governs, and acceptance and disclaimer status may be determined by such a person from the record of the Blockchain Network alone. A Transfer that the transferee solicited, initiated, or agreed to acquire — including every purchase, exchange, settlement, Qualified Designation under **Section 7.3(c)**, and other bargained-for acquisition — is accepted upon the Transfer itself, and no disclaimer right exists with respect to it.

   5. **Coordination; limits.** The following limits and coordinating rules apply:

      - (a) **Trustee office.** No person becomes Trustee by reason of an unsolicited Transfer before acceptance (**Section 7.1**); the prior Trustee's continuation in office is limited to ministerial preservation.

      - (b) **No assumption of personal obligations.** No Transfer, of itself, imposes on any transferee personal liability on any contract, covenant, or debt of the transferor or of any prior holder; obligations that attach to ownership or possession of the Property under applicable law are governed by that law and by the presumptive attribution of **Sections 6.1 and 12.7**, subject to retroactive divestment by a valid Onchain Disclaimer (**Section 7.7.3**) and confirmed by acceptance (**Section 7.7.4**).

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text:
- (c) **Sanctions.** The vesting, disclaimer, and relation-back rules of this Section operate subject to applicable sanctions and similar mandatory law; where such law applies, a Transfer to, or a dealing by or on behalf of, a sanctioned or blocked person may be ineffective, blocked, or subject to licensing requirements notwithstanding any provision of this Section.

      - (d) **Operative Instruments; tax sale.** If an Operative Instrument is recorded under **Section 10.5** while a disclaimer right subsists, Section 10.5 applies according to its terms, the person entitled being determined after giving effect to any valid Onchain Disclaimer as **Section 10.5.2** provides. A tax sale or other involuntary transfer that terminates the Trust under Section 10.5 is the terminal resolution of an unsolicited Transfer that was never discovered or disclaimed; nothing in this Section prevents or delays that operation of law.

      - (e) **Protected parties; theft.** An Onchain Disclaimer does not limit the rights of a qualifying purchaser or protected secured party under **Section 11.4** or of a person protected under **Section 4.3**, and does not affect **Section 7.5** (a Transfer resulting from unauthorized access or use is governed by Section 7.5 whether or not disclaimed).

passages.text: - (f) **Death of the transferor or transferee.** If a transferor to whom a disclaimed interest reverts has died, **Sections 7.6 and 10.3** apply to the transferor's position as they would for any Beneficiary, and the death of a transferor or of a presumptive transferee before a disclaimer is not, by itself, an acceptance and does not terminate the disclaimer right; a disclaimer made on a deceased or incapacitated transferee's behalf by the transferee's legal successor or personal representative, to the extent applicable law permits, is not an exercise of Owner Rights.

   1. first, the Beneficiary will burn the Property Token by executing the `burn` or `burnBatch` functions on the Token Contract;

   3. the Trustee will transfer the Property out of the Trust.

   A Redeem executed by the then-present Beneficiary otherwise than as a Disclaimer Burn does not change that Beneficiary's position: the Beneficiary remains the Beneficiary notwithstanding the destruction of the Property Token (Section 2.3 notwithstanding), and remains entitled to direct conveyance under this Section 10.1 at any time.

Within ten (10) calendar days of recording, the Beneficiary shall deliver a copy of the recorded Notice by certified mail, return receipt requested, to: (a) the Property address as shown in the records of the county assessor or tax collector and, if different, the assessee or taxpayer mailing address shown on the county tax roll; where those records show no situs address for the Property (as is common for unimproved land), delivery to the assessee or taxpayer mailing address of record satisfies this clause (a); (b) each person who appears in the official records of the county recorder as the holder of a recorded lien, deed of trust, mortgage, or other encumbrance against the Property, at the address shown in the recorded instrument or, if more current contact information is reasonably available to the Beneficiary, at such current address; and (c) each secured party of record under any financing statement filed against the Beneficiary as debtor and covering the Property Token or the Beneficial Interest, as disclosed by a search of the applicable UCC filing office of the Beneficiary's location, at the address shown in the financing statement.

The Property Token constitutes a "controllable electronic record" as defined under Article 12 of the Uniform Commercial Code as adopted in California and, to the extent adopted, any other applicable jurisdiction ("**UCC Article 12**"), for so long as it is capable of being subjected to control under UCC Article 12 (as it is intended and expected to be at all times, subject only to the fractionalized configuration described in **Section 6.3**): the classification is statutory, and no custody, holding, or other arrangement concerning the Property Token — including the arrangements described in **Sections 11.2 and 11.3** — varies it. A person has "control" of the Property Token when the requirements of UCC Article 12 are satisfied, which the parties intend may be achieved through blockchain-native mechanisms such as cryptographic keys and smart contract systems. The parties intend that control under UCC § 12-105 may be established, and the person having it readily identified, by pseudonymous, blockchain-native means, including by cryptographic key or account identification. For purposes of UCC § 12-107(c)(1) (Cal. Com. Code § 12107(c)(1)), this Agreement — a record logically associated with the Property Token and readily available for review through the Token Metadata — expressly provides that the State of California is the Property Token's jurisdiction for purposes of UCC Article 12 and the Uniform Commercial Code.

When the Property Token is deposited into a smart contract for collateralization, lending, escrow, pooling, or similar arrangements, such smart contract may serve as a method of obtaining and evidencing "control" for purposes of UCC Article 12; programmed restrictions or automated processes within such smart contract do not, by themselves, defeat control. The standards and procedures for enforcement and disposition specified in the smart contract are agreed standards for purposes of UCC § 9-603 — intended not to be manifestly unreasonable — to the extent the debtor's authenticated security agreement or assent record (including a record described in **Section 7.3(c)(2)(B)**) identifies, references, or objectively incorporates them; and nothing in this sentence varies any rule of Part 6 of UCC Article 9 that is nonwaivable in a consumer transaction. Nothing in this Agreement waives any rights or duties that cannot be waived under UCC § 9-602, nor does it constitute post-default consent to acceptance of collateral in satisfaction of an obligation under UCC § 9-620. The collateral in any financing secured by a deposit or pledge of the Property Token is the Property Token (a controllable electronic record) and/or, to the extent expressly granted, the Beneficial Interest (personal property under **Section 1.4**); the parties intend, and shall structure every such financing so, that no mortgage, deed of trust, lien, or other security interest in the Property itself is created;

passages.text: 3. **Custodial Holding.** Notwithstanding **Sections 1.3, 2.3, 7.1, and 7.3(a)**, where a person holds the Property Token as custodian for another person — directly, or indirectly through one or more further custodians — under an agreement with that person, the custodian does not acquire the Beneficial Interest by reason of that holding; the Beneficial Interest vests in the person for whom the Property Token is ultimately held, as the custody arrangement and the custodian's records identify that person. A holding resulting from a Transfer described in **Section 7.5.1** confers no beneficial ownership on the custodian or on any person claiming through it. A transfer of a person's rights against the custodian, made as the custody arrangement provides, operates as a transfer of the Beneficial Interest under **Section 7**: the custody agreement together with the record of that transfer constitutes the explicit assignment of Owner Rights described in **Section 7.3(b)(ii)**, and is subject to **Sections 7.5 and 11.4** to the same extent as a Transfer of the Property Token itself. Where the Property Token is held for more than one person, their respective interests and the manner in which Owner Rights are exercised among them are those the custody arrangement and the custodian's records provide. Nothing in this Section determines the rights and duties as between a custodian and the person for whom it holds, or whether any person has control of the Property Token under applicable law; those matters are governed by the custody arrangement and by law other than this Agreement.

passages.text:
4. **Qualifying Purchasers; Protected Secured Parties; Deliberate Loss Allocation.** Transfers of the Property Token are intended to enable transferees who obtain control for value, in good faith, and without notice of an Adverse Claim (**Section 11.4.6**) to qualify as "qualifying purchasers" under UCC Article 12 and thereby take free of adverse claims to the extent provided by applicable law. The mechanism is layered, and the parties adopt each layer expressly:

   1. **The Property Token.** A qualifying purchaser acquires its rights in the Property Token free of a claim of a property right in the Property Token, as UCC § 12-104(e) provides. UCC Article 12 governs the Property Token as a controllable electronic record; the parties do not assert that it embodies, or of its own force transfers, the Beneficial Interest (**Section 11.7**).

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: 2. **Power to transfer the Beneficial Interest.** The Grantor declares as a term of this Trust, and every Beneficial Interest Holder — as an express condition of acquiring any interest under or through this Agreement or the Property Token — irrevocably agrees, that a person having control of the Property Token (within the meaning of UCC § 12-105), whether or not that person had authority as against the prior Beneficiary, has the power to transfer the Beneficial Interest to a qualifying purchaser meeting all of the requirements of this Section 11.4. A qualifying purchaser's acquisition of control therefore carries the Beneficial Interest by the assignment mechanics of this Agreement (**Sections 1.4 and 7**): this power, and the defeasance stated in **Section 11.4.3**, are terms of the trust under which the Beneficial Interest is created and held — law other than UCC Article 12 within the meaning of UCC § 12-104(f) — operating alongside the purchaser's rights in the Property Token itself under UCC § 12-104(d) and (e). This power exists only in favor of a purchaser who establishes control, the giving of value, good faith, and the absence of notice of an Adverse Claim, in each case determined as of the time the purchaser obtains control (**Section 11.4.6**); it does not validate the wrongdoer's ownership, excuse the wrongdoer, or limit **Section 7.5** as to any transferee who does not satisfy those conditions.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text:
3. **Defeasance of the prior claim.** Independently and cumulatively, every Beneficial Interest Holder takes its interest under this Agreement subject, from its creation, to defeasance in favor of a qualifying purchaser or protected secured party: as against such a person, the claim of any prior holder to the Beneficial Interest is extinguished and converts to a claim in personam against the person who effected the unauthorized Transfer. In addition, every Beneficial Interest Holder agrees, as a term of the interest it acquires, that any security interest or other lien it grants or suffers in any interest it holds under this Agreement is subordinate to the interest of a qualifying purchaser or protected secured party of the Property Token, and every person claiming through such a holder — including its secured parties and transferees — takes subject to this subordination.

   4. **Protected secured parties.** A party who obtains a security interest in the Property Token for value, in good faith, without notice of an Adverse Claim (**Section 11.4.6**), and who obtains control of the Property Token as required by applicable law (a "**protected secured party**") shall receive the same protection under this Agreement as a qualifying purchaser to the extent permitted by applicable law. A secured party who has not obtained control receives no protection under this Section 11.4 beyond what applicable law and its own agreements provide.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: 5. **Allocation.** Where a qualifying purchaser or protected secured party prevails, the prior Beneficiary's remedy is against the party who effected the unauthorized Transfer, not against the qualifying purchaser or protected secured party. This allocation is deliberate: it preserves the prior holder's ownership against thieves, donees, and transferees with notice (**Section 7.5.1**), while giving good-faith purchasers for value the finality that makes the Property Token reliable in commerce; as between the two innocent parties, the loss falls on the holder responsible for the security of the compromised credentials (**Section 7.5.2**), whose recourse is against the wrongdoer. Third-party finality under this Section rests on applicable law and on the property and trust rules stated here, not on **Section 4.1** alone; whether a purchaser or secured party met these conditions remains subject to adjudication under **Sections 7.5.4 and 12.4**.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text:
6. **Notice standard.** For every purpose of this Section 11.4 (and of **Section 7.5.3**), the notice that disqualifies a purchaser or secured party is notice of a claim of a property right in the Property Token or in the Beneficial Interest inconsistent with the transferor's power to transfer (an "**Adverse Claim**," adapting UCC § 12-102(a)(2)), determined as of the time the purchaser or secured party obtains control. Knowledge or constructive notice of an interest in the Property appearing in the real property records — including any recorded mortgage, lien, lis pendens, or tax lien — is not notice of an Adverse Claim; such interests bind the Trust's title under **Section 11.8** and are not claims to the Property Token or the Beneficial Interest. Nor is the filing of a financing statement notice of an Adverse Claim (UCC § 12-104(h)).

5. For the avoidance of doubt, the UCC characterizations in this Section 11 have no bearing on whether the Property Token is a security as used in any other context or regulation, nor do they constitute an admission that the Property Token is a security for any purposes other than the Uniform Commercial Code. It is the intent of the parties that the Property Token shall not be a security for purposes of US federal securities law (including the Securities Act of 1933 and Securities Exchange Act of 1934), California securities laws, or any other applicable state, local, or foreign securities laws.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: 6. **Real-Property Law Preservation.** Nothing in this Section 11 displaces, modifies, or supersedes the real-property recording statutes, deed requirements, title-vesting rules, or real-property perfection and priority rules of the jurisdiction where the Property is located. "Control" of the Property Token within the meaning of UCC Article 12 determines rights in the Property Token as a controllable electronic record, but does not by itself transfer, encumber, or create any interest in record title to the Property. Transfer of record title to the Property requires a deed or other instrument that satisfies the recording and conveyancing requirements of applicable real-property law, executed and delivered in accordance with this Agreement.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: 7. **UCC Characterization of the Beneficial Interest.** The Property Token is the controllable electronic record; the Beneficial Interest is not itself a controllable electronic record, a controllable account, or a controllable payment intangible, and the parties do not assert that UCC Article 12, of its own force, transfers the Beneficial Interest. The Beneficial Interest is personal property (**Section 1.4**) and a "general intangible" as defined in UCC § 9-102(a)(42), of which the Property Token is the authoritative record; the Beneficial Interest is transferred only through the Property Token or through the ownership events expressly defined in this Agreement (**Sections 7.3(b)(ii), 7.3(c), 7.6, 7.7, and 10.3**, including a transfer, during custodial holding, of a person's rights against the custodian under **Section 11.3**, which constitutes the assignment described in Section 7.3(b)(ii)). A security interest in the Property Token or in the Beneficial Interest attaches under UCC § 9-203 to the extent expressly granted by the debtor (**Section 11.2**), and is perfected, has priority, and is enforced under UCC Article 9; a secured party may obtain and evidence control of the Property Token as described in **Sections 11.1 and 11.2**, and may perfect by any method applicable law permits. The assignment of the Beneficial Interest is effected by the mechanics of **Section 7** of this Agreement, as a matter of trust law and party agreement; UCC Article 12 governs rights in the Property Token as a record, including the protections described in **Section 11.4**.

passages.text:
8. **Priority Framework: the Land Lane and the Token Lane.** Interests in the Property, on the one hand, and interests in the Property Token and the Beneficial Interest, on the other, arise and travel in two distinct legal lanes. This Section states the framework — which restates, builds on, and in no event weakens **Section 11.6** — by which this Agreement allocates every interaction between them:

   1. **The land lane.** As to record title to, and interests in, the Property itself, the real-property law of the jurisdiction where the Property is located — including its recording acts, lien-priority rules, tax-lien and tax-sale law, foreclosure procedures, and homestead laws — governs, always. An interest in the Property valid under that law binds the Trust's title according to that law, regardless of any token-side transaction; and no Transfer of the Property Token, no control of it within the meaning of UCC Article 12, and no provision of this Agreement defeats, subordinates, or displaces any such interest.

   2. **The token lane.** As to ownership, assignment, encumbrance, and priority in the Property Token and the Beneficial Interest, this Agreement, applicable trust law, and — to the extent applicable — UCC Articles 9 and 12 govern. The Beneficiary's interest is at all times an interest in the Trust (**Section 1.4**): the token lane controls everything the Trust has; the land lane determines what the Trust has.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: 3. **The crossing gate.** The event that carries a land-lane outcome into the token lane is a recorded instrument. When an instrument effecting a transfer of the Trust's title by operation of law or legal process is recorded, **Section 10.5** converts the token-side position accordingly: the Trust dissolves as to the Property, the Property Token becomes a Void Token, and the token-side claim converts to the wind-up authority and proceeds entitlement of **Section 10.5.2** and the reinstatement eligibility of **Section 10.5.4**. Where the recorded conveyance deed recites the Token Contract address and Token ID as **Section 3.1.2** requires, that deed gives such notice of the Trust and of the token-property relationship as the recording acts of the jurisdiction give to its recitals; no additional recording is required for the Trust's title to be of record.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: 4. **Applications.** Without limiting the foregoing: (a) a lien or encumbrance validly recorded against the Property has priority, as to the Property, over any later token-side pledge or Transfer; the later pledgee or transferee acquires the Beneficial Interest, or a security interest in the Property Token or Beneficial Interest, in a Trust whose title is so encumbered, and if the recorded lien is foreclosed and the resulting instrument recorded, the token side holds the **Section 10.5.2** rights in any surplus; (b) a purchaser of the Property Token acquires the Beneficial Interest in a Trust whose title is exactly what the land records and applicable real-property law make it — the protections of **Section 11.4** run against competing claims to the Property Token and the Beneficial Interest, never against interests in the Property; and (c) whether an unrecorded land-side claim binds the Trust's title is determined by the recording acts and other applicable real-property law, which this Agreement neither strengthens nor weakens.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text:
5. **Court residual.** Judicial resolution under **Sections 10.4 and 12.4** remains available for the cases this framework does not answer mechanically, including: competing claims to beneficial ownership of the Property Token itself (**Section 7.5.4**); contests recorded during a Quiet Period (**Section 10.2.2**); challenges to the validity of an Operative Instrument (**Section 10.5.3**); disputes concerning assent to a designation (**Section 7.3(c)**), solicitation or disclaimer of a Transfer (**Section 7.7**), or death and successor identity (**Sections 7.6 and 10.3**); and the status of the Property Token under **Section 11.1**.

9. **Governing Law of the Property Token; Fallback Without Article 12.**

   1. Matters governed by UCC Article 12 are governed by the local law of the Property Token's jurisdiction, which **Section 11.1** expressly designates as the State of California pursuant to UCC § 12-107(c)(1); under UCC § 12-107(e), that law applies even if a matter or transaction bears no relation to California. The location of the Property therefore does not determine the law governing the Property Token: matters of real-property law are governed by the mandatory law of the situs (**Sections 11.6 and 12.3**); matters concerning the Property Token as a record are not.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text:
2. If, notwithstanding the foregoing, no enactment of UCC Article 12 applies to a matter concerning the Property Token, the Property Token remains fully operative. The assignment mechanics of this Agreement and applicable trust law (**Sections 1.4 and 7**) do not depend on UCC Article 12: they continue to vest the Beneficial Interest in the person determined under **Section 7** upon each valid transfer of beneficial ownership, binding every person who claims under or through this Agreement or the Property Token. In that case only the third-party negotiability layer varies: the take-free protections described in **Section 11.4** are available to the extent applicable law provides, and the allocation rules of **Sections 7.5 and 11.4** continue to bind all persons bound by this Agreement as a matter of contract and trust law.

   3. Custodial holding as described in **Section 11.3** remains available but is never required; nothing in this Section requires the use of a custodian or any other third-party arrangement for the Property Token to carry the Beneficial Interest.

1. If any part of any provision of this Agreement or any other agreement, document, or writing given pursuant to or in connection with this Agreement shall be invalid or unenforceable under applicable law, said part shall be ineffective to the extent of such invalidity only, without in any way affecting the remaining part of said provision or the remaining provisions of this Agreement.

2. The headings of the sections and subsections of this Agreement are inserted for convenience of reference only and do not form a part or affect the meaning hereof. Wherever used herein, a pronoun in any gender shall be considered as including any other gender pronoun. References to the singular include the plural, and vice versa.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: 3. To the extent it is not contrary to a strong public policy of the jurisdiction, if any, having a more significant relationship to this Agreement, this Agreement, the rights and obligations of the parties hereto, and any claims and disputes relating thereto, shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of California (not including the choice of law rules thereof). Notwithstanding the foregoing, matters relating to the conveyancing, recording, and transfer of record title to the Property, the validity and priority of liens and encumbrances on the Property, and probate or succession proceedings affecting the Property, shall be governed by the mandatory laws of the jurisdiction where the Property is located to the extent such laws cannot be varied by agreement. Matters governed by UCC Article 12 are additionally subject to the express Property Token jurisdiction designation in **Section 11.1** and the governing-law rule of UCC § 12-107. The parties intend and agree, as a term of the Trust, that the Trust's internal affairs are administered by reference to the laws of the State of California as its designated governing law and agreed place of administration for internal-affairs purposes, wherever the Trustee or the Beneficiary may from time to time be located. The Beneficial Interest and the Owner Rights are subject to applicable insolvency and creditor law, including the estate-property, automatic-stay, and avoidance provisions of the United States Bankruptcy Code, which this Agreement does not and cannot vary.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: 4. The parties to this Agreement hereby consent to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of any State or Federal Court of competent jurisdiction located within the State of California, in the County of San Francisco, in connection with any actions or proceedings arising directly or indirectly from this Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, actions to quiet title, foreclose liens, or otherwise adjudicate interests in the Property may be brought in any court of competent jurisdiction where the Property is located, and this Agreement does not waive or limit such jurisdiction.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: 5. **No Merger of Interests.** The Trust created by this Agreement shall not fail or terminate by reason of the merger of legal and equitable interests. The parties acknowledge that, because the Property Token is transferable and beneficial ownership passes with valid Transfers under **Section 7**, the equitable interests in the Trust are at all times held by the class of Beneficial Interest Holders (including determinable future Beneficiaries and legal successors under **Sections 7.6 and 10.3**), and are not held solely by the present Beneficiary even when the present Beneficiary also serves as Trustee. Without limiting the foregoing: the contingent equitable interests of the Beneficial Interest Holders described in **Section 2.26** — including those of the successors who would take under **Sections 7.6 and 10.3** — arise simultaneously with the creation of the Trust and are determined by the objective mechanics of this Agreement, so that at no instant — including the instant of formation, where the Grantor is the initial sole Beneficiary and deemed Trustee — are legal title to the trust property and all equitable interests in the Trust united in a single person within the meaning of Texas Property Code § 112.034(a) or (b) or any similar merger statute or doctrine.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: If any court of competent jurisdiction determines that any provision of this Agreement would otherwise cause a merger of legal and equitable title, such provision shall be automatically construed and, if necessary, reformed to the minimum extent required to preserve the separation of legal and equitable interests and the continuity of the Trust, consistent with the Trust Purpose stated in **Section 1**. Any construction or reformation under this Section, and any suspension under **Section 12.6**, takes effect as of the moment immediately before the event that would otherwise cause the merger. **Perpetuities savings.** Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, every interest created under this Agreement shall vest, if at all, within the period permitted by the rule against perpetuities, or any analogous statutory rule (including Texas Property Code § 112.036 where it applies), of each jurisdiction whose law governs the validity of that interest — and, where more than one such rule governs an interest, within the shortest period that governs it. Where a governing rule measures the permitted period by lives in being, the measuring lives are the Grantor (if a natural person), each natural person who is the Beneficiary on the Creation Date, and the descendants of each of them living on the Creation Date; the permitted period under such a rule is twenty-one (21) years after the death of the last survivor of those measuring lives, or any longer period that a statutory rule of the governing jurisdiction allows.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: Any interest that has not vested by the end of the period governing it terminates at that time. The Trust shall itself terminate no later than the earliest date on which any rule governing the validity of the Trust or of any interest under it requires its termination (the "**Perpetuities Termination Date**"), if it has not terminated earlier under **Section 10**. Termination under this Section is an Alternative Dissolution Event (**Section 2.22**): on the Perpetuities Termination Date, this Section substitutes, automatically and without any act of any person, for the Redeem described in **Section 1.2(a)** and for the signature described in **Section 10.1.2**, and the Trustee shall execute, deliver, and record a deed conveying the Property to the then-present Beneficiary — who is the mandatory grantee, determined under **Section 7** as of that date — in the manner provided in **Section 10.1**, with **Section 10.6** applying upon its recording. This savings provision shall be construed to sustain, never to defeat, the interests and the continuity of the Trust created by this Agreement.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: 6. **Springing Trustee for Continuity.** If, notwithstanding **Section 12.5**, a court of competent jurisdiction determines that a merger of legal and equitable interests has occurred or is imminent, the Trust shall not terminate. Instead, the present Beneficiary's role as Trustee shall immediately and automatically be suspended, such suspension taking effect as provided in **Section 12.5**. Pending qualification of the Continuity Trustee described below, the suspended Trustee shall retain only ministerial authority to preserve the trust res and prevent waste; the suspended Trustee shall have no authority to make distributions, encumber the Property, or take any action beyond those strictly necessary to maintain the status quo. A temporary special trustee (the "**Continuity Trustee**") shall then serve solely to preserve the trust res and complete any recordable acts necessary to maintain the property-token relationship. The Continuity Trustee shall be selected by the Beneficiary and may accept the office through a signed electronic record satisfying **Section 4.1**; if the Beneficiary fails to designate a Continuity Trustee within thirty (30) calendar days of the court's determination, any Beneficial Interest Holder may petition the court described in **Section 12.4** to appoint one. A vacancy in the office of Continuity Trustee pending appointment does not terminate the Trust.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: The Continuity Trustee holds the office subject to the affirmative duties of **Sections 8.1.2 and 8.1.4**, and shall have no discretion over distributions, no authority to direct or encumber the Property, and no powers beyond those duties and the acts strictly necessary to maintain the Trust's existence and execute documents at the Beneficiary's direction. The Continuity Trustee's appointment terminates automatically upon the earliest of: (a) a valid Transfer of the Property Token to a new Beneficiary, (b) the Beneficiary's appointment of a different Trustee through a signed electronic record satisfying **Section 4.1** or another instrument permitted by applicable law, or (c) dissolution of the Trust under **Section 10**. Nothing in this Section creates a standing professional trustee requirement, imposes ongoing fees, or grants any platform, company, or third party approval rights over Trust operations.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: 7. **Tax Treatment.** As among the parties, and to the maximum extent permitted by applicable tax law, the present Beneficiary shall at all times be treated as the owner of the Property for all federal, state, and local tax purposes. Without limiting the foregoing, the parties intend: that the Beneficiary's power to Redeem the Property Token and to receive conveyance of the Property under **Section 10.1** — exercisable solely by the Beneficiary, the Trustee's duty to convey upon its exercise being mandatory and ministerial — is a power described in section 678(a)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code, so that the present Beneficiary is treated as the owner of the entire Trust for federal income tax purposes; and that each person who acquires the Beneficial Interest for value is, in addition and independently, treated as a grantor and owner of the Trust to the extent of the interest acquired, within the meaning of Treasury Regulation § 1.671-2(e)(3). Where applicable tax law limits the treatment of any person as owner by reason of that person's status — including the limits of section 672(f) of the Internal Revenue Code on treating a foreign person as owner — the Trust may be a separate taxpayer with return, identification-number, and withholding obligations of its own, and nothing in this Agreement excuses or shifts them. The attribution of this Section allocates tax incidence under this Agreement;

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: it does not, and cannot, displace the mandatory assessment, collection, classification, or lien rules of any taxing authority, and property-tax assessment, liability, and liens attach to the Property under the law of the jurisdiction where it is located. During the period in which a transferee may disclaim under **Section 7.7**, the presumptive transferee is the present Beneficiary and tax owner unless and until a valid Onchain Disclaimer occurs; upon a valid Onchain Disclaimer, the relation-back rule of **Section 7.7.3** governs attribution under this Agreement to the maximum extent permitted by applicable tax law, so that the transferor (or the transferor's successor) is treated as the tax owner throughout and the disclaiming transferee is treated as never having been the tax owner. Ownership changes effected under this Agreement without a recorded deed — including a Qualified Designation (**Section 7.3(c)**), an acceptance or disclaimer under **Section 7.7**, and a succession under **Section 7.6** — may constitute reportable changes in ownership under applicable tax law; nothing in this Agreement excuses any resulting filing or report, responsibility for which follows the tax-owner attribution of this Section as among the parties. The existence of contingent interests held by future Beneficial Interest Holders under **Section 2.26** does not create a separate taxable interest, does not entitle any future Beneficial Interest Holder to current income or deductions, and does not alter the pass-through treatment of the Trust.

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text: 8. **Digital Execution and Acceptance.** The Grantor executes and adopts this Agreement by creating the Trust and causing this Agreement to be attached to, and logically associated with, the Property Token as described in **Section 3.1**; the Confirmed Transactions described in Section 3.1 together constitute the Grantor's execution and delivery of this Agreement as of the Creation Date. Each Beneficiary, Trustee, and Beneficial Interest Holder accepts and becomes bound by this Agreement by acquiring or accepting the applicable interest or office through the objective mechanics of this Agreement, including a Mint, a Transfer, a Qualified Designation under **Section 7.3(c)**, an acquisition of the Beneficial Interest through custodial holding under **Section 11.3**, a succession event under **Sections 7.6 and 10.3**, a Trustee appointment or deemed appointment under **Section 7.1**, or another electronic act recognized by this Agreement. A transferee controlling an Account or Smart Wallet is bound upon the Transfer, with acceptance of an unsolicited Transfer governed by **Section 7.7**; a person merely designated while a Functional Contract has custody becomes Beneficiary only upon Qualifying Assent Evidence under **Section 7.3(c)**; a person for whom the Property Token is held under **Section 11.3** is bound upon acquiring the Beneficial Interest under that Section; a successor under **Section 7.6** takes subject to, and bound by, this Agreement upon the transfer at death (a Key Successor who is not the person entitled being bound in their representative capacity only).

passages.title: Fabrica Trust Agreement (US)
passages.text:
Execution, acceptance, and any counterpart of this Agreement may be evidenced entirely by electronic records and signatures as described in **Section 4.1**. No paper counterpart, separate signature page, or wet signature is required for this Agreement to bind a person whose acceptance is established under these terms, except to the extent a nonwaivable law expressly requires otherwise.

**END OF AGREEMENT**
